job.title: Staff Software Engineer
job.description:
1 big thing: Axios is a growth-focused media company helping people get smarter, faster, on what matters. We’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer—a senior, hands-on individual contributor—to lead architecture and delivery for Axios’ core products across multiple teams using strong product-engineering and AI-native practices.

Why it matters: Axios delivers clear, trustworthy news to millions of readers. You’ll be anchored to a product area while shaping full-stack systems and technical direction across multiple teams and connected systems. This is not a people-management role.

AI is core to how we build. You’ll use coding agents throughout implementation, testing, review, debugging, documentation, and operations while remaining accountable for architecture, quality, security, and product outcomes. Staff impact comes from sustained scope, judgment, and results—not tool use alone.

You’ll work with product managers, designers, engineers, and leaders to shape plans, align dependencies, resolve ambiguity, build resilient systems, and help others make better technical decisions.

Responsibilities:

As a Staff Software Engineer, you’ll lead reliable product and platform work across Axios’ frontend and backend systems. You’ll remain hands-on while driving multi-quarter initiatives, improving technical coherence, and using agentic practices to accelerate delivery. Key responsibilities include:

  • Cross-team technical leadership: Lead mission-critical or high-risk initiatives spanning teams and connected systems. Frame problems, align ownership and dependencies, make tradeoffs explicit, and drive production adoption.
  • Architecture and design: Own architecture for a product area and scalable boundaries across frontend, APIs, data, and production systems. Lead design reviews and establish standards within your sphere of influence.
  • Hands-on system ownership: Own the technical direction and long-term evolution of key systems while writing and reviewing code, prototyping, debugging, leading migrations, and operating services in production.
  • AI-enabled product and engineering: Identify where models, agents, retrieval, or automation create value. Build reusable capabilities with measurable behavior, guardrails, and judgment about when conventional software is better.
  • Quality, reliability, and incident leadership: Improve testing, performance, observability, security, and operational readiness. Anticipate systemic risks, address technical debt, and help lead resolution and learning during critical production issues.
  • Technical leadership and mentorship: Mentor mid- and senior-level engineers across teams, spread systems thinking and design patterns, and build alignment through proposals, reviews, and influence without authority.
  • Product and technical strategy: Partner with product, design, and engineering leaders to shape the product-area roadmap, align dependencies, and connect technical investment to reader, editorial, and business outcomes.

Skills:

The ideal candidate is a staff-level engineer with sustained multi-team impact, deep expertise in a relevant domain, broad systems thinking, and a commitment to user experience, reliability, scalability, maintainable code, and effective AI-enabled practice. You should have:

  • Experience: Typically 7+ years in professional software development, or equivalent sustained Staff-level impact, including leading complex initiatives across multiple teams or systems.
  • AI-native development: Hands-on experience using agentic coding tools—such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or comparable tools—to complete meaningful, multi-step software work, rather than only generating snippets or using autocomplete.
  • Agent direction and context: Ability to write clear strategies, specifications, and acceptance criteria; provide context; scope complex work; decide what to delegate; and redirect incomplete or incorrect approaches.
  • Verification and engineering judgment: Ability to review AI-generated code critically, validate assumptions, identify security, scalability, and maintainability risks, and catch plausible but wrong solutions. You understand that AI raises the importance of sound architecture, testing, and human judgment.
  • Frontend development: Hands-on experience building production interfaces with JavaScript or TypeScript and React, preferably with Next.js, plus judgment to guide frontend architecture across teams.
  • Backend development: Hands-on experience building production services and APIs. Our backend systems use Go and Python, and you should be able to shape reliable service boundaries and work effectively in or learn either language.
  • Data fundamentals: Experience with relational databases, SQL, schema design, transactions, and migrations.
  • Quality and security: Experience with testing, accessibility, input validation, authentication, authorization, and web security practices, plus the ability to raise standards across teams.
  • Engineering judgment: Ability to operate independently in ambiguity, identify high-leverage problems, align teams, make sound tradeoffs, and connect decisions to product and business goals—including when AI is not the right tool.
  • Communication: Ability to build alignment through clear proposals and reasoning, communicate risks and tradeoffs across functions, and drive clarity during disagreement.
  • Continuous learning: Curiosity about changing models, tools, and practices, paired with an evidence-based approach. You share useful patterns, identify what fails, and make others more effective.

We’ll be even more excited if you have:

  • Experience building production AI-enabled features using model APIs, structured outputs, tool or function calling, retrieval, or agent workflows.
  • Experience evaluating and operating AI-enabled systems through regression tests, evaluation harnesses, tracing, feedback loops, model or prompt versioning, cost and latency monitoring, or human-review paths.
  • Experience extending AI development environments through MCP servers, agent tools, repository instructions, reusable skills or plugins, custom workflows, or automated code review.
  • Led a multi-team architecture, platform, migration, or modernization initiative from problem framing through production adoption.
  • Owned critical systems through incidents, scaling challenges, and long-term architectural evolution.
  • Drove adoption of technical standards, reusable tools, or platform capabilities across multiple teams.
  • Mentored experienced engineers and helped improve technical judgment beyond your immediate team.
  • Experience with CMS, publishing, media, subscription, search, or other consumer-facing products.
  • Production experience with Go or Python and distributed systems using gRPC, cloud infrastructure, containers, queues, CI/CD, or similar technologies.

What success looks like:

  • Cross-team delivery: You drive multi-quarter initiatives from problem framing through production adoption, aligning dependencies and ownership to produce durable outcomes.
  • Engineering leverage: Teams deliver more effectively because of the standards, tools, architecture, documentation, and context you create. You establish safe, repeatable AI patterns where they add value.
  • System health: Key systems become more reliable, scalable, secure, observable, and easier to change. You reduce systemic risk and improve incident prevention and response.
  • Product-area impact: Your decisions support Axios’ readers, products, editorial workflows, and business goals within the teams and systems you influence.
  • Organizational technical leadership: Engineers across teams make better decisions through your mentorship, proposals, reviews, and example. You remain a hands-on IC who multiplies others’ effectiveness.

 

Starting salary for this role is in the range of $165,000 - $215,000 and is dependent on numerous factors, including but not limited to location, work experience, and skills. This range does not include other compensation benefits. Axios' compensation philosophy takes into account the cost of labor differentials across the country. Because this is a remote-optional job posting, this salary range takes into account all possible locations within the United States, but candidates will only be eligible for the salary range for their location.

Axios is committed to embracing artificial intelligence as a core part of how we work. All team members are expected to actively develop AI literacy and use AI tools to enhance their productivity, creativity, and efficiency. We invest in ongoing learning to ensure every employee is equipped to responsibly and effectively integrate AI into their daily workflows.

What Axios brings to the table besides salary:

  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Robust PPO and High Deductible health insurance options on the Blue Cross Blue Shield network
  • Employer Health Savings Account (HSA) contribution for the high deductible health plan option
  • Dental and vision coverage
  • Primary caregiver 12-week paid leave
  • Birth-givers will have an additional 6-8 weeks depending on type of delivery, for a total of 18-20 weeks continuous leave
  • Generous vacation policy, plus holidays
  • One mental health day per quarter
  • Annual learning and development stipend
  • $100 monthly work-from-home stipend
  • Tele-mental health services through Headspace
  • OneMedical membership, including tele-health services
  • Personal health advocacy resources through HealthAdvocate
  • Inclusive fertility, hormonal health and family forming benefits through Carrot Fertility
  • Access to the Axios “Family Fund”, which was created to allow employees to request financial support when facing financial hardship or emergencies
  • Increased work flexibility for parents and caretakers
  • Virtual company-sponsored social events
  • A strong and positive work environment
  • A commitment to an open, inclusive, and diverse work culture

Equal Opportunity Employer Statement 

Axios is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, age, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. 

This policy applies to all employment practices within our organization, including hiring, recruiting, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, leave of absence, compensation, benefits, training, and apprenticeship. Axios makes hiring decisions based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs at the time.

job.title: Account Executive
job.description:
Account Executive

Position Summary

As an Account Executive, you will serve as a trusted marketing consultant to local businesses and advertising agencies, helping clients achieve their business goals through innovative advertising and marketing solutions. This role combines prospecting, relationship building, strategic planning, and revenue generation across Beasley Media Group's portfolio of broadcast, digital, streaming, event, and experiential marketing assets.

The ideal candidate is a motivated self-starter with a passion for sales, strong communication skills, and the ability to develop long-term client partnerships while driving new business growth.

Key Qualifications

  • Self-motivated, goal-oriented professional who thrives both independently and in a collaborative team environment.
  • Excellent verbal, written, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Strong organizational and time management abilities with attention to detail.
  • Effective negotiator with a customer-focused, consultative sales approach.
  • Ability to identify client needs, develop strategic recommendations, and deliver impactful marketing solutions.
  • Proficiency with CRM systems and sales pipeline management.
  • Passion for building relationships and creating measurable results for clients.
  • Valid driver's license, proof of insurance, and reliable transportation required.
  • Employment is contingent upon successful completion of an MVR check

Essential Responsibilities

Business Development & Sales

  • Generate new business opportunities through prospecting, networking, referrals, and outreach efforts.
  • Maintain and grow existing account relationships while increasing revenue and market share.
  • Develop integrated marketing solutions utilizing Beasley Media Group's full suite of advertising platforms.
  • Create and deliver compelling sales presentations and marketing proposals to local businesses and advertising agencies.
  • Identify client business challenges and recommend customized advertising and marketing strategies.
  • Secure sponsorships, promotional partnerships, experiential marketing opportunities, and digital advertising campaigns.
  • Consistently achieve or exceed monthly, quarterly, and annual revenue goals.

Client Relationship Management

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with key decision-makers, stakeholders, and business owners.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned accounts, ensuring exceptional customer service and responsiveness.
  • Regularly communicate with clients regarding campaign performance, marketing initiatives, sponsorships, and business objectives.
  • Identify opportunities to expand partnerships through upselling and cross-selling solutions.

Strategic Planning & Market Research

  • Prepare thoroughly for all client interactions by researching industries, market conditions, business objectives, and competitive trends.
  • Analyze client needs, target audiences, and historical advertising investment to develop effective recommendations.
  • Stay informed on emerging advertising, media, digital marketing, and consumer behavior trends.
  • Utilize market insights and audience data to enhance client outcomes and sales effectiveness.

Product & Industry Expertise

  • Maintain comprehensive knowledge of Beasley Media Group's products, platforms, pricing, audience insights, and marketing capabilities.
  • Continuously expand expertise in radio, digital advertising, streaming audio, video, events, promotions, and experiential marketing.
  • Understand competitive offerings and effectively position Beasley Media Group's advantages in the marketplace.

Administrative & Reporting Responsibilities

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date customer records, activity logs, and sales opportunities within the company CRM.
  • Effectively manage schedules, appointments, account plans, and follow-up activities.
  • Provide timely sales forecasts, pipeline updates, and performance reports as requested by management.
  • Document client interactions and strategic account activities to support business growth and customer retention.

Collaboration & Communication

  • Maintain regular communication with leadership regarding sales activity, pipeline development, client opportunities, and business needs.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to ensure successful execution of advertising campaigns and client initiatives.
  • Support client events, promotions, and experiential marketing activities as needed.
  • Contribute positively to a culture of teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement.

What Success Looks Like

  • Consistently meeting or exceeding revenue goals.
  • Developing strong client relationships that result in long-term partnerships.
  • Generating new business opportunities and expanding existing accounts.
  • Delivering strategic marketing solutions that help clients achieve measurable business results.
  • Serving as a knowledgeable and trusted advisor within the local advertising community.

Beasley Media Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

As the Administrative Officer, you are an essential part of the Payments and Broadcast Contract Administration (PACD) team. You are responsible for handling a wide range of administrative tasks related to contract management and compliance for the broader Business & Rights (BR) team within CBC/Radio-Canada French Services. 


As the Administrative Office, you are part of Radio-Canada's French-language Management of Rights and Business Relations team, which is responsible for negotiating agreements for the acquisition and production of content to be broadcast on Radio-Canada's platforms.


As an Administrative officer you report to the Manager, Contract Operations and Administration, and are responsible for supporting and working closely with project managers by performing administrative tasks related to the conclusion of agreements. To do so, the administrative officer must enter contractual information such as rights, licensing costs, and broadcast obligations into the contract and rights management system and prepare contractual documents (letters, contracts, amendments, or recommendations) and payment tables.


As an Administrative officer, you are also responsible for coordinating approvals and signatures on contractual documents and ensuring the compliance of data entered into the tools used by Radio-Canada. Finally, this role involves collaboration with internal partners, independent producers, and international distributors. 


Function:

Analyze and report on the Corporation’s position and alternatives in selected administrative matters to see how well departmental strategies are being applied, as well as to support decision-making and planning.

  • Negotiate a variety of service contracts and leases within established parameters, providing key administrative support for departmental activities; initiate more significant negotiations by gathering requests, offers and all necessary documents, including comparative data and reports, ahead of time; identify and highlight market trends, standards and related practices to inform the negotiation process.
  • Complete the appropriate forms and documents; prepare the necessary correspondence and reports based on available information, following up as required.
  • Familiarize other people with their job by explaining your own duties.
  • Perform all other administrative tasks.

This role requires full-time on-site presence.

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

Your Role

If you want to push the boundaries of media technology and are excited by the challenge of bridging creativity with cutting-edge tech, this role is for you!

As a key member of the Architecture and Strategic Development (Media System Architecture) team, you will design and plan CBC/Radio-Canada’s future technology infrastructure. Our mission is to transform our disparate media workflows by integrating hybrid agents, video understanding systems and advanced artificial intelligence architectures operating 24/7.

We are looking for an AI Architect with deep technical expertise in optimizing training and inference for large language models (LLMs), multimodal models and AI systems in a media context. As a technical thought leader, you will design robust systems to make AI faster, more scalable and more reliable, ensuring their seamless integration into our critical production ecosystems (PAM, MAM, studios).

Your Responsibilities

Optimizing Models, Inference and GPU Infrastructure

  • Design and build high-performance training and inference systems for LLMs and multimodal AI models.
  • Optimize end-to-end training, including high throughput data pipelines (streaming, sharding, bucketing), distributed training (parallelism strategies) and mixed precision.
  • Optimize inference and serving engines to guarantee minimum latency using KV caching design/management, batching, quantization and long-context processing.
  • Collaborate with the Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) team to design, right-size and evolve our internal GPU cluster into a new-generation infrastructure capable of supporting these massive workloads.

Strategy, Architecture and Media Ecosystem

  • Plan, develop and architect the integration of AI solutions within CBC/Radio-Canada’s media production environments (PAM, MAM, television and radio studios).
  • Evaluate and standardize integration protocols such as Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent (A2A) architectures to interconnect our models with complex production platforms (Avid, Dalet, Adobe).
  • Ensure absolute data security while developing video understanding systems that can interact with both file-based workflows (codecs, wrappers) and IP live workflows (SMPTE‑2110).

Technical Leadership, Mentoring and MLOps

  • Provide expert guidance on system efficiency, spearheading initiatives to dramatically improve architectural scalability, latency and reliability.
  • Mentor and elevate the organization’s engineers and data scientists in large-scale ML system design and performance engineering.
  • Develop robust MLOps/LLMOps pipelines with a constant focus on observability, performance profiling and automated testing.
  • Summarize and explain technological innovations to make them understandable to decision-makers and production teams and influence our strategic investments.

Featured Technology Environment

  • Inference Modelling and Optimization: PyTorch, vLLM, DeepSpeed, Accelerate, KV caching architectures, quantization techniques.
  • Infrastructure, Cloud and Compute: internal GPU clusters, distributed architectures, AWS, Azure, GCP, containers, Kubernetes.
  • Orchestration and Agents: Open WebUI, integration protocols (MCP, A2A), LiteLLM, LangChain, LangGraph, Strands.
  • Media Production: SMPTE-2110 protocols, PAM/MAM (Avid Interplay, Dalet), Adobe suite, media processing (audio/video codecs).
  • MLOps and Observability: Langfuse, Weights & Biases (W&B), MLflow, performance profiling tools.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in software engineering, information technology, artificial intelligence, mathematics or a related natural science field.
  • Functional bilingualism (English and French) essential for Canada-wide communications.
  • At least five years’ proven experience developing and deploying AI/ML solutions.
  • At least eight years’ experience building tools and platforms in a software engineering role.
  • Demonstrated experience working with language models and designing solutions optimized for cost efficiency and scale.
  • Strong conceptual understanding of LLM, RAG and AI agent architectures, including their frameworks and operational constraints.
  • Experience selecting AI framework architectures (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch, Hugging Face), cloud platforms (Azure, AWS, GCP) and orchestration tools (Docker, Kubernetes) for scalable enterprise AI solutions.
  • Knowledge of ModelOps, AI engineering, DevOps and MLOps practices (including CI/CD pipelines).
  • Solid understanding of machine learning and deep learning fundamentals.
  • Strong technical documentation skills, with the ability to produce diagrams, demos and technical artifacts that make AI architectures understandable and actionable.
  • Hands-on technical experience working with media production platforms (MAM/PAM) and designing scalable solutions in a highly available, 24/7 environment.
  • Solid working knowledge of cloud technologies (AWS, Azure or GCP), virtualization, networking and storage.

Nice-to-Have Skills (Assets)

  • Experience with modern video software architectures (e.g., NVIDIA Holoscan for Media) or ultra-high-performance IP transfer protocols.
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex workflows through cloud or hybrid data pipelines.
  • Active contributions to open-source high-performance AI projects and published research, or deep understanding of security frameworks for responsible AI.

The Software and Platform Architecture Team is looking for a creative, highly skilled and talented AI Lead Architect with deep Subject Matter Expertise in AI governance and implementation for our downtown Toronto, Ottawa or Montreal Office location.

Reporting to the Director of Software Architecture and Contract Management, you will be responsible for establishing, leading and contributing to the AI Architecture evolution and governance.

This role will join an existing team of architects who have a focus on software and cloud platforms architecture best practice and governance. 


As part of the Architecture department you will leave your mark by bridging the gap between advanced AI technologies and practical business needs.  You will help design, build, and oversee the integration of scalable artificial intelligence systems, including machine learning pipelines and agentic AI workloads, ensuring security, compliance and alignment with overall enterprise objectives.

You will enjoy innovative work in a creative and dynamic work environment, working with leading technologies, and opportunities for continued professional development.  

How will you make an impact?

As the AI Lead Architect, you will: 

  • Evaluate AI frameworks, platforms and tools (e.g., AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud) to recommend optimal build-versus-buy decisions.
  • Guide foundation model selection aligned with CBC's use cases and infrastructure capabilities.
  • Lead the architecture of AI applications using large language models (LLMs), machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing (NLP).
  • Develop architectural roadmaps for deploying AI initiatives, including generative AI (GenAI), LLMs, and agentic business processes.
  • Lead the integration of scalable artificial intelligence systems, including machine learning pipelines and agentic AI workloads, ensuring security, compliance and alignment with overall enterprise objectives.
  • Monitor emerging AI technologies and assess their business value.
  • Establish architectural standards for model performance, traceability, data lineage, and privacy compliance.
  • Understand business requirements and identify AI use cases.
  • Integrate AI solutions with enterprise applications.
  • Craft prompts, evaluate outputs, and design automated end-to-end agentic workflows.
  • Continuously test and refine models to ensure reliability, scalability, and optimal performance in production.
  • Support continuous monitoring and governance of AI solutions post-deployment.
  • Lead technical discussions with stakeholders and development teams.
  • Work with business leaders to define desired outcomes, success metrics and value drivers for AI initiatives.
  • Collaborate with ethics and compliance teams to ensure AI initiatives adhere to regulatory requirements and CBC's governance standards.
  • Work with business leaders to define desired outcomes, success metrics and value drivers for AI initiatives.
  • Mentor technical teams on AI architecture best practices.

Minimum Requirements

  • A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, or a related field.
  • 3-5 years experience in software architecture, cloud architecture, data engineering, or AI solutions.
  • 1-2 years of experience designing enterprise AI or machine learning solutions.
  • Experience delivering cloud-native AI solutions.
  • Vendor-specific certifications such as the Microsoft Certified: Agentic AI Business Solutions Architect or equivalent AWS/GCP architecture credentials are highly valued.
  • Deep understanding of Machine Learning (ML), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and AI application deployment using languages like Python or R.
  • Knowledge of AI governance frameworks and responsible AI practices.
  • Experience with data management systems and MLOps tools (e.g., Kubernetes, Git, model registries).

Desired Skills

  • Familiarity with enterprise architecture frameworks (TOGAF, Zachman, etc.).

  • Creative and Innovative.

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we all have a story to tell. What’s yours?

 

If you share our passion for Canadian storytelling, and you wish to help us engage with individuals and communities across our various digital platforms, this is where you’ll want to be!

 

Every day, you will have an opportunity to shape the way in which Canadians see themselves reflected in our digital services. Your work will have a direct impact on how millions of Canadians from various communities connect with our products, with one another, and with the diverse voices that make our country so unique.

 

You will have the opportunity to play a part in enlightening and entertaining Canadians through our innovative work in building the mediums that deliver our content. We are an innovative hub, where the talented professionals we work with are respected and valued for their contributions. Our product teams are vibrant and our work culture strives to achieve the highest standards of diversity and inclusion. We believe that hiring people with different career paths and backgrounds is fundamental in our shared success and in building healthy and highly performant teams.

 

When you join our mission, you are not only shaping the vision of CBC/Radio-Canada, but the future of our country.

 

We know that commitment to equity, inclusion and diversity is essential to creating content that mirrors and resonates with the rich and evolving makeup of our country.  We’re also committed to reaching out and connecting with our audience on multiple platforms this includes creating virtual places where communities can come together.

This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

Why is this role important?

 

You will be an important element of our over-the-top platform team. As such, working closely with the product owners, architects and technical managers, your role is to ensure the smooth execution of product front-end development and coordinate the technical work required to deliver requested features, while adhering to the standards and practices agreed to by the development management team.

 

The team you will be part of is in charge of an harmonized product, powering CBC Gem and ICI TOU.TV.

CBC North is looking for an Announcer/Operator. Reporting to the Managing Editor, the Announcer/Operator for Nipivut is responsible for finding, researching, preparing and presenting interviews, packaged items, hosting and operating CBC Nunavut/Nunavik’s noon show in Inuktitut and English. Nipivut is a daily radio show focusing on Iqaluit and stories important to Nunavut’s capital city.


Function

Performs a variety of tasks associated with the preparation, production and presentation of programs and program material – for example, announcing, hosting, versioning between English and Inuktitut, writing and operating production equipment. Work is governed by CBC program and journalistic policies and practices but is performed in the unique broadcasting environment of the community station where limited resources dictate the need for versatility, cooperation and teamwork. Activities generally conform to predetermined formats but there is latitude for initiative and independent judgment. Work can involve coordination of the work of others.


Key Tasks:

  • Plans and organizes, or participates in the planning and organizing of programs or program segments, ensures the preparation of material for broadcast and, where a Producer is not assigned, assumes production responsibility.
  • Proposes program ideas, suggests and lines up guests or interviewees, prepares background notes and questions, and conducts interviews on or off air.
  • Writes material for broadcast.
  • Develops and maintains contacts with a variety of sources.
  • Gathers and reports information from various sources.
  • Evaluates information gathered, organizes it and presents it on air in a coherent and understandable form.
  • Edits program material.
  • Interacts with program participants such as guests, interviewees, panelists and/or members of the audience. Uses interviewing skills to elicit pertinent facts and information.
  • Provides narration and linking continuity between program segments.
  • Describes actualities such as music programs, parades and sporting or other special events.
  • Reads newscasts, news bulletins, weather forecasts and other survival information.
  • Ensures the proper operating condition of equipment by making the necessary checks.
  • Ensures that program audio mixes achieve optimum results.
  • In case of technical failure, makes emergency substitutions or repairs to maintain clear and continuous service; ensures appropriate follow-up.

As required, performs the following tasks:

  • Participate in community relations activities to promote the CBC.
  • Direct a program or program segment in studio or at a remote location.
  • Maintain an appropriate level of communication with members of the audience.
  • Archive programs and program scripts and lineups.
  • Perform incidental technical functions necessary to ensure the smooth and continuous functioning of the station.


The successful candidate will have:

  • A minimum of a high school education or an acceptable combination of education and work experience.  Previous on-air experience in radio or television would be an asset.
  • Excellent on-air presentation skills.  
  • Excellent Inuktitut skills.
  • Good writing, and interviewing skills.
  • A critical thinker with strong editorial judgment.
  • A strong understanding of Inuit and northern issues.
  • Good computer skills and willingness to maintain Social Media networks using external platforms like Facebook, Twitter etc.
  • Mature, positive attitude and an excellent ability to contribute to a team environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to perform at a high level in a high pressure, tight deadline environment.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.

This role requires full time on site presence. 


CBC News is designing new ways for Canadians to understand and navigate their finances, helping them make sense of a myriad of complex economic realities through expanded financial and consumer storytelling. 

To help audiences discover that content when they want it, on their platform of choice, we’re hiring a Senior Coordinating Producer to join the CBC Audience Growth team. This is an opportunity to help shape and grow a new destination for practical, news-you-can-use financial journalism.


In this role, you’ll sit right where editorial meets audience growth, collaborating with content teams across CBC News, Entertainment and Sports to make CBC a top destination for financial journalism and related content. 


You play a critical role in identifying new audiences, and advising on the best strategies and tactics to reach them across CBC digital properties, FAST channels, CBC Gem, CBC linear channels, as well as on third-party platforms including Youtube and Tik Tok. You understand how to move people beyond discoverability and into loyal audiences who actively engage with our content, whether subscribing to newsletters, engaging with content and sharing videos. You search for opportunities to reflect a broad range of perspectives and voices in the content we share. 


You are passionate about using audience insights to inform journalism decisions, capable of analyzing reach and engagement time and adjusting your tactics to ensure the best audience experience. You have knowledge of digital products, and our owned and operated, and third party platforms.

You are future-focused, open to experimenting with new technologies, audio/visual formats and content to meet changing audience needs. 


You’re a collaborator, able to work with everyone from  front-line journalists and program leaders, to colleagues across CBC genres to optimize CBC’s best digital, social, and broadcast journalism into one easy-to-find audience experience.


What you’ll do:

  • Own the digital publishing strategy for cross division financial reporting,  working in close association with the CBC News publishing team, including aggregation, packaging, lineup management and other direct publishing functions.
  • Help manage push alerts, newsletters, YouTube and TikTok packaging, alongside and as a part of the CBC News Audience Growth team. 
  • Play a key role in planning and live event plans for major financial and money-related journalism. As required, verify user-generated content to ensure accuracy.
  • Coordinate work with business unit content teams currently based in Calgary and Toronto, as well as audio syndication, current affairs and podcasting to ensure a smooth workflow between platforms.
  • Aggregate, showcase and promote financial, business and consumer content from CBC News, CBC Entertainment and CBC Sports.
  • Use data and analytics to shape our headlines, thumbnails, and rollout plans.
  • Guide, coach and support colleagues on best-of-practices and through change as required, across local and network newsrooms.
  • Ensure that CBC journalistic standards are met and that our stories are fair, balanced, accurate, thoughtful, immediate and resonate with the communities we serve. 

What you bring: 


  • At least seven (7) years of recent experience in a large digital news environment,
  • Substantial experience writing, editing, packaging and copy editing digital content in a compelling way. 
  • Some experience helping to launch or create new content initiatives. 
  • Experience with content management systems such as Moveable Type, Media Central, MPX/The Platform, including ability to edit, photoshop and publish within those platforms; and basic HTML/CSS
  • Advanced knowledge of social platforms, including YouTube, Tik Tok, Snapchat and WhatsApp, including their algorithms and community features. 
  • Proven ability to analyze performance metrics and audience data using  measurement tools such as Chartbeat, Adobe analytics, Google Analytics. 
  • Strong visualization skills, including experience in using graphics, charts and explainers to distill complex financial data into easily digestible and actionable content. 
  • Ability to manage large volumes of fast-moving information and ensure material is distributed appropriately 24/7.
  • Excellent journalism skills with a strong general knowledge about Canadian and international economics, financial, business and consumer issues.
  • Ability to assign, manage and motivate staff and to coordinate with colleagues across departments in a productive manner and ability to mediate disputes as they arise. 
  • Excellent journalistic and critical thinking skills, including a deep knowledge of the legal and ethical issues related to business and consumer journalism.
  • Demonstrated ability to bring new perspectives, voices and lived experiences into your daily journalism. 
  • Strong communication, collaboration and interpersonal skills. 
  • Ability and willingness to work flexible hours as required.
  • Possession of a valid driver’s license as well as a driving record that meets the minimum requirements of CBC/Radio-Canada's insurance company.

That schedule is subject to change based on operational needs.


We are looking to hire an experienced copy editor to join our team and support journalism across British Columbia and our Local Service Expansion reporters in parts of western Canada.  


Reporting to the executive producer and coordinating producer, you will be responsible for the timely editing and delivery of a range of news stories — from breaking news to long-form features — to CBC’s digital and social platforms, while ensuring accuracy and balance. 


The successful candidate will demonstrate an understanding and awareness of issues and events particular to British Columbia, and will have strong ties to, and a deep understanding of, under-represented communities and equity-deserving groups across the province.

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

 

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

 

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

 

This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.


This position can be based in Montreal, Toronto or Ottawa.

 

Your Role

 

The Director, AI Governance and Adoption is responsible for driving the evolution of the enterprise AI governance framework, and facilitating the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence technologies across the organization. Acting as a strategic partner to executives and business teams, this individual supports the identification of opportunities, the integration of value-creating solutions and the development of an AI-literate culture. The incumbent also oversees the development of the practices, policies and governance mechanisms required to ensure the responsible and sustainable use of artificial intelligence technologies.

 

Key Responsibilities

 

Governance, Policy & Risk Management

  • Define and enforce corporate AI policies, directives, and guardrails across all business units.
  • Operationalize risk controls and decision accountabilities across the entire AI lifecycle (procurement, data retrieval, tool actions, and human oversight).
  • Build and maintain a central inventory of all internal and third-party AI assets to track systemic risk.

 

Shadow AI & Secure Experimentation

  • Audit unsanctioned AI tools ("shadow AI") across departments and facilitate the transition of use cases into secure enterprise environments.
  • Partner with tech teams to set safety guardrails for low-code/no-code tools, allowing employees to experiment safely.

 

Leadership, Committees & Alignment

  • Lead the AI Usage Oversight Committee and coordinate the enterprise AI Steering Committee.
  • Align AI initiatives with Legal, Privacy, InfoSec, Data Governance, and Journalistic Standards to ensure regulatory compliance.

 

Adoption, Enablement & Literacy

  • Develop training programs, playbooks, office hours, and champion networks to boost organization-wide AI literacy.
  • Help business units integrate deployed AI solutions into their everyday production workflows.

 

Workflow Re-Engineering & Value Tracking

  • Direct a cross-functional "Fusion Team" to help management re-engineer legacy workflows for native AI integration.
  • Define, track, and report performance and governance metrics to prove ROI and accountability.

 

Vendor Management & Industry Representation

  • Advise Procurement and Legal on standards for evaluating and onboarding third-party AI vendors.
  • Represent the organization (CBC/Radio-Canada) at national and international conferences, contributing to public media data provenance standards.

 

Internal Governance & Executive Alignment

  • Senior Advisory: Advise executives on AI strategy, run governance committees, and deliver executive leadership-level briefings when required.
  • Standards & Training: Roll out AI policies across all departments (Media, Tech, Business) and partner with L&D on staff training and literacy initiatives.

 

AI Adoption & Change Management

  • Fusion Team Leadership: Stand up and lead a cross-functional team of change management, training, and process optimization specialists.
  • Workflow Integration: Work with department heads and staff to resolve workflow pain points and drive adoption of approved AI tools.
  • Tracking & Reporting: Partner with Innovation Leads to establish ROI metrics and report adoption progress, blockers, and learnings to leadership.

 

External Relations & Industry Networks

  • Industry and Peer Collaboration: Partner with media organizations, industry groups (EBU, INMA), and analysts (Gartner) to benchmark best practices.
  • Thought Leadership: Share CBC/RC case studies and governance frameworks with external and public stakeholders.

 

What You Bring

 

Qualifications, experience & skills

  • 7+ years of technology leadership experience, with 3 years of supervisory experience required.
  • At least 5 years explicitly focused on operationalizing data or technology strategy, machine learning, technology risk management, or corporate governance programs.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required. A degree in Information Technology, Computer Systems Analysis, Engineering, or Management Information Systems is preferred.
  • Bilingualism (English and French).
  • Enterprise AI Governance: Proven track record building and managing AI oversight programs, governing models and agentic workflows, and developing policies, audits, and control documentation.
  • Strategy-to-Operations: Ability to turn high-level strategy into actionable standards, operational workflows, and scalable operating models.
  • Enterprise Change & Adoption: Demonstrated success scaling technology adoption across matrixed, multi-stakeholder organizations.
  • AI & Data Expertise: Deep knowledge of AI lifecycles, generative/agentic risks, data privacy, and public media compliance standards.
  • Executive Leadership: Exceptional communication skills to translate complex AI concepts and risks into business impact for executive and board-level stakeholders.

Your Role

 

In an environment where data has become a critical strategic asset supporting decision-making, advanced analytics and artificial intelligence solutions, CBC/Radio-Canada is implementing an enterprise-wide data governance program. The creation of the Director, Enterprise Data Governance role is at the heart of this transformation and aims to establish the foundations required for the effective, secure and consistent management of information assets.

 

Key Responsibilities

 

Framework, Policies & Compliance

  • Develop, refine, and enforce enterprise-wide data governance policies, directives, and standards aligned with corporate priorities.
  • Work with Legal, InfoSec, and Data Engineering to establish data classification rules, access controls, and compliance monitoring.
  • Define core data concepts and maintain central governance documentation and artifacts.

 

Core Programs & Data Operations

  • Data Catalog & Metadata: Oversee the implementation of an enterprise data catalog and metadata management processes to ensure reporting mechanisms and datasets are clear and accessible.
  • Data Quality & Lineage: Stand up an enterprise data quality program and implement data lineage tracking to monitor how data moves across systems.
  • Usability & AI Readiness: Partner with technology and analytics teams to make sure data is clean and structured for BI, reporting, and AI/ML models.

 

Governance Bodies & Stakeholder Leadership

  • Manage the Enterprise Data Governance Steering Committee to align senior leadership on strategic priorities.
  • Lead the Enterprise Data Council (domain leads and Data Officers) to translate strategic directives into policies and actionable initiatives.
  • Drive the creation of cross-functional networks of data stewards, owners, custodians, and working groups as needed.

 

Data Literacy & Culture

  • Lead change management, training, and communication programs to improve overall data literacy across the corporation.
  • Influence senior executives and business stakeholders to adopt governance practices and understand their role in protecting and using data.
  • Build, mentor, and lead a small, high-impact data governance team.

 

Metrics, KPI Tracking & Reporting                       

  • Define, track, and report on core governance KPIs, including data quality, issue resolution, policy compliance, and user adoption.
  • Build and maintain executive dashboards to regularly report program progress and outcomes to leadership.

 

What You Bring

 

Qualifications, experience & skills

  • 5+ years of experience in data management, governance, or a related field.
  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field.
  • Proven experience building and launching enterprise data governance programs.
  • Experience leading enterprise-grade data catalog / data governance tooling initiatives.

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public broadcaster.

Technology and Infrastructures (T&I) is the backbone and the future forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. We are the people that make stuff work.  We make connections; between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly-regarded pioneer of media technology. Not just in Canada, but around the world. Today, we’re transforming ourselves from conventional radio and television broadcaster into a modern digital media company. Technology is the driving force. T&I is the team making it happen.

This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

Your Role


We are looking for highly skilled and organized Enterprise Architect with deep subject matter expertise in Enterprise Software and Platform Architecture for our downtown Toronto, Ottawa or Montreal Office location.

Reporting to the Director of Software and Platform Architecture, you will be responsible for establishing an unified technological vision by understanding business processes and translating business requirements into technical solutions that deliver business value.

As part of the Architecture and Strategic Development (ASD) Department you will leave your mark by driving the shift from IT-centric to business-centric enterprise architecture.

You will enjoy innovative work in a creative and dynamic work environment, working with leading technologies and opportunities for continued professional development.  

How will you make an impact?

As the Enterprise Architect, you will:

  • Define and promote  a common vision of Enterprise Architecture  and establish clear direction on roles, responsibilities and priorities with stakeholders.
  • Lead the evolution of the Enterprise Architecture practice and drive the shift from IT-centric to business-centric enterprise architecture.
  • Define the strategy to connect EA with data governance,risk management, information security to monitor its implementation and effectiveness.
  • Participate in designing, documenting and communicating the current and target state architectures for major initiatives and other vendor-driven system replacements.
  • Document the High Level Architecture that outlines the structure, components, and relationships between business processes, data, applications and technology infrastructure.
  • Ensure that enterprise investments align with business goals and objectives.
  • Ensure that architectural decisions align with organizational policies, industry best practices and regulatory requirements.
  • Help establish and enforce architecture governance processes and standards.
  • Drive innovation by identifying emerging technologies and evaluating their potential for the organization.
  • Coach and mentor other architects, product owners/managers and business stakeholders to instill architectural thinking.
  • Build and maintain relationships with business and  technology stakeholders.

Perks you can look forward to:

  • Four weeks of vacation per year.
  • Work from home opportunities.
  • Competitive total rewards package.
  • Opportunities to work with cutting edge technology.
  • Opportunities for continued learning and professional development - including access to e-learning services, customized courses and certification opportunities.
  • Opportunities to become a member of our Employee Resource Groups.
  • A creative and dynamic work environment, where your ideas and contributions can be heard, valued and respected.
  • A supportive management team committed to upholding the highest standards of diversity and inclusivity.

What you bring to our team

Minimum Requirements

  • Minimum Bachelor’s degree in computer science, business (or related experience).
  • Five or more years of enterprise architecture and/or business experience in strategic and operations planning.
  • Ten or more years of experience in solution or technical architecture and application development.
  • Knowledge of business ecosystems such as SaaS, Cloud Platforms, On-prem and hybrid solutions.
  • Understanding of business models, operating models, financial models, cost-benefit analysis, budgeting and risk management.
  • Familiarity with enterprise architecture tools, related graphical models and frameworks.
  • Understanding of various operating models such as project-centric and product-centric.
  • Effective leadership skills with strong soft and interpersonal skills, including teamwork, facilitation and negotiation.

Desired Skills

  • Organizationally savvy, with situational and contextual intelligence of the political climate of the enterprise and how to navigate obstacles and politics.
  • Balances the long-term (“big picture”) and short-term implications of individual decisions and organization goals.
  • Excellent written, verbal, communication and presentation skills with the ability to articulate new ideas and concepts to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Ability to work with remote teams.
  • Bilingualism (English and French) is a strong asset.

CBC Prince Edward Island is looking for a host for its Island Morning radio program.  

In this role, you will be the voice that sets the news agenda for listeners across P.E.I., helping them make sense of their world as they get up each morning.

You are an insatiably curious early-morning storyteller with a passion for drawing emotion and stories out of interview guests. You are equally comfortable holding a politician accountable as you are chatting with children, and you know when to put people at ease and when to challenge them. 

You understand that audiences want to be both entertained and informed as they start their day, and you realize the importance of making audiences feel welcome and part of a community. You know that using a full range of tone, including humour, is key to strong radio current affairs programming.

You have a sense of adventure, an eclectic range of interests and a keen desire to meet new people, explore our communities, and learn other perspectives. You are passionate about championing stories from P.E.I.’s under-represented communities, and you love meeting listeners where they live through in-person public appearances and at remotes.

An experienced journalist and a keen observer, you must be able to quickly analyze a broad range of issues and thrive in the fast-paced, high-pressure world of live, local radio. You have a strong grasp of our province’s political landscape and its resource-driven economy, and you understand how these issues affect the day-to-day lives of the people who live here.

As a member of the Morning team, it’s clear you care about your colleagues. You act as a team unifier and collaborator, and are always looking for creative solutions to challenges.

This role requires full time on site presence. 

Your responsibilities:

  • Pitch and produce original stories that deepen Island Morning’s community connections, elevate a range of voices and reflect the day’s top local news.

  • Conduct research and interviews, gather audio, write radio scripts, and package and present content for all platforms including audio, video and digital. 

  • Host Island Morning live on air between 6:00-8:30 a.m. weekdays, conducting interviews on a wide variety of current events.

  • Interact extemporaneously with program participants such as guests, reporters, experts and members of the audience.

  • Participate in public relations or community outreach activities to promote Island Morning and CBC, with a focus on growing new audiences and building community connections.

Your profile:

  • An engaging, curious, and spontaneous on-air personality, with a wide range of genuine interests, knowledge and insight, reflecting curiosity in many current affairs topics, and an ability to make them relevant to existing and new audiences.

  • Strong journalistic skills, demonstrated through original story ideas, live interviewing, innovative storytelling, and writing and vetting abilities.

  • Excellent critical thinking skills, including knowledge of and familiarity with CBC Journalistic Standards as well as the legal and ethical issues related to journalism.

  • Ability to react quickly to changing circumstances and breaking news; comfortable going off-script when needed.

  • Familiarity with digital and social storytelling, including podcasting, and a willingness to learn and tackle new tasks across all CBC platforms (TV, radio, digital).

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across teams and locations.

  • A proven work ethic and a positive team-first attitude. 

  • A strong desire to live and promote the values of diversity and an inclusive and respectful work culture.

  • A passion for public outreach and an enthusiastic ambassador of public broadcasting and the program.

  • Ability to work a variety of shifts including early starts, late finishes and weekends.

  • University degree or equivalent in a related field, with a minimum of five years of relevant or comparable experience.

We want to hear what you sound like! Please include a link to samples of your on-air work in your cover letter.

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media.

 

The Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) team is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation's technologies and infrastructure, enabling the creation and continued delivery of quality content across all platforms. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people, and places. We are the space in between.

 

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology—not just in Canada, but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force and we are the team making it happen.

 

This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines and operational needs.

 

Your Role

 

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Strategic Alignment and Engagement, the Junior Specialist plays a pivotal role in nurturing corporate culture and enhancing the employee experience within CBC/Radio-Canada’s Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) division.

 

As a key member of the People & Engagement team, you will act as a champion for internal engagement initiatives. You will collaborate with clients and partners to deliver ad hoc communications support while co-ordinating and rolling out events and initiatives that drive active participation, team cohesion and a sense of community. In this role, you will leverage your interpersonal strengths, writing flair and graphic design talent to build meaningful relationships and produce compelling copy and visual content.

 

We are seeking a versatile communicator with a keen interest in technology and employee engagement. You bring exceptional bilingual writing abilities (French and English), sharp analytical thinking and the skill to quickly distil complex technical concepts into clear, captivating messaging and eye-catching visual designs.

 

Outstanding interpersonal skills will enable you to thrive as an advocate for team culture and create the type of engaging content required for the role.

 

The position can be based in Toronto or Montreal.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Gather content for, design and share internal communications materials with the goal of building a unified, engaging culture within T&I.
  • Create and maintain communication channels and platforms targeting T&I, including the newsletter, staff portal and iO pages.
  • Provide logistical support for internal events designed to strengthen the workplace culture at T&I.
  • Connect with T&I team members to boost engagement and uncover inspiring stories that build pride and belonging.
  • Actively support the development and rollout of engagement programs and campaigns that inspire employee participation.
  • Apply graphic design expertise to create dynamic, high-impact visuals tailored to various communication channels.
  • Stay aligned with CBC/Radio-Canada and T&I strategic priorities — specifically regarding official languages, equity, diversity and inclusion — to ensure consistent, relevant and effective messaging.
  • Help define T&I’s voice, culture and brand to ensure clear recognition and strong resonance among staff.
  • Actively contribute to co-ordinating and promoting corporate and T&I initiatives.
  • Adhere to and promote organizational content accessibility standards.

 

What You Bring

 

Skills and Qualifications

  • University degree in communications, marketing, public relations or journalism an asset.
  • Experience in event co-ordination and content writing.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills in both official languages (English and French).
  • Ability to work well in a team environment and collaborate effectively with others.
  • High degree of autonomy and self-motivation.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with a proven ability to respond to multiple urgent requests and meet deadlines.
  • Ability to clearly demonstrate flexibility and agility when faced with changing priorities.
  • Strong graphic design skills and proficiency with visual design software (such as the Adobe Creative Cloud suite) an asset.
  • Familiarity with content management systems (CMSs), Mailchimp and RGE Studio an asset.

Program Manager


This is a permanent full-time role, based in Regina.

CBC Saskatchewan is looking for a program manager to help lead CBC Saskatchewan at a pivotal time in the province’s history. You will report to the Director, Journalism and work alongside CBC Saskatchewan’s leadership team to execute the station’s editorial vision on our programs.


As the program manager, you will lead all programming on video, audio and digital platforms. You will be a key point person, along with the Managing Editor, in JSP guidance and programming direction. You will work closely with our communications team to ensure program and community outreach align.


You will be a champion of audience growth. You will bring audience metrics and data to our program teams. And you will work relentlessly to help connect our storytelling with the community. 


You will work with a great team, and will be a key supporter of its ongoing development.


You will be a great leader, and an even better teammate.


Main responsibilities:


  • Oversee CBC Saskatchewan programming
  • Work within the leadership team to execute an editorial vision across CBC digital, radio, and visuals that balances immediate breaking news with enterprise storytelling.
  • Ensure our storytelling adheres to CBC’s journalistic standards and practices, ensuring all content is fair, balanced, and accurate. 
  • Ensure our coverage reflects the true diversity of Saskatchewan, building trust with new audiences through inclusive storytelling.
  • Oversees the station’s community outreach strategy
  • Ensure program content is strategically leveraged, adapted, and shared across CBC Saskatchewan’s digital and television platforms to maximize impact.
  • Drive the CBC Saskatchewan hiring strategy.
  • Oversee the onboarding of new editorial staff, ensuring deep familiarity with CBC’s Journalistic Policy, technical tools, and local newsroom culture.
  • Oversee performance management of all programs, including mentorship and training and development.
  • Act as the primary local authority on CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices (JSP), when Managing Editor is unavailable, ensuring all stories meet the core tenets of accuracy, fairness, balance, and integrity.
  • Provide real-time counsel on complex journalistic questions, including legal risks (defamation, publication bans), ethical dilemmas, and sensitive interviews.
  • Serve as the final escalation point in the newsroom for breaking, highly sensitive, or controversial local stories, coordinating with CBC Legal and network leadership when necessary.
  • Help navigate audience complaints or corrections transparently, upholding CBC’s accountability to the public


Experience Required

  • Minimum of 10 years' related experience, including experience leading in a newsroom 
  • A track record of guiding complex journalistic decision making
  • Experience managing staff and resources within budgetary constraints
  • Experience leading the application of journalistic standards and practices in a daily newsroom setting
  • An ongoing interest in and understanding of media trends as they apply to a multiplatform newsroom
  • Experience in setting clear objectives and goals, and then to deliver on them 
  • Proven ability to make decisions rapidly and frequently within tight deadlines

In this role, you will work closely with the host of CBC Morning Live on daily and longer-term projects. Working with the senior producer and other program leaders, you identify, develop and produce daily responsive video segments that run within live programming, while ensuring they’re optimized for people to watch on-demand on mobile. You also support breaking news coverage and special programming, including when the program is hosted from the field.  


You have experience writing for broadcast and working with video - from gathering to editing. You know your way around a control room and how a program is crafted. You can also spot opportunities to expand the reach of our journalism to new viewers - always advocating for the audience and how we can address their needs on any given story. You thrive in breaking news and are a fountain of ideas of how to treat it. You thrive in a high-stress, tight-deadline environment and are able to work flexible hours and on weekends, if needed.


The ideal candidate will hit the ground running because of their familiarity with key production tools. Experience on a national news team is crucial and experience working with digital and/or social content is a strong asset.

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we all have a story to tell. What’s yours?

 

If you share our passion for Canadian storytelling and you wish to help us engage with individuals and communities across our various digital platforms, this is where you’ll want to be!

 

Every day, you’ll have an opportunity to shape the way in which Canadians see themselves reflected in our digital services. Your work will have a direct impact on how millions of Canadians from various communities connect with our products, with one another and with the diverse voices that make our country so unique.

 

You’ll have the opportunity to play a part in enlightening and entertaining Canadians through our innovative work in building the mediums that deliver our content. We’re an innovative hub, where the talented professionals we work with are respected and valued for their contributions. Our product teams are vibrant, and our work culture strives to achieve the highest standards of diversity and inclusion. We believe that hiring people with different career paths and backgrounds is fundamental in our shared success and in building healthy, high-performing teams. When you join our mission, you’re not only shaping the vision of CBC/Radio-Canada, but the future of our country.

 

We know that commitment to equity, inclusion and diversity is essential to creating content that mirrors and resonates with the rich and evolving makeup of our country. We’re also committed to reaching out and connecting with our audience on multiple platforms; this includes creating virtual places where communities can come together.


This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

Why This Role Matters

 

You will be a core member of our software development team. Working closely with product managers and developers, your mission is to champion product quality from day one by embedding a shift-left testing strategy.

 

Rather than testing only at the end of the release pipeline, you will collaborate from the initial requirements and design phases to prevent defects, establish clear acceptance criteria and help shape our test architecture. You will drive comprehensive testing strategies — spanning automated, exploratory and regression testing — to ensure smooth, frequent and reliable releases while advancing adherence to quality standards and industry best practices.

 

Our team is responsible for the OHdio ecosystem, Radio-Canada’s flagship French-language audio platform. By joining this cross-platform initiative (covering iOS and Android mobile apps, web, connected car systems like CarPlay and Android Auto, and smart devices), you will directly impact the daily listening experience of hundreds of thousands of users. From live radio streams and original podcasts to audiobooks and curated playlists, you will ensure continuous stability, high performance and top-tier quality for a premier digital product.

 

Our Evolving Quality Culture

 

The OHdio team is actively transitioning to an integrated quality engineering culture. You won't be stepping into a rigid, pre-established framework; you will play a hands-on role in building it. You will help drive our shift-left practices, structure our automated testing stack (Playwright, Appium, TestRail) and define the engineering standards that will guide our team for years to come. If you want to make a lasting impact on how we build and ship digital products, this role is for you.


Perks you can look forward to:

  • Flexible work schedules, allowing you to prioritize yourself, your family and your work.
  • Work from home opportunities.
  • Competitive total rewards package.
  • Opportunities to work with cutting edge technology.
  • Opportunities for continued learning and professional development.
  • Opportunities to become a member of our Employee Resource Groups.
  • Pair programming and mentorship opportunities, where you can learn from the best in the industry and help coach new talent.
  • A creative and dynamic work environment, where your ideas and contributions can be heard, valued and respected.
  • A supportive management team committed to upholding the highest standards of diversity and inclusivity.
  • An environment which favours experimentation and an iterative approach in order to achieve the highest form of technical innovation.

 

How You Will Make an Impact

  • Actively participate in design sessions to identify acceptance criteria, edge cases, risks and functional ambiguities before development begins.
  • Act as a quality gatekeeper to ensure features meet all readiness criteria before entering the development workflow.
  • Draft and maintain structured test cases (BDD/steps) in TestRail, prioritizing them as the product evolves.
  • Define feature-level test strategies alongside developers, determining the appropriate test types (unit, integration, snapshot, E2E, manual) across each layer.
  • Identify and prepare necessary test data for validation.
  • Collaborate with developers during sprints to clarify acceptance criteria and resolve ambiguous technical behaviours.
  • Perform incremental validations throughout the sprint to catch defects early.
  • Document defects with clear, reproducible steps so developers can act on them immediately without back-and-forth.
  • Help build, expand and maintain our automated test suite in collaboration with developers.
  • Actively participate in the release management process.
  • Track and analyze quality KPIs (defect discovery stages, reopen rates, automation coverage, etc.) to drive data-informed retrospectives.
  • Share best practices with other QAAs to maintain consistent approaches across projects.
  • Empower all team members to work autonomously and take ownership of quality.

 

What You Bring

  • College diploma or university degree, or equivalent experience.
  • Experience working on complex web and mobile application development projects.
  • Strong hands-on experience with shift-left QA practices (e.g., drafting acceptance criteria and test cases prior to development).
  • Deep understanding of application life cycles across iOS, Android and web environments.
  • Solid grasp of test pyramid concepts (unit, integration, snapshot, E2E, smoke and regression testing).
  • Experience writing BDD test scenarios (Gherkin syntax) in TestRail.
  • Proficiency with API testing and payload validation tools (Postman, Playwright API or equivalent).
  • Ability to interpret CI/CD build results and diagnose pipeline failures.
  • Experience conducting structured exploratory testing.
  • Confidence in making data-driven go/no-go release decisions.
  • Strong collaborative approach when working alongside developers and product owners.
  • A proactive mindset with a knack for asking the right questions to resolve ambiguities before they turn into defects.
  • High attention to detail and self-direction skills.
  • Experience working within Agile environments.
  • Fluency in French (required).
  • Working knowledge of spoken and written English an asset.
  • Experience with mobile E2E automation frameworks (Appium, Detox or equivalent) an asset.
  • Familiarity with AI-assisted testing tools (Copilot, MCP TestRail, agentic AI) an asset.
  • Proficiency with browser diagnostic tools (Chrome DevTools) an asset.
  • Understanding of digital accessibility standards (A11Y) an asset.

 

Please note this is a 12-month contract position, renewable annually. This regular position is not a consulting role but a long-term opportunity with competitive CBC/Radio-Canada employee benefits.
