job.title: INVESTIGATIVE REPORTER/MMJ - WNDU
job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. The portfolio includes 80 markets with the top-rated television station and 100 markets with the first and/or second highest rated television station in average all-day ratings across 116 of such markets that were measured by Nielsen in 2025. We also own the largest Telemundo Affiliate group with 46 markets and Gray Digital Media, a full-service digital agency offering national and local clients digital marketing strategies with the most advanced digital products and services. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About WNDU:

WNDU boasts a history of more than 70 years and sits on the campus of the world-renowned University of Notre Dame. We cover northwest Indiana and southwest Michigan. We produce over 36 hours of live news each week and continue to expand our coverage. Our team is committed to the highest standards in news, entertainment, informational, and public service programming. Our viewers love having a major research university in their backyard, the history of a strong manufacturing sector, and a robust court system. They also demand accountability from those institutions. The stories are here. We need the right journalist to find the stories and tell them.

Job Summary/Description:

WNDU in South Bend, Indiana is looking for an Investigative Reporter/MMJ. You will dig. You will file records requests. You will work sources. You will gather documents. You will tell complex, consequential stories in ways that are clear, fair, and impossible to ignore. And you will do it across every platform, on air, online, and on social. This role is not just about producing lengthy series pieces; we expect you on air regularly as part of the 16 News Now team. When a breaking news story has an investigative angle, a document, a record, a source with context no one else has, we want you gathering and fronting that information, bringing depth and accountability to stories as they happen, not weeks later. If you have the chops and the experience, we want to hear from you; apply now.

Duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

- Drive original daily investigative and enterprise reporting for WNDU. We need more than a long-form series. We want accountability journalism that shows up in every newscast.
- File and manage public records requests (FOIA, state open records) as a core reporting tool, not an afterthought.
- Use data, documents, and records to build stories from the ground up.
- Develop, cultivate, and protect confidential sources across government, law enforcement, business, and the community.
- Examine breaking and day-of news through an investigative lens - gathering records, sourcing context, and fronting stories that go deeper than the surface.
- Manage longer-form investigations simultaneously at different stages of development.
- Shoot, write, edit, and present your own stories as a full MMJ. Own the story from pitch to air. We do have photographers who will work with you, but you shouldn't be reliant on them for every story or shoot.
- Translate complex investigative findings into compelling, accessible content for broadcast, digital, and social audiences.
- Collaborate with editorial leadership on story development, legal review, and publication strategy.
- Uphold the highest standards of accuracy, fairness, and SPJ ethics - every story, every time.

Qualifications/Requirements:

- Proven investigative or accountability reporting experience; we want to see the work.
- A track record of using public records, data, or documents to break original stories.
- The ability to work at two speeds simultaneously: daily investigative hits AND longer-term series development.
- Strong on-camera presence and MMJ skills; you shoot, edit, and present your own material, and you are comfortable being a visible, recognizable face of the 16 News Now brand.
- Source development skills built over time; you have relationships, and you know how to build new ones.
- The ability to take a dense, document-heavy story and make it matter to a general audience.
- Unshakable ethical standards; you understand the weight of this work, and you handle it accordingly.
- Comfort with legal and editorial scrutiny; you document your reporting, and you stand behind it.
- Resilience: investigations get complicated, sources go cold, and stories take longer than expected, but you do not quit.
- Valid U.S. driver's license and ability to drive a company vehicle.
- A journalism-related degree is preferred, but not required; your body of work must speak for itself.
- Must be able to carry 35+ pounds of gear, and be experienced in shooting and editing unique content. We do have photographers to partner with on appropriate assignments.
- Familiarity with ENPS, Arc, and Edius is a plus, but not required.

If you feel you’re qualified and want to work with a great group of people,  go to https://gray.tv/careers#currentopenings, you may type in the job title, station call letters, or click on "apply now", upload your resume, cover letter, and references

job.title: MEDIA EXECUTIVE - KSFY/KDLT (SIOUX FALLS)
job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About KSFY/KDLT:

Sioux Falls and the surrounding area remain one of the fastest-growing regions in the Upper Midwest and are home to 300,000 people, constituting more than 30% of the state's population. Healthcare and finance make up much of a diverse and broad workforce. The business climate in South Dakota continues to be one of the top in the nation, fueled by no state income tax and a diverse workforce.

There is never a shortage of activities or events, with summers packed with outdoor festivals and concerts, including free concerts at the Levitt at the Falls outdoor music venue.

Still, many also enjoy the city’s nearly 30 miles of bike trails and parks, including the namesake of the city, the beautiful waterfalls of the Big Sioux River! Yes, winters can be challenging, but it does not mean people hibernate. Colder temperatures provide plenty of outdoor and indoor activities all winter long. From parades like the annual Parade of Lights down Phillips Avenue to outdoor ice skating parks, life does not slow down in the winter in Sioux Falls.

The city is home to a 12,000-seat arena that is continually hosting major events and entertainment acts, ranging from the Professional Bull Riders, college and semi-professional hockey, indoor football, to concerts with names like Paul McCartney, Garth Brooks, and Elton John.

The city is also home to a new indoor aquatic center, an indoor ice-skating facility, a basketball arena, and an indoor tennis complex. Multiple award-winning golf courses, both public and private, surround the city, offering a relaxing and challenging day on the links

Culinary appetites never need to look far from being satiated, as there is no shortage of places to eat. Not only is Sioux Falls home to many familiar restaurant chains, but it’s also known for many great locally owned, nationally recognized restaurants and restaurateurs. For those looking for a quick weekend getaway, nothing to fear. You can drive to Omaha in three hours, Minneapolis in four, and the Black Hills in five. Since Sioux Falls is centrally located in the Midwest, direct and connecting flights to almost anywhere in the United States are often less than a few hours in length.

Dakota News Now is an award-winning television operation serving viewers in the eastern half of South Dakota as well as portions of southwest Minnesota and northwest Iowa. The stations operate from a relatively new studio in downtown Sioux Falls, branding all stations under the Dakota News Now umbrella. The facilities put Dakota News Now on the cutting edge of television and news gathering technology, making it one of the most state-of-the-art television stations in the market and the region. The Dakota News Now team produces 36 hours of news each week.

Some of our employees have been here for more than 25 years. For others, this is their first job out of college. It’s a great mix that gives us different perspectives while covering the news and assisting local clientele in achieving their marketing goals.

Learn more about Dakota News Now & Sioux Falls here: https://www.dakotanewsnow.com/page/ksfykdlt-careers/

About KOLN/KSNB:

KOLN is the CBS affiliate in the Lincoln, Hastings, Kearney market. Located in the thriving capital city of Lincoln, the station is the area`s dominant news leader, with number one newscasts in every daypart. The 1011NOW news brand is well-known throughout the region as a trusted source for quality news, weather, and sports coverage.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you the kind of person who sees a complex technical glitch and thinks, "Challenge accepted"? Do you dream in gigabytes and broadcast frequencies, and thrive on the adrenaline of keeping a 24/7 operation running flawlessly? We’re looking for a Media Systems Engineer to be the technological heartbeat of our central and western Nebraska stations. Whether it’s maintaining massive tower sites or ensuring a live stream hits every phone in the state, you’ll be the wizard behind the curtain, making sure our communities stay connected and informed.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

• Master the infrastructure: Maintain and evolve broadcast systems across Hastings, Grand Island, North Platte, and every tower site in between (yes, you’re the guardian of the signal!).
• Drive technical innovation: Don’t just fix things—improve them. You’ll execute a strategic plan to keep our technology modern, digital-first, and ahead of the curve.
• Support the storytellers: Provide expert engineering for studios, post-editing suites, and field production teams so they can focus on telling great stories.
• Own the live moment: Ensure every piece of gear is ready for the spotlight during live broadcasts and streaming events, documenting and crushing technical hurdles before they hit the air.
• Stay compliant and sharp: Keep us in the good graces of the FCC and FAA by managing all regulatory requirements for our tech components.
• Monitor the pulse: Keep a close eye on multiple air channels and transmitters, ensuring our "on-air" product is always high-quality and high-definition.
• Bridge the IT gap: Use your deep knowledge of server and desktop operating systems to keep our newsgathering, weather, and graphic systems running at peak performance.

Qualifications/Requirements:

• The Foundation: An engineering or electronics degree (or equivalent experience) plus 2-3 years in the broadcast or professional tech world.
• Digital Fluency: You’re a pro with IP-based video/audio transport and streaming technologies—you know the future of media is multi-platform.
• Cool Under Pressure: When the "On Air" light is red, and something breaks, you’re the calmest person in the room.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you the kind of person who sees a storm on the horizon and immediately starts thinking about how to explain the "why" and "when" to your neighbors? WHSV is looking for a high-energy Meteorologist to join our award-winning First Alert Weather Team in the beautiful Shenandoah Valley. This isn't just about reading the models; it’s about owning the weather narrative across every platform—from our weekend evening newscasts to the palm of our viewers' hands.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

- Live the "First Alert" brand: Embody our commitment to being the most trusted, local weather source in the Valley and our West Virginia viewing area with urgency and accuracy. We keep our viewers updated every step of the way, giving them the information they need to plan days in advance.
- Own the weekend evenings: Create and deliver compelling, conversational on-air forecasts for our 6:00 p.m. and 11:00 p.m. newscasts that keep viewers informed and safe.
- Drive digital weather: Don't just wait for the linear hit; engage our audience on social media, our weather app, and streaming platforms throughout the week.
- Tell the weather story: Spend your weekdays digging into weather-related content, whether that’s field reporting on local climate impacts or creating innovative graphics that make complex science simple.
- Collaborate and innovate: Work closely with our news and digital teams to ensure our weather coverage is seamless, multi-platform, and always ahead of the curve.
- Learn from the best: You'll get the chance to receive feedback from our award-winning weather team, which has 20 years of combined experience in the industry.

Qualifications/Requirements:

- A degree in meteorology and a background in broadcast communications/journalism preferred
- Unstoppable motivation: You have a genuine passion for meteorology and a relentless drive to communicate the forecast wherever the audience is.
- A digital-first mindset: You’re as comfortable going live or posting on social media as you are in front of the studio camera.
- Creative storytelling: You don't just show maps; you tell a story that connects the data to people's lives (and you’ve got the ideas to prove it!).
- Independence and teamwork: You can crush a solo shift but also thrive in a collaborative "weather center" environment. You bring a positive attitude to our team's strong work culture.
- Technical chops: You know your way around weather graphics systems and are ready to push the limits of what they can do.
- Urgency and calm: You handle severe weather with the perfect mix of "get-to-the-basement" urgency and "I’ve got this" authority while being able to make decisions quickly.
- Ability to work all shifts (we have newscasts beginning at 5:00 a.m. and going until 11:30 p.m.; must be able to work all those hours/shifts when needed), including during snow and severe weather events.

Ready to join the First Alert Weather Team and make your mark in the Valley? Let’s talk.

KALB-TV is the #1 most-watched television station in Central Louisiana. KALB-TV includes the powerhouse NBC that has dominated the market for more than 70 years, CBS, and the CW.

Are you a natural storyteller who thrives both in the field and at the desk? KALB, the dominant news leader in Alexandria, Louisiana, is searching for a dynamic MMJ/Anchor. We aren't looking for a "teleprompter reader" — we want an enterprising journalist who can pitch, shoot, and edit compelling enterprise stories, take command of the anchor desk, and connect with Central Louisiana across broadcast, digital, and social platforms.

Think local news is still just a 6:00 and 10:00 broadcast? Think again. We are building the future of local storytelling at KSNB Local4, and we need an agile, digital-first journalist ready to command both the field and the screen. You won't just report packages; you will be part of our multi-platform newsroom, stepping directly onto our OTT streaming desk to assist in live coverage, break news in real time, and connect with audiences wherever they watch. Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

• Lead digital-first publishing: Push breaking updates, live streams, and custom video content straight to mobile, web, and social feeds before the evening broadcast even airs.
• Master modern newsroom tools: Shoot on ENG gear and edit under tight deadlines using industry workflows like ENPS and Edius without sacrificing speed or accuracy.
• Engage the community: Build trusted sources across Hastings and surrounding towns, representing Local4 at community events and listening directly to our viewers

• Multi-platform screen presence: Comfort and charisma whether anchoring live on a streaming desk, seated at a traditional anchor set, or going live from the field on a smartphone.
• Newsroom experience: College degree in journalism (or equivalent professional experience) with proven newsroom chops in shooting, writing, and editing on deadline.
• Streaming and digital savvy: An intuitive understanding of what hooks digital audiences on OTT channels, connected TVs, and social video platforms.
• Technical fluency: Hands-on operational experience with camera gear, non-linear editing (Edius), and newsroom production software (ENPS).
• Speed and composure: The ability to go live on the fly during breaking news, synthesize fast-moving facts, and keep viewers informed with clarity and calm.
• Community connection: A collaborative attitude, strong ethics, and genuine curiosity about the people and stories of Central Nebraska.
• Valid driver's license: Clean driving record and the flexibility required for the daily rhythm of breaking news.

Do you seek an adventurous and important community role, a position unlike any other local broadcast/digital Multimedia Journalist in the country? Alaska's News Source is seeking an MMJ who is ready to immerse themselves in the nation's largest statewide community, pitch/shoot/edit/present compelling stories daily, and travel on assignment to report on breaking news events and other critical stories that impact our viewers across Alaska. The shift for this position includes nights and/or weekends.

Duties/Responsibilities will include (but not be limited to):

* Research, gather, write, and report news stories for on-air and online in the most accurate, appealing, timely, and creative way using all sources
* Report "live" on the scene, especially during breaking news
* Make regular beat checks
* Conduct interviews in the field and on-set
* Develop and maintain sources of information and knowledge about assignments
* Demonstrate sound news judgment, collaborate with others to present the story

* Use knowledge of appropriate field lighting to enhance overall news presentation. Critique, feedback, and training are part of the job
* Communicate regularly with the digital staff and other appropriate staff members during breaking news
* Follow clothing and appearance guidelines
* Must be a visual storyteller; perform creative stand-ups and explanatory live shorts
* Evenings, weekends, and holiday work are expected
* Perform other job-related duties as assigned

Qualifications/Requirements:

* Bachelor's degree in journalism or other related field
* On-Air experience in the broadcast news industry preferred
* Experience with broadcast/digital cameras, newsroom software (ENPS), and non-linear editing (Grass Valley Edius experience a plus)
* Be able to write in a clear, concise, conversational manner
* Knowledge of AP Stylebook
* Must possess excellent interview and conversational writing skills
* Excellent live reporting skills and strong on-camera presentation skills required
* Basic computer knowledge including newsroom software (such as ENPS), Microsoft applications and internet use

About KATC:

KATC-TV is Acadiana's trusted source for local news, weather, and sports. Job Summary/Description:

KATC-TV is looking for a Multimedia Journalist who can find compelling local stories, develop sources, and deliver strong journalism across broadcast and digital platforms. The ideal candidate is an energetic storyteller who can shoot, write, edit, and report independently while also responding quickly to breaking news and live coverage.

* Maintain high standards of accuracy, fairness, ethics and professionalism.

Qualifications/Requirements:

* Strong writing, reporting, shooting and video-editing skills.
* Demonstrated ability to develop sources and generate original story ideas.
* Strong live reporting and on-camera presentation skills.
* Ability to work independently in the field and make sound editorial decisions under deadline pressure.
* Ability to cover breaking news and adapt quickly as stories develop.
* Strong understanding of digital journalism, social media and multiplatform storytelling.

About KEYC:

Since 1960, KEYC-TV/KMNF-CD have succeeded with a culture that values skills, encourages creativity, and fosters professional growth.

Enjoy all four seasons in the booming Greater Mankato metropolitan area. The friendly, welcoming region is a happy mix of city and country living. We maintain the most highly visited social media sites in southern Minnesota.

Job Summary/Description:  

KEYC News Now is searching for that rare talent who can not only chase down a story but also command the anchor desk and produce a killer newscast. If you're a storyteller who thrives on urgency, connects deeply with people, and sees every platform—from broadcast to TikTok—as an opportunity to inform, then get ready to make your mark. We're talking about owning the news from concept to air (and online!), delivering content that truly resonates with our viewers.

Ready to report and help anchor for a station that truly impacts its community? We want to hear from you!

Duties/Responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

What You'll Do:
* Create compelling content: Report, shoot, write, voice, and edit daily news stories for both television and our buzzing digital platforms, making sure every piece is relevant and engaging.
* Lead the newscast: Anchor and produce dynamic newscasts as needed, bringing energy and authority to every broadcast and ensuring our viewers are informed and connected.
* Own the story cycle: From generating 3+ fresh story ideas daily to breaking news live on location, you'll be the force driving our local coverage.
* Drive digital engagement: Master social media and online news production, updating our website and social accounts throughout the day with urgency and immediacy.
* Connect with the community: Build authentic relationships and truly "think like a viewer," delivering news that matters most to the local community.
* Collaborate seamlessly: Work hand-in-hand with the news team, bringing a great attitude and leadership skills to every shift, even when schedules shift.
* Uphold our standards: Adhere to the highest standards of news judgment, ethics, and station branding in all content you create.

Qualifications/Requirements:

What You Bring:
* A Bachelor's Degree in Communications, Journalism, English, or a related field—you've got the foundation.
* Proven broadcast journalism experience: You know the rhythm of a newsroom and the demands of live television.
* Exceptional writing and verbal communication skills: You craft balanced, clear, and concise copy that grabs attention.
* A true digital-first mindset: You don't just understand digital/social media strategy; you execute it with urgency.
* Sharp news judgment and unwavering ethics: You know what's important and how to tell the story responsibly.
* The grit to go get the story: Able to carry 35-45 pounds of ENG equipment and ready to cover anything from features to breaking news.
* Impeccable time management skills and the ability to thrive under tight deadlines.
* Integrity, accountability, and a team-player attitude—you make the newsroom better.
* A valid driver's license and a clean driving record—you're ready to hit the road when news breaks.
* Flexibility to work various schedules, as news doesn't always keep regular hours.

Why You'll Love It Here:
* Multi-faceted impact: This isn't just a job; it's a chance to truly shape local news across all platforms.
* Community connection: You'll be at the forefront of stories that matter, building real relationships within the KEYC News Now community.
* Dynamic environment: One day you're digging deep into a feature, the next you're live on breaking news. Every day is different, and every day is exciting.
* Competitive compensation: We offer a salary/wage of $20-23 per hour (DOE), reflecting your valuable experience and versatility.
* Be part of the future: Gray Media is committed to innovation, and you'll be a key player in how we deliver news in a digital-first world.

About WLOX:

Ready to join a newsroom that aggressively uncovers the truth? For over six decades, WLOX has been South Mississippi's undisputed news leader, proudly holding down both the #1 and #2 spots as the region's ABC and CBS affiliate. We're building the future of local news with a sharp focus on impactful investigative journalism and leading the charge in digital storytelling across every platform. Here, you'll be part of an award-winning team committed to serving our community while shaping the evolving landscape of media.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you wired to uncover stories that truly matter? Do you thrive at the intersection of local news and digital speed? WLOX is on the hunt for a Multimedia Journalist who can bring their A-game to every platform, from broadcast to the web, and into the heart of our community. If you're a self-starter with a nose for news and a passion for connecting with audiences wherever they are, then this is your opportunity to make a significant impact!

Duties/Responsibilities will include (but not be limited to):

- Craft compelling stories: Write, shoot, and edit engaging news stories for TV, web, and all our digital platforms, ensuring our community is always informed and connected.
- Be the first on the scene: Report live and react instantly to breaking news, severe weather, or major community events, bringing real-time updates across every screen and channel.
- Unearth vital narratives: Research, pitch, and develop impactful news stories that resonate deeply with our local audience and shed light on important issues.
- Own the moment: Navigate fast-paced, high-pressure environments and make sound, split-second decisions during live broadcasts, maintaining composure and confidence under pressure.
- Step up to the anchor desk: Seize opportunities to fill in as an anchor, showcasing your versatility and leadership in front of the camera (based on your interest and ability, of course!).

Qualifications/Requirements:

- A degree in Communications/Journalism or an equivalent passion-driven, real-world experience (we value grit and smarts!).
- An insatiable curiosity for current events and what truly matters to our local community.
- Digital fluency: You're not just comfortable with social media; you wield it as a powerful newsgathering, storytelling, and audience engagement tool.
- Team player & solo star: You thrive in collaborative environments but are equally effective working independently, especially when deadlines are tight.
- Physical readiness: Able to confidently lift and carry essential equipment, including your tripod, camera, and lights—because great stories don't always happen in a studio!
- A clean driving record and a valid driver's license (essential for covering stories across our community).
- Unshakeable news judgment: You know a story when you see it, how to tell it responsibly, and why it matters to our viewers.
- Urgency with empathy: You're driven to get the story first, but always with respect, understanding, and a commitment to accuracy.

WTOK-TV is a trusted ABC network station with a history of serving the communities of eastern Mississippi and Western Alabama with top-rated news, weather, and sports. We also offer syndicated programming on the CW, myTOK, Gulf Coast Sports & Entertainment Network, and Telemundo Mississippi network. We take pride in serving our viewers, our community, and our advertisers for 71 years.

Our mission is to be engaged with the community and promote civic and economic development with a focus on improving the lives of our viewers. We use cutting-edge technology to provide accurate and timely news information on television and digital platforms.

Job Summary/Description:

WTOK-TV is seeking a multi-talented, highly motivated hybrid Weekend Anchor / Producer / Multimedia Journalist to join our news team. This unique role is perfect for a storyteller who thrives in every stage of news production—from digging up and reporting stories on weekdays to anchoring and producing newscasts on weekends. This position also carries a heavy digital focus, contributing directly to our digital platforms to drive traffic, user sessions, and viewer engagement.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

- Produce & Anchor: Own the weekend newscasts. You will be responsible for stacking, writing, and producing high-quality broadcast rundowns, and anchoring the live broadcasts.
- Digital Ownership: Manage and update our digital news platforms (web, app, and social media) during the weekend shifts to keep our audience informed.
- Content & Trend Monitoring: Actively monitor local social media pages, community groups, and digital platforms on the weekends to catch breaking news, source local story ideas, and gather user-generated content to enrich our coverage.
- MMJ Reporting: Find, pitch, shoot, write, and edit compelling local stories. You will be expected to turn high-quality, accurate stories daily.
- Digital Content Integration: Turn your broadcast stories into digital assets by writing web stories and publishing active social media updates.
- Platform Consistency: You will create and publish engaging post assets (e.g., a 15–25s quick-take vertical video, a photo with bullet points, or a text graphic) across WTOK's social media platforms simultaneously.
- Story Tiering: Adhere to newsroom story tiering workflows (Tier 1 vs. Tier 2) to maximize web users, pageviews, and video plays.

Qualifications/Requirements:

- A degree in Journalism, Communications, or a related field is preferred.
- Experience in shooting, writing, and non-linear editing (Edius, Premiere, etc.).
- Strong on-camera presence, vocal delivery, and teleprompter reading skills.
- Ability to write engaging, concise broadcast copy and AP-style web articles.
- Experience with digital Content Management Systems (CMS) and professional social media publishing.
- Excellent time-management skills and the ability to work independently under tight deadlines.
- Demonstrated ability to work independently as a self-starter and collaboratively within a tight-knit newsroom team.
- A valid driver's license with a clean driving record.

job.title: NEWS ANCHOR (EVENING) - WEAU
job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. The portfolio includes 80 markets with the top-rated television station and 100 markets with the first and/or second highest-rated television station in average all-day ratings across 116 of such markets that were measured by Nielsen in 2025. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About WEAU:

WEAU News is the dominant news organization serving western Wisconsin. We are committed to earning and keeping the public’s trust through accurate, transparent, and unbiased journalism. We deliver essential local news across every platform our audience uses — digital, mobile, streaming, and broadcast — and we take that responsibility seriously.

Job Summary/Description:  

WEAU News is hiring an evening anchor to help lead a digital-first newsroom serving Eau Claire, La Crosse, and western Wisconsin. Our goal is to be the premier multi-platform news organization in the state, putting streaming, on-demand video, mobile alerts, and social media at the center of how our audience connects with us.
The most valuable trait for this role is ownership. When news breaks, we expect our anchors to ensure WEAU owns the story with speed, accuracy, and strong news judgment across all platforms. This is a high-visibility role that demands excellence, adaptability, and unwavering editorial integrity.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Storytelling & Digital Execution (Primary Focus):
• Write for Different Platforms: Write clear, accurate, and engaging copy adapted specifically for each platform, seamlessly shifting styles between broadcast scripts, in-depth web articles, quick-strike push alerts, and social media.
• Digital-First Storytelling: Commit to immediate digital delivery, including creating platform-native vertical videos, mobile-optimized clips, and real-time text updates during active news events.
• Audience-Focused Engagement: Publish stories, video clips, and breaking developments to the station website, app, and social channels with compelling, attention-getting framing that avoids clickbait and maintains our high standards of trust.
• Search Engine Optimization (SEO): Apply strong SEO best practices, including keyword optimization, clear headline writing, and metadata tagging to maximize the reach and searchability of our local reporting.
• Collaboration: Work closely with digital producers and editors to ensure accuracy, speed, and editorial integrity online.

On-Air & Streaming Performance:
• Anchor afternoon and evening newscasts, breaking news cut-ins, and streaming segments with consistent quality.
• Conduct compelling, live interviews with newsmakers, experts, and community leaders across both broadcast and digital platforms.
• Pivot seamlessly during breaking news, delivering timely updates for streaming, mobile alerts, and social media feeds.
• Maintain a professional, credible, and engaging on-air presence tailored to each distribution platform.

Newscast Production & Story Development:
• Collaborate with producers on story selection, rundown stacking, and digital-first coverage plans.
• Pitch and develop unique local stories that resonate in mobile, social, and streaming environments.
• Participate in daily editorial meetings with a sharp focus on multiplatform distribution.
• Review and approve copy, ensuring all scripts meet strict standards for accuracy, clarity, and digital optimization.
• Produce newscasts and assist with video editing when necessary.
• Contribute original reporting, including special in-field coverage and digital-exclusive projects.

Community Engagement:
• Engage with viewers across on-air, streaming, social media, and in-person channels.
• Represent WEAU at community events, station partnerships, and public appearances.
• Monitor and respond to audience feedback to help shape coverage based on local needs and emerging digital trends.

Skills & Competencies:
• Digital Audience Engagement: Skilled at writing high-performance, attention-getting headlines and social copy that drive traffic while strictly upholding traditional editorial standards and avoiding sensationalism or clickbait.
• Multiplatform Writing: Expert ability to pivot writing styles, structure, and length to fit the specific constraints and audience expectations of web, social, mobile app, and broadcast.
• Digital Video Strategy: Fluent in the use and optimization of digital video, including horizontal streaming formats, platform-native vertical video, and social teasers.
• Search Engine Optimization (SEO): Strong understanding of search trends, Google News ranking factors, and keyword placement to increase the digital footprint of local stories.
• Leadership: Sets the tone for digital-forward coverage and positively influences newsroom culture.
• Adaptability: Thrives under the pressure of breaking news, rapid updates, and shifting multiplatform demands.
• Collaboration: Works seamlessly with producers, reporters, photojournalists, and digital teams.
• News Judgment: Makes sound, ethical editorial decisions with strong digital instincts.
• Integrity: Upholds strict ethical standards, never compromising accuracy for speed.
• Resilience: Successfully manages a demanding evening schedule and the fast pace of live television and digital news.

Qualifications/Requirements:

• Previous anchoring and/or reporting experience in a professional, multiplatform newsroom.
• Proven track record of digital content creation, including writing for the web and producing native social media videos.
• Strong writing and copy-editing skills with a complete mastery of AP Style.
• Demonstrated experience with SEO best practices and digital analytics tools.
• Excellent on-camera presence with a natural, conversational, and authoritative delivery.
• Bachelor’s degree in journalism, communications, or a related field.
• Deep knowledge of journalism ethics, public records laws, and source verification practices.
• A valid driver’s license and a clean driving record.

job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. The portfolio includes 80 markets with the top-rated television station and 100 markets with the first- and/or second-highest-rated television station in average all-day ratings across 116 of such markets that were measured by Nielsen in 2025. We also own the largest Telemundo Affiliate group with 46 markets and Gray Digital Media, a full-service digital agency offering national and local clients digital marketing strategies with the most advanced digital products and services. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About KOLN/KSNB:

Think local news is still just a 6:00 and 10:00 broadcast? Think again. We are building the future of local storytelling at KSNB Local4, and we need an agile, digital-first journalist ready to command both the field and the screen. You won't just report packages; you will be part of our multi-platform newsroom, stepping directly onto our OTT streaming desk to assist in live coverage, break news in real time, and connect with audiences wherever they watch. If you want a role that blends aggressive reporting with cutting-edge digital streaming and broadcast anchoring, let's talk.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you a versatile storyteller ready to own the anchor desk and lead the digital conversation? KSNB Local4 is looking for a high-energy Weekend Anchor/Streaming Anchor/MMJ to anchor our weekend broadcasts, drive live OTT streaming coverage, and report high-impact stories across Central Nebraska. Join a digital-first newsroom where you can sharpen your anchoring skills and connect with audiences across every platform.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

• Step behind the broadcast desk: Serve as a weekend anchor & producer for scheduled linear newscasts, writing conversational copy and collaborating with producers to execute tight, engaging broadcasts.
• Anchor on the OTT streaming desk: Assist our live digital desk for streaming newscasts, breaking news cut-ins, and extended deep-dive coverage tailored specifically for OTT platforms and connected TV apps.
• Own enterprise reporting: Pitch, shoot, write, and edit high-impact local stories across Central Nebraska that prioritize truth, community context, and strong character-driven visuals.
• Lead digital-first publishing: Push breaking updates, live streams, and custom video content straight to mobile, web, and social feeds before the evening broadcast even airs.
• Master modern newsroom tools: Shoot on ENG gear and edit under tight deadlines using industry workflows like ENPS and Edius without sacrificing speed or accuracy.

Qualifications/Requirements:

• Multi-platform screen presence: Comfort and charisma whether anchoring live on a streaming desk, seated at a traditional anchor set, or going live from the field on a smartphone.
• Newsroom experience: College degree in journalism (or equivalent professional experience) with proven newsroom chops in shooting, writing, and editing on deadline.

Our CBS station is highly competitive in news and has top-rated sports and prime content. Our digital reach is also best-in-market—Azfamily.com leads the market in multi-platform unique users and is home to Arizona’s Family Originals (long-form programs, documentaries, docuseries, and podcasts, including True Crime Arizona, nearing 2M downloads). Arizona’s Family Sports features premier properties, including the Arizona Cardinals, Phoenix Suns, Phoenix Mercury, Phoenix Rising, and AIA state championships.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you the kind of person who actually loves the thrill of morning news? Do you thrive on the adrenaline of uncovering exclusive content and the challenge of bringing it to life with demonstrative, high-energy live shots? We’re looking for a Weekend Morning Anchor/Reporter who doesn’t just read the news—you own it. Whether you’re leading the desk on Saturday & Sunday mornings or reporting live from the field with a "show-don't-tell" mindset, you’ll be the face of the best morning show in Arizona. This isn't just a seat at a desk; it’s a multi-platform partnership where you’ll also have the chance to step into the spotlight as a fill-in host for our streaming shows.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

What You'll Do:
• Lead the morning conversation: Anchor weekend morning newscasts with energy, authenticity, and a conversational style that makes viewers feel like they’re waking up with a friend.
• Master the live shot: Deliver demonstrative, active live reports that take the audience to the heart of the story—no "standing in front of a building" here!
• Own the digital space: Engage our audience across all platforms, from social media updates to hosting live Q&A segments and filling in on our streaming shows.
• Drive the editorial engine: Be a newsroom leader who pitches original, promotable story ideas and collaborates deeply with producers to craft a winning show.
• Connect with the community: Get out from behind the desk to build real relationships with news sources and represent the station at local events (yes, you’ll be a local celebrity!).
• Craft compelling narratives: Research, write, and edit in-depth content, including hard news, features, and mini-documentaries that matter to Arizona.

What You Bring:
• A "Morning Person" mindset: You bring the energy even before the sun comes up (and you know how to make it look easy).
• Killer live skills: You’re a pro at field anchoring and can handle the unpredictability of live TV with authority and calm.
• Digital-first curiosity: You’re constantly engaged in the news cycle and know how to pivot your storytelling for streaming and social platforms.
• Community-driven hustle: You’re a natural connector who is always looking for the next great story and isn't afraid to pick up the phone.
• Strong editorial judgment: You have a sharp eye for what’s "promotable" and the writing skills to make every script sing.
• Technical scrappiness: You can edit and rewrite copy on the fly and aren't afraid to get your hands dirty in the production process.
• Urgency and empathy: You understand the weight of the stories you tell and deliver them with the respect and speed they deserve.

Why You'll Love It Here:
• The best team in the desert: You’ll be joining Arizona’s top-rated morning news team in a culture that values innovation and collaboration.
• Multi-platform growth: Between anchoring, reporting, and streaming host opportunities, your career path here is wide open.
• Real community impact: You’ll be telling the stories that shape the lives of our viewers every single day.
• Innovation-led environment: Gray Media is leading the future of local news—you’ll have the tools and the freedom to try new things.

Ready to wake up Arizona and make your mark? Let’s create something amazing together.

Qualifications/Requirements:

- Five years of general on-air news reporting experience. Journalistic skills, editorial judgment with knowledge of editing and photography skills, or equivalent work experience
- Bachelor’s degree in Journalism or Communications preferred

Specific Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
- Ability to work under pressure, adapt to change, meet deadlines, work well as a team and independently.
- Exceptional communication skills and excellent knowledge of current events

Job Summary/Description:

WSAW/WZAW, the Gray Media-owned CBS and FOX affiliate in north-central Wisconsin, has an immediate opening for a weekday News Producer who is excited to work on award-winning newscasts. Our producers create, coordinate, and showcase content that appears on-air and online. You will also be cross-trained to produce content for all of WSAW's digital platforms, including our website and streaming desk. You must be an innovator who can see the big picture, as well as someone who is a stickler for the details, writing conversationally (for TV) and with AP Style (for digital).

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- You will report to and work closely with the News Director and Executive Producer in shaping and ensuring the execution of our digital-first strategy on all platforms (website, social media, our news and weather apps, Digital Streaming Desk, and television).
- Act with urgency and immediacy. Be first and best with the story. You are expected to research and write copy daily as new information is learned and to share it on all platforms, including television, WSAW.com, and social media.
- Identify opportunities for live streaming on our website, getting live and user-generated content to our TV newscasts and streaming desk, and sending push alerts to extend the reach of our work.
- Ensure story selection and placement in your rundown fit journalistic/editorial standards, as well as WSAW/WZAW's brand pillars.
- Understand our DMA, key target audiences, and where they live.
- Produce engaging and error-free work. Pay attention to the details!
- Communicate and collaborate professionally and respectfully with your coworkers to enhance the viewer experience and understanding of content.

Qualifications/Requirements:

- We prefer a college degree in journalism or a related field.

- Strong research skills, ability to employ critical thinking skills to dig and go "beyond the press release" and confirm incoming news tips via email or social media.
- Strong time management skills are also essential. Must be able to work quickly while maintaining accuracy in your work. Must have the ability to multitask and maintain composure, especially while under deadline pressure and during breaking news.
- A strong candidate will have an established and responsible presence on digital platforms, including social media.
- Working knowledge of CMS and Digital platforms, including ARC, Social News Desk, and Google QuickPlay. Photoshop experience is a plus.
- Understanding of and adherence to AP Style.
- Strong communication skills (written and verbal).
- Flexibility to work different hours and shifts (for example, to cover a coworker's time off or to assist in breaking news and specialized coverage).
- Must have a clean driving record and be able to carry 35+ pounds of gear.

With Mississippi's mild climate, outdoor recreation is a way of life, supported by an extensive network of walking, running, and cycling trails throughout the metro. And for quick getaways, Jackson is just a short drive from beautiful Gulf Coast beaches and all the fun you can handle in New Orleans.

Sports fans will feel right at home here. Our DMA includes two SWAC programs, Jackson State and Alcorn State, and fans of SEC athletics are near four powerhouse schools: Ole Miss, Mississippi State, Alabama, and LSU. Our CBS station is highly competitive in news and has top-rated sports and prime content. Our digital reach is also best-in-market—Azfamily.com leads the market in multi-platform unique users and is home to Arizona’s Family Originals (long-form programs, documentaries, docuseries, and podcasts, including True Crime Arizona, nearing 2M downloads). Arizona’s Family Sports features premier properties, including the Arizona Cardinals, Phoenix Suns, Phoenix Mercury, Phoenix Rising, and AIA state championships.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you a newsroom adrenaline junkie who lives for the rush of a breaking story? Arizona’s Family is looking for a dynamic, high-energy Producer who doesn't just build rundowns—they craft experiences. We’re looking for a risk-taker who can think critically under pressure and thrives in a fast-paced environment where resources are plentiful and the expectations are high. If you’re a self-starter who knows how to pivot on a dime and loves the challenge of making every newscast feel like "must-see" TV and digital content, we want to talk to you.

• Craft compelling newscasts: Build and produce high-impact newscasts that align with our brand and meet our high newsroom standards for quality and accuracy.
• Own the "Big Story": Use your solid news judgment to identify what matters most to our Phoenix audience and showcase it with creativity and urgency.

• Lead with immediacy: Work with a relentless sense of urgency, making quick, decisive calls to keep our coverage first and best.
• Collaborate like a pro: Partner with reporters, anchors, and photographers to execute a cohesive vision for every show, every day.

Why You’ll Love It Here:
• Resources Galore: We give you the tools, the technology, and the team you need to do the best work of your career.
• A Culture of Innovation: We don’t just do things the way they’ve always been done; we encourage you to experiment and push boundaries.
• Impactful Work: You’ll be part of a legendary newsroom that is deeply rooted in the Arizona community and committed to telling stories that matter.
• Growth Opportunities: At Gray Media, we invest in our people, providing the mentorship and path you need to level up.

Qualifications:

What You Bring:
• The Experience: You have at least two years of line producing experience, preferably in a competitive market where the stakes are high.
• Killer Writing Skills: You write for the ear and the eye, crafting scripts that are conversational, urgent, and editorially sound.
• Digital-First Mindset: You understand that our audience lives on their phones as much as their TVs, and you know how to reach them there.
• Critical Thinking: You don’t just follow a plan; you analyze, adapt, and take calculated risks to make the coverage better.
• Decisiveness: You can make big calls in the heat of the moment without breaking a sweat.
• The Credentials: A Bachelor’s degree in Journalism, Broadcasting, or equivalent real-world experience that has prepared you for the grind.
• Team Spirit: You thrive in a collaborative culture where we win as a team and support each other through the chaos of breaking news.

Home to 3TV, CBS 5, and Arizona’s Family Sports, Arizona’s Family produces 100+ hours of local news and programming every week. 3TV is #1 in Arizona and one of the strongest independent stations in the country. Our CBS station is highly competitive in news and has top-rated sports and prime content. Our digital reach is also best-in-market—Azfamily.com leads the market in multi-platform unique users and is home to Arizona’s Family Originals (long-form programs, documentaries, docuseries, and podcasts, including True Crime Arizona, nearing 2M downloads). Arizona’s Family Sports features premier properties, including the Arizona Cardinals, Phoenix Suns, Phoenix Mercury, Phoenix Rising, and AIA state championships.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you a storyteller who thrives on the pulse of a breaking story? Do you have the grit to uncover enterprise pieces that no one else is talking about? Arizona’s Family—the undisputed news and streaming leader in Phoenix and across the entire state—is looking for a Reporter who doesn’t just cover the news but owns it. Whether you’re live on the scene or crafting a mini-doc for our streaming platforms, you’ll have the resources of a powerhouse newsroom and a culture that’s built to help you grow. Ready to tell stories that matter to all of Arizona?

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

What You’ll Do:
• Own the story: Research, pitch, and execute high-impact reporting assignments across all platforms—from the evening news to our 24/7 streaming channels.
• Drive digital engagement: Craft compelling content for web and social media that meets our audience where they are (because news doesn’t just happen on a TV screen).
• Master the live shot: Deliver energetic, authoritative reporting from the field or the studio, with the versatility to step behind the anchor desk when the team needs you.
• Build your network: Develop and maintain deep connections with news sources to stay ahead of the curve and uncover exclusive enterprise content.
• Think big picture: Propose and produce everything from hard news follow-ups to features and mini-documentaries that showcase your range.
• Connect with Arizona: Represent the station at community events, becoming a trusted face for the families we serve across the state.

What You Bring:
• Killer storytelling skills: You know how to weave a narrative that keeps people watching, whether it’s a 30-second breaking update or a long-form feature.
• Multi-platform mindset: You’re as comfortable going live on Instagram as you are on the 6 PM news.
• Relentless curiosity: You’re a natural detective who loves digging for the "why" behind the "what."
• Urgency and accuracy: You thrive under the pressure of a deadline but never sacrifice the facts for speed.
• Collaborative spirit: You’re a team player who works seamlessly with producers, photographers, and the assignment desk to get the job done.
• Adaptability: You can pivot from a hard news investigation to a community feature without missing a beat.
• The basics: A solid track record in reporting, a clean driving record, and a degree in journalism or a related field.

Why You’ll Love It Here:
• A culture of growth: We don’t just hire talent; we invest in it. You’ll have the mentorship and resources to take your career to the next level.
• State-wide impact: As a leader in both Phoenix and statewide streaming, your work will reach and resonate with millions of Arizonans.
• Energizing environment: Our newsroom is fast-paced, supportive, and filled with people who are as passionate about the craft as you are.
• Innovation at the core: We are digital-first and future-focused, giving you the tools to experiment with new ways of storytelling.

Ready to make your mark in the desert? Let’s create something amazing together.

Qualifications/Requirements:

Education:
• Bachelor's Degree in Journalism, broadcasting, or equivalent work experience
• Local travel required

Experience:
• Two years of general on-air news reporting experience. Journalistic skills, editorial judgment with knowledge of editing and photography skills, or equivalent work experience

Specific Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
• Ability to work under pressure, adapt to change, meet deadlines, work well as a team and independently. Exceptional communication skills and excellent knowledge of current events

We're the NBC affiliate in the rapidly growing Wilmington market, serving New Hanover, Brunswick, Columbus, Pender, and Bladen counties that make up the beautiful coastal Cape Fear Region. WECT is the most accessible local news outlet in our market, with WECT.com, News & Weather apps, and streaming platforms. WECT is the dominant #1 station in the market.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you a visual storyteller who lives for the "wow" factor?

Do you thrive on the adrenaline of a breaking story and the satisfaction of a deep-dive community piece? We’re looking for a Multimedia Journalist (MMJ) who doesn't just report the news but owns it—across every screen.

Whether you’re crafting a lead for one of our on-air newscasts, going live on our streaming newscasts in the WECT Digital Studio, or engaging with our audience on social, you’ll be the heartbeat of the Cape Fear region.

If you’re a scrappy, digital-first journalist who wants to make a real impact in southeastern North Carolina, let’s talk.

Duties/Responsibilities will include (but not be limited to):

What You'll Do:
* Own the story: Manage and develop compelling content from initial concept to final publication across digital, social, and broadcast platforms.

* Respond with urgency: Jump into breaking news situations with authority and calm, keeping our community informed in real-time.
* Connect with the community: Build deep roots in the Cape Fear region, developing sources and uncovering the stories that truly matter to our neighbors.
*Step into the spotlight: Take advantage of potential anchoring opportunities to lead our coverage and connect directly with viewers.

What You Bring:
* A digital-first mindset: You understand that "news" happens 24/7, and you’re ready to feed the beast on social and streaming first.
* Killer storytelling skills: You know how to find the "human" element in every story and make it resonate with an audience.
* Technical chops: You’re a pro with a camera and an editing suite (and you’re not afraid to learn new tools as they emerge).
* Sharp news judgment: You know what’s important, what’s interesting, and how to tell the difference under pressure.
* A positive, "can-do" attitude: You’re a team player who lifts others up and thrives in a collaborative, fast-paced environment.
* Urgency and empathy: You care about the stories you tell and the people they affect, and you move fast to get them right.
* Flexibility: News doesn't follow a 9-to-5 schedule, and neither do you—you’re ready to go where the story takes you.

Qualifications/Requirements:

* Bachelor’s degree in journalism or related field preferred
* Strong writing skills (broadcast and print style)
* Experience with CMS/digital publishing platforms
* Experience with broadcast newsroom software such as ENPS
* Experience with video editing software (preferably Edius)

About KTVK/KPHO:

Home to CBS 5, 3TV, and Arizona’s Family Sports, Arizona's Family produces more than 100+ hours of local news and programming every week. CBS 5 is Arizona’s Most-Watched Television Station, driven by the power of CBS programming and sports, while 3TV is one of the strongest Independent television stations in the country, with its highly rated morning show, Good Morning Arizona. And the reach of Arizona's Family doesn't stop with linear television. Azfamily.com is the market's top performer in local multi-platform unique users. It is also home to Arizona's Family Originals. Our in-house original content production team works on several long-form programs, documentaries, docuseries, and original podcasts, including True Crime Arizona, which is nearing 2 million downloads.

Arizona’s Family Sports is home to the state’s premier sports franchises, including the Arizona Cardinals, Phoenix Suns, Phoenix Mercury, Phoenix Rising, and the Arizona Interscholastic Association high school state championships.

Job Summary/Description:

Can you tell a story that stops a scroll and commands a screen? Are you the kind of editor who lives for the adrenaline of a breaking news cycle and knows exactly how to turn raw footage into a powerful, high-impact narrative? Arizona’s Family is looking for a high-energy News Video Editor to join our team in Phoenix. We don’t just "cut tape" here—we craft visual experiences across broadcast, social, and digital platforms that empower Arizonans to live their best lives. If you’re a technical wizard with a creative soul and a "get it done" attitude, we want to see your reel.

Duties/Responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

What You'll Do:
• Craft compelling narratives: Edit high-impact video for daily news, investigative pieces, and special projects across all platforms (TV, web, and social).
• Manage the feed: Acquire and route video feeds from satellite, microwave, and backpacks, ensuring our field crews are always ready for air.
• Master the workflow: Work closely with the Chief News Editor to keep our content management and archive systems running like a well-oiled machine.
• Collaborate in real-time: Communicate with control rooms and field crews with urgency and precision to execute flawless live broadcasts.

What You Bring:
• Non-linear expertise: You’re a pro with modern editing software and understand the technical nuances of digital workflows.
• News-first mindset: You understand the urgency of a newsroom and can pivot from a breaking news clip to a long-form feature without missing a beat.
• Visual storytelling chops: You have an "eye" for great shots and an "ear" for perfect pacing that keeps viewers engaged.
• Digital fluency: You understand what makes a video go viral and how to optimize news content for different social platforms.
• Grace under pressure: You thrive in a fast-paced, high-stress environment and never miss a deadline (even when the clock is ticking down).
• Technical savvy: Familiarity with receiving feeds and managing assets in a content management system.
• Team-first attitude: You’re a communicator who lifts the team and is always looking for ways to improve the final product.

Why You'll Love It Here:
• Be a part of a powerhouse: Work for Arizona’s most-watched station and a leader in multi-platform innovation.
• Real community impact: Your work helps raise millions for local charities and powers movements like our Surprise Squad.
• Creative freedom: We value "scrappiness" and digital-first thinking—if you have a great idea for a social edit, we want to hear it.
• Growth opportunities: At Gray Media, we focus on the training and development of the best and brightest in the business.

Qualifications/Requirements:

• High School diploma or equivalent required. Bachelor’s degree in Broadcast Journalism/Production, Communications, or equivalent experience preferred
• Two years’ experience working as a news video editor in a television news environment preferred
• Strong understanding of non-linear editing
• Familiarity with receiving video feeds from satellite, microwave, backpack, and other transmission sources preferred
• Must be able to work accurately in a fast-paced, high-stress environment while consistently meeting deadlines
• Must possess an understanding of current journalism standards
• Strong technical and organizational skills

Ready to create something amazing with Arizona's Family? Let's talk.

WTVG is located in Northwestern Ohio. Our viewers and customers are extremely friendly and down-to-earth. We are a region of proud automotive workers home to several manufacturing plants. WWSB-TV is the ABC Television station serving Sarasota & Manatee Counties on the Suncoast of Southwest Florida. Beautiful, postcard-worthy views are bountiful, and so are the opportunities to enjoy the Florida lifestyle. Yes, the beaches are minutes away. Job Summary/Description:

ABC7 is searching for Newscast & Web Producers to help grow our digital-first newsroom. In addition to breaking and updating news on our website and social platforms, our producers thrive on building newscasts rich with story showcasing, targeted layering, and studio storytelling. You’ll embrace the concept of a hungry rundown, aggressively adding "happening now" live content and real-time social interaction.

ABC7 Sarasota is searching for our next Newscast & Web Producer in our digital-first newsroom. This is an amazing opportunity to learn and grow at a station that values a caring culture and competes for broadcast viewers & digital users in the Tampa Bay market.

Together, we break local news on our website, push it on social, and add context & emotion on television. Writing is at the core of the position, and you’ll be expected to seamlessly move between formats.

As a producer, you're expected to be more than a show-stacker. Our producers embrace advanced concepts of aggressive showcasing and hungry rundowns while boothing, adding "happening now" live content and real-time social interaction to newscasts.

Please note: Our newsroom runs 24-7. Expect this schedule to support our morning newscasts and website, including a mixture of weekdays and weekends (including holidays).

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

- Works with News Managers and Anchors to create and execute newscasts
- Partners with Digital Managers to write, post & update news stories on all platforms
- Participates in daypart editorial meetings, evaluating potential lead stories
- Selects, showcases & writes local, regional, national & international content for newscast presentations.
- Makes graphics, maps & lower thirds for all stories.
- Collaborates with directors for clean production to increase studio storytelling
- Writes copy for web and edits video for playback
- Edits video for newscasts
- Communicates with newsmakers and fields inquiries from viewers

- Two years of newscast producing experience helpful. Also needed:
- A positive attitude, willingness to learn, and ability to collaborate
- An internship in a commercial newsroom

You will host a digital talk show at least once a week featuring politicians from across South Dakota. You'll also be required to have a story ready to air on our broadcast channels every day. Job Summary/Description:

A Solutions Journalist at WIS joins a market-leading, award-winning newsroom to research, develop, and produce enterprise reporting that doesn’t stop at identifying what’s broken. This role is for an investigative-minded storyteller who understands evolving audience demand for journalism that holds power accountable while also rigorously examining responses—what’s being tried, what’s working (or not), for whom, and why.

Solutions journalism is not “good news.” It is tough, evidence-based reporting about responses to problems, grounded in:

• Evidence of effectiveness (data, results, credible evaluation)
• Insight (what can be learned and why it matters here)
• Limitations (tradeoffs, gaps, risks, what hasn’t worked, who’s left out)

The ideal candidate is an aggressive self-starter with strong public records skills, understands how to research, has a deep commitment to fairness and verification, and has the ability to produce compelling, high-impact stories across broadcast and digital platforms.

 Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

• Pitch, report, and produce enterprise/solutions stories that examine both the problem and credible responses, with clear evidence and limitations
• Shoot, write, edit, and publish multiplatform video (broadcast + digital) with high standards of verification and transparency
• Plan and execute short- and long-term projects on a shared enterprise calendar with newsroom stakeholders
• Use public records (FOIA), databases, documents, and data to uncover accountability and measure outcomes
• Develop sources and leads that reveal exclusive information and deepen reporting over time
• Interrogate claims made by institutions and organizations promoting “solutions,” testing what’s true and what’s overstated
• Center the audience with clear “why it matters” framing and practical context, without advocacy or cheerleading
• Present information fairly and accurately, including right-of-reply and strong attribution
• Collaborate closely with News leadership, digital, and producers to maximize reach, clarity, and follow-through reporting
• Build and maintain reporting systems (trackers, databases, timelines) to ensure stories evolve beyond a single hit
• Create strong digital components (explainers, FAQs, document viewers, short-form video, follow-ups) that extend impact and engagement

Qualifications/Requirements:

• 3-5 years’ experience in investigative, enterprise, or accountability reporting (solutions journalism experience is a plus)
• Refined ability to write for both broadcast & digital presentation
• Bachelor’s degree in journalism or related field
• Understanding of and adherence to AP Style for digital platforms and broadcasting writing for TV
• Ability to operate a field camera, editing, and lighting equipment
• Ability to lift/carry equipment ranging from 35-50 lbs
• Must have a valid driver’s license and a clean driving record
• Represent WIS professionally/responsibly in the community and newsroom, online and in person
• Must have the desire to win, reflect critically on your work, and apply feedback
• Demonstrated ability to report with rigor on evidence, impact, and limitations (data literacy and document reporting preferred)

job.title: Anchor Reporter
job.description:
WGAL News 8, the Hearst-owned NBC Affiliate serving the Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA market, has a rare opportunity to join our news team as an Anchor/Reporter. This market is rapidly growing, vibrant, and home to a wide variety of industries and cultures with a high quality of life and easy access to many major northeast cities. The Anchor/Reporter is someone who can bring the energy of live reporting to our anchor desk. In addition to credibility, poise, and personality; we’re looking for an anchor who isn’t afraid to head out into the field and break the big stories. Our next anchor/reporter will enterprise exclusives, tell compelling stories, and execute energetic live shots. We are looking for this market’s next leader who isn’t afraid to ask tough questions and will hold those in power accountable. Our anchors are newsroom leaders who help mentor and grow producers and reporters. Our anchors write and edit scripts with conversational communication in mind. We are looking for someone with an excitement about not only what we’re doing now as first informers, but what’s possible in the future. The ideal candidate excels not only in presenting on TV, but also excels on social media and with multiplatform content. If you are versatile and an enterprising self-starter who is fast, and efficient, works well under tight deadlines, can develop sources, and has excellent live reporting skills; this might be a great fit. This role reports to the News Director.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Delivers scripted and ad lib material with professionalism, personality, and purpose   

  • Works with and guides reporters and producers in newscast production

  • Plans, gathers and assembles stories on day-of news or special project assignments

  • Works with or without a photographer to gather and edit compelling video and captivating sound

  • Produces and posts regular vertical video and social media content. 

  • Coordinates with news managers and producers to develop stories that go beyond surface details, that accentuate unique enterprise angles, and have exclusive content

  • Develops a network of sources who provide tips, early access to information, and allow the reporter to break stories of significance.

  • Uses social media and multiplatform storytelling to connect with audience, enhance both the station and individual brand

  • Can juggle multiple stories and projects at once, demonstrates exceptional time-management skills by meeting all deadlines under extraordinary pressure.

  • An ability to summarize information into easy-to-understand components

  • Unwavering journalistic integrity and ethical standards

  • Appears on behalf of the station at public events

  • In-person attendance is required

 

Requirements:

  • Past anchor experience required; 2-5 years preferred

  • Past reporting experience (2-5 years) required

  • Demonstrated ability to enterprise and uncover

  • Your demo reel should be indicative of your everyday work

  • Bilingual experience is a plus

  • Proven Anchor with ability to connect with viewers, in addition to strong reporting skills

  • Ability to operate mobile transmission devices and use the latest technology

  • Can work in all weather conditions and carry up to 50 pounds

  • Valid driver’s license, can drive large vehicles over long distances, and a clear driving record.

  • Ability to work varied shifts, including overnights and weekends

  • Can deal with the stresses and pressures of time-sensitive newscast production
