job.title: Product Marketing Manager, News
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is looking for a motivated, collaborative, creative, analytical, and user-centric product marketer to help deepen audience engagement with our News product, with a particular focus on community and sharing features in the core Times app.

Reporting to the Director of Product Marketing, News, you will be embedded within the Community News Product team as the dedicated product marketing lead. You will partner closely with product, design, and newsroom stakeholders to leverage our community and sharing experiences to drive daily habit and new audience growth.

Your core focus will be the Community News Product team, with opportunities to support other editorially driven News product teams as priorities require. You will combine strategic leadership with hands-on execution: helping shape the product roadmap, developing go-to-market strategies, leading cross-functional launches, and creating lifecycle marketing programs that help our readers feel connected to our journalism, our newsroom, and each other.

This role is a hybrid position, where you'll be in the office three times per week in our NYC Headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Act as the embedded product marketing lead for the Community News Product team, partnering with product, design, and newsroom stakeholders to define the role of commenting, community features, and sharing in the News product experience.

  • Partner with editors, reporters, and newsroom leadership to increase journalist participation in comments and community spaces, ensuring those interactions align with editorial values while deepening trust and engagement among readers.

  • Validate unique market and audience opportunities within News community and sharing experiences by gathering insight into reader and reporter perspectives, creating audience segmentation frameworks and personas that build empathy for how people participate in and benefit from community features and C2C sharing.

  • Craft positioning and messaging and develop go-to-market strategies for evolving community and sharing features, such as commenting improvements, reporter-led interactions, and sharing prompts. Use market and customer insights to design campaigns and in-product programs that increase engagement, repeat visits, and new audience growth.

  • Create and increase habitual product usage and retention by monitoring KPIs, conducting message tests and experiments, and supplementing quantitative data with qualitative feedback from readers and newsroom partners.

  • Collaborate with other News product teams. Lead and influence cross-functional teams without formal authority, helping stakeholders align on shared goals and balance growth, user experience, and editorial integrity.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to the Director of Product Marketing, News.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of related experience in marketing, product marketing, or product management, including at least 2 years of insights-driven go-to-market experience.

  • Experience with the product development lifecycle and operating within product-led teams; experience driving successful go-to-market strategies for product and feature launches, aligning product marketing and messaging to a larger brand narrative, and translating brand strategy into product marketing output.

  • Experience working in newsroom or editorial environments, driving audience and engagement with journalism or community features.

  • Demonstrated experience partnering with editorial or audience teams to design and promote community or social experiences (comments, reactions, forums) that deepen engagement.

  • Lead teams without formal authority, collaborating across product, newsroom, marketing, and data disciplines to achieve shared outcomes.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Digital subscription, content, newsletter, or mobile app experience.

  • Experience with referral programs, C2C community management, or two-sided marketplaces.

  • Distill essential insights from research and create clear and thoughtful market requirement documents and creative briefs.

  • Balance creative, conceptual thinking with data-driven projects; excel in creative and analytical environments; identify and assess success metrics.

  • Capacity for, and interest in, flexing across both planning and execution, shifting between strategic direction-setting and hands-on go-to-market work as needed.

  • Demonstrated collaboration with different disciplines; build trust and relationships quickly, with empathy for customers and expertise in understanding user experience.

  • Experience working on products where brand and editorial integrity are competitive advantages, maintaining trust while experimenting with new community formats and engagement tactics.

The Product Marketing, Editorial Solutions team develops newsroom-driven advertising experiences that align brand and marketer needs with the editorial strategy of The New York Times. Partnering with colleagues across Sales, Revenue Operations, Product, Audience Insights, Ad Operations, and the newsroom, the team ensures agreement. The team ensures that our editorial sponsorships and alignment products are clear and drive value for both advertisers and readers.

As the Product Marketing, Editorial Solutions Director you will be an important connection between the needs of our advertisers and the editorial strategy of The New York Times. You will collaborate with partners across Revenue Operations, Sales and Product Marketing to develop and scale sponsorship opportunities based on an understanding of advertising demand and newsroom priorities.   • Stay current on the external advertising landscape — our competitive set, category trends and latest digital capabilities — with a focus on sponsorship and alignment products.

  • Develop clearly defined, market-ready editorial sponsorship and alignment products, including pricing, packaging, positioning and go-to-market materials for sales enablement..
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

job.title: Reporter Fellow, Local Investigations - Mississippi, Louisiana, & Arkansas
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role

The Times is looking for reporters with a local story idea who want to investigate it under the editing guidance of Dean Baquet, The Times’s former executive editor, and a group of veteran investigative editors.

The goal of the Local Investigative Fellowship is to provide fellows the opportunity to learn the ways and means of investigative reporting from some of the best in the business. Our fellows will be based in the communities where they are reporting and make periodic trips to The Times’s offices for training and support.

This one year program is for reporters who have a local investigative story idea rooted in Louisiana, Mississippi, or Arkansas.  

This is a NY Guild role based in Louisiana, Mississippi, or Arkansas.

Responsibilities:

  • Spend a year producing signature investigative work focused on your state or region that will be published by The Times.
  • Under the guidance of Mr. Baquet and a handpicked group of veteran editors, you will receive the rare opportunity to learn the judgment, skills and techniques needed to excel at investigative journalism from the best in the business.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3 to 5 years of professional experience as a reporter covering a beat for a local newspaper or local digital news outlet
  • You are an independent journalist or a journalist employed at a newsroom willing to provide a yearlong sabbatical

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Significant experience covering a beat and an idea for an investigative story that you have not had the time, resources or editing support to pursue
  • Ability to bring a new perspectives to investigative journalism

Learn more about the program here. 

To apply, upload a résumé, Cover Letter (as described below) and five clips in one attachment. Applications that fail to include any of these materials or follow these instructions will not be considered. 

Your Cover Letter must include at least one story idea or pitch, but you may include multiple if you'd like. Please limit each story idea or pitch to 500 words. We are not looking for polished story ideas or pitches. Instead, your answers to these questions will help us assess where you are in the reporting process and what editorial support and resources the local investigative fellowship could offer you.

  • What is your investigative story idea or area of focus? How would your story expose something new, something no one else has already revealed?
  • Describe who has been harmed and in what way. Is the harm enough to spark outrage?
  • Will your story hold someone accountable? Who and how?
  • What critical records, data and human sources will be required to tell your story? Describe how you have, or could, obtain these critical sources.
  • What do you need help with to report this story, and what are the barriers?
  • Can you give us a sense of what has been written about the subject? Please include clips of notable reporting on the topic.

We appreciate proposals that are as detailed as possible. Successful applicants have included specifics about what they aimed to prove through their investigations. 

For example, a reporter for The Baltimore Banner had reason to believe that the city’s overdose crisis was the worst in the nation. Mississippi Today had evidence of abuses in local sheriffs offices. And a reporter for The Desert Sun in Palm Springs, Calif., suspected a pattern of deaths inside local jails. 

Candidates should submit five published clips that show excellence — in evocative writing, through high-impact news stories and by highlighting the voices of local communities. Your clips should be uploaded to the additional materials application question below. Please ensure to include the full text of your clips, not just the links.

What makes a good local investigation?

  • Starts with high stakes
    How does the story affect people’s lives and livelihoods? Their health, safety and basic quality of life?
  • Has a clear line of accountability
    Great investigations have a line of accountability to someone or some group with significant power.
  • Reveals something
    Does your investigation reveal something that someone or some institution is trying to keep secret?
  • Has a clear sense of place
    The most important element for any local investigation: How is it (e.g. the policy, the circumstance or the failure) unique to your community?

You may apply to the Local Investigations Fellowship once per calendar year. You may also apply for other newsroom opportunities, however separate applications must be submitted for each program.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. We will not sponsor new work visas for the fellowship, but we may consider you if you have an existing work visa or a valid student visa that can be extended via Optional Practical Training

Applicants will be notified about their status on a rolling basis. 

Keep in mind that the fellowships are very competitive and generate a high level of interest. We won’t be able to accept applications that are mailed or emailed to us. Nor will we acknowledge the status of every application upon receipt or during the vetting process. We will contact you for interviews as needed.

These positions are represented by the NewsGuild of NY

You will oversee the end-to-end measurement of video effectiveness, from individual videos to longer-form recurring concepts, and translate data into relevant strategies that inform production, distribution, and editorial decisions. You will also work with product, design, and editorial teams to improve on-platform video experiences.

You will report to the Managing Director, News Products on the Audience Insights Team and will collaborate with partners across the Newsroom. You understand how to blend market research and user research methods and practices into actionable insights for an entire mission.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop audience research to support the creation and growth of video franchises and recurring shows. Drawing on research methods used by production studios and streaming networks, you'll conduct research that can inform greenlight decisions — including concept testing, pilot testing, audience appetite studies, and competitive landscape analysis.
  • Partner with video leadership to evaluate whether a format, host, or editorial premise has the demand to sustain an audience over time. For existing shows, help build longitudinal tracking that monitors audience health: loyalty, satisfaction, and reasons for churn.
  • Help build a video performance tracking program grounded in survey-based measurement, tracking metrics like awareness, recall, engagement, and sentiment among defined audience segments over time.
  • Working alongside analytics teams, you'll help establish benchmarks, monitor performance across all surfaces where video is published (owned and operated, social, streaming), and develop a consistent cadence of reporting that gives editorial, product, and business stakeholders a reliable read on how our videos are landing with audiences.
  • Lead quantitative and qualitative research among target audiences to support video strategy and format development (e.g., format preference studies, thumbnail and title concept tests, viewer satisfaction studies). Partner with video producers and editors to understand their needs and scope appropriate methodologies, from brief development through questionnaire design, survey launch, and insight delivery.
  • Manage multiple research projects and ad-hoc requests simultaneously, developing timelines and planning resources.
  • Partner or lead research on other editorial projects and franchises, such as newsletters, podcasts, or other emerging products
  • Collaborate with research partners, analytics teams, and company partners.
  • Identify opportunities to improve the quality, speed, and effect of video measurement, including recommending new vendors, tools, and methodologies.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of experience in market research, user research, or consumer insights, with an emphasis on multimodal and product research.
  • Proficiency in both qualitative and quantitative research methodologies and experience with continuous improvement and new ideas.
  • Experience leading all facets of a tracking program, including vendor relationships, questionnaire development, data mining, and reporting.
  • Fluency in analyzing large datasets, identifying insights, and creating clear reports.
  • Experience developing timelines across multiple projects, applying project management skills.
  • Experience managing external research partners/vendors.
  • Experience with visualization tools and creating compelling presentations.

job.title: Research Lead, New AI Products & Platforms
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Mission Overview & Responsibilities: 

We are looking for a Research Lead with a passion for ensuring that reader-centric insights are at the heart of the product development process. You will lead a variety of end-to-end research projects that drive strategy for the New A.I. Products and Platforms (NAPP) Mission. You will work with a cross-functional digital product team, including Product, Design, Editorial, Engineering and Marketing. You will report to the Managing Director of News Products and Audience Insights at The New York Times.

The mission of the New York Times Audience Insights team is to help The Times grow by understanding our audience. The Audience Insights team is centralized team of researchers working with teams across The New York Times. We utilize product, human-centered design, innovation, market and UX research, and we draw from principles in the social sciences (Psychology, Anthropology, Sociology and Behavioral Economics).

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City office.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead a human-centered design approach for products teams, inspiring colleagues to build innovative product features grounded in user needs to drive NAPP and company goals.

  • Use research-based insights and GenAI tools for rapid prototype iteration.

  • Own evaluation for quality and editorial integrity: Create frameworks to assess the success of A.I. prototypes and products.

  • Build innovative solutions using AI tools to support certain parts of the research process.

  • Champion A.I. innovation and ethics: Stay up to date with industry trends, new research methodologies, LLM advancements, and emerging technologies. Champion the ethical and responsible use of AI, ensuring our tools uphold our standards of accuracy and objectivity.

  • Complement research with behavioral data, proprietary and industry research, and A/B testing results to provide a holistic view of our users.

  • Work with Audience Insights researchers across News Product, Marketing, Cooking, Wirecutter, The Athletic and Games to identify opportunities to collaborate and avoid duplicative product work.

  • Manage external research vendors to support moderation, fieldwork, and analysis, ensuring high-quality and efficient project execution.

  • Contribute to the collaborative culture of Audience Insights and the NAPP Mission; help The New York Times understand, and build empathy for, our audiences.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications: 

  • 8+ years of research and insights experience.

  • Experience researching chat interfaces or GenAI search tools and using a range of GenAI tools and features in your work.

  • Experience moderating qualitative research and facilitating brainstorms and workshops with cross-functional partners.

  • Mastery of a range of research methods . These methods include participatory design, in-person and remote interviews, ethnographies, co-creation, and user-initiated feedback tools. Additionally, surveys, card-sorting, and usability studies are also part of the range.

  • Experience executing qualitative and quantitative research and selecting the right approach based on the problem to be solved.

  • Experience synthesizing complex findings into compelling narratives and visualize insights for diverse audiences.

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • Experience conducting research for early-stage 0-1 product development, helping teams identify opportunities, validate concepts, and shape new product experiences.

  • Experience working in rapid prototyping environments, using research to inform iterative product development and experimentation.

  • Experience building alignment among cross-functional stakeholders, including Product, Design, Engineering, Editorial, and Marketing partners.

  • Experience presenting to stakeholders, senior management, and fellow researchers.

  • A deep curiosity about the role of AI in shaping the future of information, media, and journalism.

job.title: Senior Analyst, Total Rewards
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. About the role

As the Senior Analyst, Total Rewards (Data Insights & Modeling), you will be a strategic partner reporting directly to the SVP, Total Rewards. You will bridge the gap between complex data science and talent strategy, serving as a lead architect for our global compensation structures. You will go beyond traditional reporting to build and maintain the predictive models that forecast salary market movement, simulate compensation cycles, and drive pay equity outcomes. This position is pivotal in ensuring our compensation practices remain fair, equitable, and market-relevant, directly supporting our ability to attract and retain the world-class talent necessary to sustain The New York Times’s journalistic mission.

  • Strategize design and maintenance of global compensation structures using advanced data science and predictive analytics.
  • Develop sophisticated models for variable pay (AIP/LTI) and annual merit/bonus cycles under various business performance scenarios.

  • Conduct statistically significant pay equity analyses to identify and remediate gaps across demographics.
  • Build and maintain automated Total Rewards benchmarking tools and executive dashboards.
  • Lead the advancement of data insight capabilities to support compensation analytics for the New York Times workforce.
  • Manage participation in external compensation surveys, including job matching and data validation.

Basic Qualifications

  • 5–8+ years of experience in Compensation or Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), with at least 3 years focused on advanced modeling.
  • Proficiency in statistical analysis (correlation and regression) and experience with HCM systems (e.g., Workday).
  • Advanced proficiency in Excel (VBA, Power Query, Complex Nested Formulas) and data visualization tools (Tableau, Power BI, or Visier).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with SQL, Python, or R.
  • CCP (Certified Compensation Professional) or GRP certification.

job.title: Senior Community Editor
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Every week, The New York Times hosts hundreds of conversations in our comments sections across a wide variety of topics and types of articles — from investigations and breaking news to features and service journalism. We are seeking a Senior Editor to work directly with reporters, writers and editors to build this community.

This role is designed for an editor who thrives in fast-paced environments, possesses sharp news judgment, and loves finding creative ways to bring reader voices into our journalism. You will be collaborating with editors and reporters to identify opportunities for them to participate in comments, editing posts for length, clarity and accessibility and finding appropriate places to embed conversations in our journalism. You will also work closely with the wider community team to ensure our editorial approach and workflow fits into evolving moderation and policy guidelines.

The ideal candidate is eager to experiment with new approaches to reader engagement, be comfortable training creative teams on technical concepts and is brimming with ideas for how to build and support online communities.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Identify articles and storylines that would benefit from journalist participation in the comments, and reach out to editors and reporters in advance of publication.
  • Edit posts for length, clarity and tone, helping to grow the number of journalists who are independently posting in creative ways that align with our style.
  • Collect high quality examples of reporter participation and help train the global newsroom on best practices.
  • Make Community team initiatives more visible and useful to the wider newsroom and enterprise by writing regular internal updates.
  • Build pathways to community surfaces by embedding comments across the report and help track their effectiveness.
  • Pitch and execute on community-first initiatives that deepen reader-reporter relationships, e.g. AMAs, UGC roundups
  • Collaborate with cross-functional partners to build and improve tools that make journalist participation easy and intuitive.
  • Help to develop guardrails and approaches for staff to participate in conversations about hot-button topics across the report.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Community Editorial Lead.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of editorial experience with news organizations or media companies
  • Excellent editorial judgment and project management skills
  • Demonstrated interest in the online community ecosystem
  • Passion for The New York Times mission and commitment to be part of our innovation and growth

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience training reporters and editors on digital tools and editorial approaches.
  • A proven ability to meet deadlines in a fast-paced news environment.
  • Editing samples of work you have assigned or played a significant role in shaping.

job.title: Senior Designer, Games Marketing (Temporary)
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Senior Designer, Games Marketing plays an important, hands-on role in concepting and developing campaigns and marketing efforts that support The New York Times' business for the Games product. This role sits within the Games marketing vertical and reports to the Associate Creative Director, Games, Marketing.

You will work closely with other marketing creative team members (writers, designers and our audio and video teams), as well as partners in marketing and media strategy, product design, audience insights and brand identity to bring to life campaigns across the marketing funnel that drive performance while upholding a high bar for design craft. You are responsible for driving creative ideation, execution and production of marketing assets, as well as helping evolve the design systems, libraries and templates that support experimentation at scale.

You bring a refined aesthetic, a nuanced understanding of typography, layout and color, motion design and strong design craft skills. We want an individual who is not only just a stellar designer, but also idea‑focused and can do the work of efficiently bringing their ideas to life in a way that inspires and excites others, and then presents them effectively and enthusiastically.

This is a temporary 6 month role reporting to the Associate Creative Director, Marketing, Games. It can be either remote within the US or hybrid in our NYC offices. If hybrid in our NYC headquarters, you can typically expect to come into the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and execute conceptual, visually compelling marketing campaigns for the Games product, ensuring work supports awareness, consideration, conversion and retention goals across the full reader and subscriber journey.
  • Design and adapt campaign creative across paid, owned and earned channels — including digital, social, email, in‑app placements, app stores and OOH — in line with The Times' brand standards and Games marketing strategy.
  • Translate in‑product experiences, editorial formats and key feature benefits into clear marketing assets that deepen engagement and drive habitual use of the Games product.
  • Implement the practical application of design systems for Games marketing, including creating, implementing and maintaining component libraries and style guides in Figma, and ensuring pixel‑perfect execution across platforms and devices.
  • Collaborate with writers, art directors, audio and video partners to concept, refine and ship creative that clearly communicates the value of our journalism and our lifestyle products and drives subscriptions and engagement.
  • Help develop and maintain scalable visual systems, templates and libraries that enable disciplined experimentation across paid and owned marketing channels while upholding a high bar for craft and brand consistency.
  • Work from creative briefs, participate actively in reviews and incorporate feedback from stakeholders, staying comfortable with shifts in strategy or approach based on evolving business needs.
  • Create clear, compelling presentation materials and articulate the rationale for your design decisions to colleagues and leadership, connecting creative choices to performance, user behavior and broader marketing strategy.
  • Bring fresh ideas and a spirit of experimentation to how we market our journalism, product experiences and bundles, contributing to a culture of continuous learning on the marketing creative team.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Associate Creative Director, Marketing, Games.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 7+ years of hands-on graphic design experience at an advertising agency, digital agency, studio or in‑house team, with a focus on marketing or advertising creative and demonstrable experience in growth‑oriented campaigns.
  • A portfolio that shows both sharp execution and conceptual thinking across social, digital display, email, in‑app, app store and print, with clear examples of how your design choices clarify complex ideas and drive performance across the funnel.
  • Deep proficiency in core visual design principles — typography, layout, balance, hierarchy, proportion, color, emphasis and unity — and a refined aesthetic from concept through production.
  • Expert‑level skills in Figma and Adobe Creative Suite, including building and maintaining components, styles, libraries and design systems used across a marketing organization.
  • Demonstrated expertise in design systems: creating, implementing and maintaining component libraries and style guides; ensuring pixel‑perfect execution; and applying system thinking with a focus on practical implementation.
  • Proficiency in motion graphics and animation, with hands-on experience using After Effects and other motion tools to bring narratives to life across marketing channels.
  • Experience partnering with developers and product teams to ship high‑quality digital experiences.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • B.A., B.F.A. or M.F.A. in graphic design, visual communication or another related design discipline, or equivalent professional experience and portfolio that demonstrates comparable design training and craft.
  • Comfort working cross‑functionally with partners in marketing strategy, media, product design, audience insights and brand identity, and enthusiasm for collaborating on campaigns that both look great and perform against growth goals.
  • Understanding of trends in digital advertising and growth marketing, plus familiarity with the latest social media ecosystem and how brands show up in a way that feels authentic and aligned with our standards.
  • A belief in the value of journalism to people and society, and genuine curiosity about our work and company — ideally, you enjoy reading, watching and listening to New York Times journalism and playing New York Times Games.

About the role:

The Senior Director, Global Benefits will be responsible for the strategic design, operational excellence, and holistic governance of all benefits and perquisites for The New York Times on a global scale. Reporting to the SVP, Total Rewards, this leader will architect a robust benefits strategy that attracts, engages, and retains top talent and ensures fiscal sustainability. This role is also responsible for leading the Benefits operations function to deliver a superior employee experience through resource optimization and cost-efficient best practices. Beyond design and administration, the incumbent will partner with Corporate Communications and Culture to drive an engaging communications strategy, ensuring our diverse and complex population understands the full value of their benefits package. 

This is a hybrid role based in our New York headquarters. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and implement a global benefits strategy that aligns with our goals, ensuring equity and relevance in local markets across the US and internationally.
  • Oversee the design and execution of all benefits programs, ensuring they are competitive, comprehensive, and compliant with local, federal, and international regulations (e.g., ERISA, ACA, GDPR).
  • Lead the Global Benefits Operations department, overseeing a team of benefits administrators to deliver a high-quality employee experience.

  • Collaborate with Legal counsel to review plan documents and summary plan descriptions, ensuring all programs meet legal requirements and minimize liability.
  • Ensure that benefit plans for unionized employees are administered following collective bargaining agreements.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • Experience working with a unionized workforce and supporting labor negotiations.

We are a team of editors, designers, program managers, developers, strategists and audience experts who create content for leading brands around the world.

This role will contribute to the creation of branded content advertising — from brainstorming and conceptualizing creative ideas to answering client briefs to writing, editing and commissioning projects. You will take specific leadership in B2B campaigns, in both growing new advertiser opportunities and following through in production. Specifically, the core tasks of the Senior Editor, T Brand Studio International includes participating in brainstorms and creating pitches. Additionally, you will conduct research and interviews, write, commission and edit articles. Furthermore, you will see video and podcast projects through the production process. The Senior Editor will be part of the larger T Brand team based in London, Singapore, Paris and New York. This is a hybrid position, you will report to the Editorial Director, EMEA and APAC, T Brand International, based in London. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

job.title: Senior Editor, Style, NYT Wirecutter
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

Wirecutter is seeking a visionary senior editor to oversee our style team.

As Wirecutter's senior style editor, you'll be responsible for guiding and expanding our style and accessories coverage to become an indispensable destination for readers looking for straightforward, engaging, and smart advice to help them develop their personal style. You will lead a team of writers and work closely with the photo and video team, audience development team, and lifestyle writers and editors to make sure our coverage is helpful, engaging, and up-to-date. We ask that you have writing, editing, and management skills, as well as subject-matter expertise.

You have sharp editing skills and a firm grasp of all categories of style, including clothing basics, fashion accessories, bags and carrying items, shoes, and more. You have a strong knowledge of the style landscape, whether menswear or womenswear. You're a fashion expert who knows brands and trends as well as how to apply a skeptic's eye to the industry's claims at large. You know that when it comes to personal style, there's no such thing as the best product for everyone, but you understand how Wirecutter's method of rigorous testing, thorough reporting, and deep beat expertise can help readers find the perfect option that fits their needs. You also understand the importance of journalistic standards and integrity, and you're passionate about cutting through the clutter to provide inclusive recommendations at any budget.

A successful person in this role will be comfortable creating an exciting guide-based coverage plan while managing a team and collaborating with colleagues across Wirecutter's newsroom. You have a solid network of fashion freelancers, publicists, and sources, and an instinct for what makes a good style story. As a Wirecutter journalist, you'll also recognize the importance of considering those with different needs and diverse perspectives.

This is a hybrid position, based out of our LIC office in NYC and includes regular attendance in the office.

Responsibilities:

  • Plan coverage for style and accessories guides and projects over the course of the year
  • With the editorial director, execute strategy for our coverage and manage a team of writers in execution of dynamic style content, including guides, short-form, and multi-platform coverage
  • Assign projects to freelance and staff writers as needed, and manage them on a per-project basis
  • Manage editors and writers as direct reports, set clear expectations, facilitate performance feedback, and support learning and development
  • Manage editorial process and serve as top or lead editor for guides, short-form journalism, and other projects that fall under your area of coverage
  • Approve ideas from your team and use data to support pitches and to monitor performance
  • Contribute original ideas to test planning, suggest creative reporting strategies, challenge writers' assumptions
  • Interact with our reader community through multiple channels, including social, comments, and through our community team
  • May be required to attend trade shows and product news events as needed
  • Perform related work as assigned
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the editorial director of lifestyle

Basic Qualifications:

  • Minimum 5 years of professional editing experience and at least two years managing editors and/or writers, with a proven ability to effectively manage projects and direct reports
  • The ability to write clearly and accessibly about topics for lay audiences, and edit with an eye for helping others do the same
  • Deep knowledge of fashion subject matter and clear sense of good aesthetic taste

 Preferred Qualifications:

  • Excellent communication and people management skills
  • An effective organizational system with the ability to manage multiple projects at various stages in the publication process
  • A commitment to high standards of reporting and accuracy
  • An understanding of how to use web analytics data to make editorial decisions

Please include a cover letter and your résumé/CV.

For roles in the U.S., dependent on your role, you may be eligible for variable pay, such as an annual bonus and restricted stock. The Developer Platforms organization provides cloud infrastructure and tooling to 100+ teams and 750+ engineers in NYT Product Engineering through an internal developer platform. The DevEx Platforms team (6 engineers) focuses on developer experience and workflow automation.

We’re now expanding into more AI-assisted developer workflows using tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and Copilot to support debugging, migrations, test generation, and everyday development in a safe, measurable way.

This role sits in Developer Platforms and reports to the Engineering Manager of the DevEx Platforms team.

About the Role

As a Senior Software Engineer on DevEx Platforms, you’ll build GenAI-augmented developer experiences and platform capabilities used across all of The New York Times.

Your work will help teams ship faster and more safely, pay down technical debt through structured migrations and platform modernization, and turn effective internal practices into reusable tools and agents.

What You’ll Do

  • Design and build GenAI-powered developer tooling: prompts, IDE integrations, Cursor/Claude rules, and telemetry to understand how they’re used.
  • Build and run the GenAI developer platform: Tools, services, and integrations leveraging LiteLLM to power both local and background/long-running agents, providing auth, configuration, and LLM routing.
  • Own guardrails and observability for agentic workflows: integrate with Datadog, DX, and FinOut, define sensible standards, and make sure agents interact with Jira, GitHub, and internal platforms in a safe, auditable way.
  • Work closely with engineers and managers across Product Engineering to understand how they build software today and to design solutions that actually fit the way they work.
  • Support our mission and values, including journalistic independence, and keep ethics and safety central to how we use AI in developer workflows.
  • This role includes limited on-call responsibilities; the schedule will be set when you join.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Engineering Manager of the DevEx Platforms team

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience
  • 2+ years of experience improving developer experience through workflows, documentation, and capabilities of the internal platform
  • Experience designing and building cloud native applications. We use Golang
  • Hands-on experience building software using GenAI tools, like GitHub's Copilot, Cursor or Claude Code

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of hands on experience managing and deploying resources in AWS
  • 2+ years of experience managing workloads deployed on Kubernetes
  • Experience in prompt engineering or building AI-powered tools

This role requires limited on-call hours. An on-call schedule will be determined when you join, taking into account team size and other variables.

As a Senior Engineer, Marketing, you'll be embedded with the Marketing team, providing us with technical leadership, consulting, and systems thinking. You'll assemble the orchestration systems, integrations, and AI capabilities that help teams work faster, and in more data‑driven ways. You will lead end‑to‑end design, implementation, and management of the marketing campaign lifecycle system, integrations, internal tools, and learning/experimentation infrastructure. You will report to our Director, Advertising Systems.

Responsibilities:

  • You will write high-quality, secure, and well-tested code, contributing to standards and documentation for Marketing infrastructure, data models, and tools
  • You will build the campaign lifecycle orchestration backbone
  • You will build integrations and internal tools that connect project management, collaboration, creative, media, and email/lifecycle platforms
  • You will work with Marketing partners as a technical advisor, translating needs into designs
  • You will integrate AI agents and automations (including LLM-powered flows) into Marketing workflows according to company GenAI guidance
  • You will design and operate data pipelines and models that ingest marketing and performance data into a data layer, supporting experimentation and analytics workflows
  • You will deliver abstractions and APIs that ensure AI systems and our users to create campaign wrap-ups, insights, next-test recommendations, and more from that data
  • You will lead reliability, observability, and incident response for integrations, data pipelines, and automations, including monitoring, logging, alerting, auditing, feature flags for pilots, and change management.
  • You will demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience with a focus on backend or full-stack development for distributed systems and APIs.
  • Proficiency in Python or TypeScript/Node.js and experience building integrations, services, data pipelines, and internal tools (using modern frontend frameworks such as React or similar).
  • 5+ years of experience with REST/GraphQL APIs, OAuth2, webhooks, and event-driven patterns
  • Hands-on experience building applications with large language models (LLMs), such as prompt flows, retrieval-augmented generation, or AI agents, using approved GenAI tools.
  • 1+ years of experience delivering production systems on cloud platforms (AWS preferred), including using serverless services (e.g., Lambda, API Gateway, managed databases/queues) and CI/CD practices.
  • 3+ years of experience working with marketing and performance data and supporting experimentation and analytics workflows, including designing metrics and dashboards.

  • 1+ years of experience implementing or integrating campaign orchestration and workflow automation tools (such as Notion, Monday.com, Asana, or similar) into marketing or operations environments.
  • 1+ years of experience working with or integrating Marketing technology stacks, such as customer data platforms (CDPs) or CRMs, ad platforms, email or lifecycle platforms, project management tools, and collaboration tools.
  • 1+ years of experience partnering with data engineers and analysts to design schemas, interfaces, and experimentation frameworks that serve both BI and AI use cases.
  • AWS serverless expertise across services such as Lambda, API Gateway, RDS, SQS, SNS, CloudFront, and related tooling.

  • 1+ years of experience configuring and using observability tooling such as DataDog, along with infrastructure-level logging, alerting, networking, and application security.
  • 1+ years of Experience with tools such as BigQuery, Hex, Mode, Statsig or similar for analytics and experimentation.

The New York Times is looking for a Senior Engineering Manager, reporting to the Director of Engineering, Games Platform, to lead a team focused on our mobile platform. In this role, you will lead and support engineers and collaborate with cross functional partners to deliver and maintain the premier destination for digital puzzle games.

This position is key to building the next generation of our Games app across iOS and Android. We see value in continued investment in Games as a standalone subscription opportunity and a valuable member of the overall NYTimes bundle, which also includes News, Cooking, Wirecutter and The Athletic. We view our mobile platform as the best opportunity for Games to continue driving engagement with our product, in addition to driving subscription growth.

NYT Games is a supportive and collaborative team that values inclusion, diversity and personal growth. We combine exceptional product development with a world-class suite of puzzles including beloved titles such as the NYT Crossword, Spelling Bee, Connections, Crossplay and Wordle. Come help us on our journey to grow a world-class mobile platform, as we continue delivering delightful experiences to millions daily.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 2-3+ days/week.

  • Define and drive a multi-year technical strategy for the mobile platform, balancing feature delivery with architectural scalability.

About the Role

New York Times Wirecutter team is looking for a Senior Manager, Audience & Product Analytics to power our growth strategy. Your core mandate will be to build an understanding of our audience— who they are, how they engage with content and product features, and what brings them back. You will lead a team of analysts responsible for understanding audience trends, driving product improvement, and optimizing user engagement. You will provide leadership and data-driven insights, working with audience, product, and engineering leads to establish goals, design experiments, and uncover new opportunities.

You will report to the Executive Director of Data Analytics and Insights, Wirecutter. This opportunity is flexible to in office or remote work.

Responsibilities

  • You will manage a team of three direct reports—promoting a culture of curiosity and excellence while setting clear deliverables, supporting career growth, and ensuring high-quality analytics output
  • You will analyze audience growth, traffic drivers, customer journey touch points, and user engagement trends to inform strategic decision-making.
  • You will partner with functional leads (Product, Design, Engineering, Editorial) to set strategy, define goals, and build the audience and product analytics roadmap.
  • You will lead the design, execution, and post-analysis of product experiments (A/B testing). Provide expertise on primary metrics, trade-offs between competing goals, and recommendations to evolve product offerings.
  • You will translate complex behavioral data and insights into compelling narratives and actionable recommendations 
  • You will demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications

  • 6+ years of experience in data analytics, with direct experience working with product or publishing teams.
  • 2+ years of dedicated people leadership experience managing analysts.
  • 5+ years of experience in A/B testing
  • 1+ years of experience reporting on audience engagement, traffic trends, or customer journey modeling for a digital publisher or media organization.
  • Advanced mastery of SQL and experience with BI/data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Looker).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Proficiency in Python or R
  • Knowledge of the digital media industry or affiliate marketing.
  • Quantitative degree in Statistics, Data Science, Economics, Computer Science, or a related field.

job.title: Senior Manager, Lifecycle Marketing (Temporary)
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About New York Times Games

The New York Times is looking for a Senior Lifecycle Marketing Manager to join the New York Times Games team, reporting to the Executive Director of Marketing, Games.

In 2025, players completed more than 11 billion games across our portfolio, led by hits like Wordle and Connections, alongside the iconic New York Times Crossword, which has existed in print since 1942.

Games is one of the largest and fastest-growing businesses among our portfolio of products, including Cooking, Wirecutter, The Athletic and News.

About the Role

We need a senior lifecycle marketer to lead how we keep Games players engaged over time across email, push (app and desktop), display and other channels. You will focus on deepening engagement with our existing players (non sub + sub)  and reducing churn. 

You will lead the end-to-end marketing lifecycle strategy for Games players, from onboarding and activation through ongoing engagement, win-back and reactivation. You will design and run cross-channel programs that create timely, relevant, and personalized experiences for our players, grounded in data and insight. You will work closely with product, growth marketing, product marketing, data and creative partners to bring these programs to life.

This is a temporary hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters, reporting to the Executive Director, Marketing, Games. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities

Lifecycle Strategy and Planning

  • Define the lifecycle marketing strategy for Games, including goals for activation, engagement, retention and reactivation.
  • Map player journeys and identify key moments where lifecycle programs can deepen engagement and reduce churn.
  • Partner with product and product marketing to ensure lifecycle programs align with feature launches, game updates and the broader Games roadmap.

Channel Execution and Optimization

  • Lead the planning and execution of lifecycle campaigns and automations across email, push, display and other channels, from brief through launch, in partnership with channel owners. 
  • Work with channel owners to build, test and optimize always-on programs (onboarding flows, engagement nudges, winback journeys) that drive meaningful changes in player behavior.

Data, Measurement and Insights

  • Own key lifecycle metrics for Games, including retention, reactivation, engagement and churn, and build reporting that gives the team a clear view of performance.
  • Partner with analytics and data science teams to use segmentation, cohort analysis and predictive signals to inform targeting and personalization of lifecycle programs.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Build strong relationships with product, product marketing, growth marketing, media team and channel owners, audience insights, data analytics, engineering and creative to align on shared goals, design and launch lifecycle programs.

Player Experience and Brand Stewardship

  • Champion the perspective of our players, bringing research and behavior insights into planning and creative development.
  • Balance performance goals with a thoughtful, respectful approach to frequency, personalization and offers. 

Basic Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in lifecycle marketing, CRM, retention marketing or related fields, with a track record of driving measurable improvements in engagement and retention.
  • Experience owning cross-channel lifecycle programs (email, push, and at least one additional channel such as display or in-app messaging) for consumer products or subscription services.
  • Strong analytical skills and comfort working with data to build hypotheses, design tests and interpret results.
  • Operate in cross-functional environments and collaborating with product, analytics, media partners and creative teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with cohort and funnel analysis.
  • Interest in The New York Times and New York Times Games; prior experience with digital subscription, content, or mobile app products.
  • Demonstrated ability to operate both autonomously and collaboratively, with curiosity about identifying and forging new opportunities.

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role

NYT Wirecutter is looking for a Senior Manager, Revenue Analytics to power our business strategy. Your core mandate is to increase audience monetization across our primary businesses—Affiliate, Advertising, and E-commerce—ensuring we preserve long-term audience trust. As a player-coach role, you will lead a team of analysts and partner closely with Revenue, Product, and Marketing leads to establish KPIs, run conversion experiments, and build attribution frameworks that scale revenue. You will report to the Executive Director, Data Analytics.

Responsibilities

  • You will lead, mentor, and onboard a team of two direct reports, nurturing their career growth
  • You will analyze affiliate revenue drivers (e.g., merchant commissions, EPC, conversion rates, and partner yield) across all content touch points.
  • You will be the analytics lead for the newly launched Wirecutter Store, reporting on unit economics, merchandise performance, cart funnel analytics, order value (AOV), and customer acquisition/repeat purchase metrics
  • You will partner with Ad Ops and Advertising teams to track ad yield (RPM, eCPM), fill rates, and ad unit viewability, balancing display and custom content revenue against user experience and page speed
  • You will evaluate trade-offs between affiliate links, ad placements, and Wirecutter Store product placements on site, creating a holistic monetization framework to maximize total revenue per user.
  • You will lead recurring commercial reporting for Wirecutter Leadership, communicating complex multi-channel revenue dynamics, forecasting, and strategic expansion opportunities.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications

  • 6+ years of experience in revenue or e-commerce analytics, with direct experience supporting affiliate marketing, digital advertising, or online retail operations
  • 2+ years of people management experience
  • 3+ years of experience analyzing diverse revenue models, including affiliate marketing, programmatic/direct digital advertising, and DTC e-commerce operations
  • 3+ years of experience in A/B testing, conversion rate optimization (CRO), and pricing/placement experiments aimed at.
  • Advanced mastery of SQL and experience with BI/data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Looker) to build end-to-end commercial dashboards and financial reporting models.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 1+ years of experience working with e-commerce platforms (e.g., Shopify, Magento), ad tech/SSP platforms, and affiliate network platforms
  • Proficiency in Python or R
  • Quantitative degree in Economics, Business Analytics, Finance, Statistics, Data Science, or a related field

job.title: Senior Manager, UX Writing
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About Us

Marketing plays a key role in extending the journalistic legacy and mission of The Times into the future. Our job is to answer the question: “Why is quality journalism worth paying for?” We create award-winning marketing that builds awareness of our brand and affinity for the breadth of our journalistic offering. Above all, we strive to be timely, straightforward and relevant in our marketing — illustrating in new and creative ways how The New York Times can enrich the lives of our readers.

About The Role

In an ongoing effort to create new and elevated product experiences, we’re looking for a Senior Manager, UX Writing to concept, develop and execute UX writing across The New York Times portfolio, including our core news product and Games, Cooking, Wirecutter and The Athletic.

You will write crisp, clear and engaging copy for customer journeys, partnering with product, design, marketing, engineering, research and editorial teams to create experiences that grow, engage and retain subscribers. You will also manage a small team of freelance UX writers, coordinating resources, assigning projects and developing practical standards and workflows.

We're looking for candidates who can balance the clarity that UX copy demands with the personality and approachability of an engaging brand. We will look to you to help create solutions that inspire and excite others, then present them effectively and enthusiastically. This is a hybrid role based in our New York headquarters, reporting to the Associate Creative Director, Writing. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Write clear, accurate and compelling user-interface copy for experiences on nytimes.com, in The New York Times app and more.
  • Manage inbound UX writing requests, prioritizing tasks and assigning overflow projects as needed.
  • Maintain quality and consistency across projects and teams, acting as a brand voice steward to ensure all UX copy meets brand, newsroom and product style guidelines and lives up to the journalism itself.
  • Expertly apply brand voice in wayfinding moments, enhancements, paywalls and payflows, plus new tools and features, adjusting tone as appropriate. Touch points might include push notifications, tooltips, light boxes, bottom sheets, screens for new flows and more.
  • Mentor in-house writers and manage a small team of freelance UX writers.
  • Consider problems from multiple angles while aligning work with overarching business and engagement goals.
  • Use insights, data and strategy to influence product copy.
  • Collaborate with designers, prototypers, marketers and more to create compelling UX solutions.
  • Communicate the strategic intent of your work in meetings, presenting rationale to a broad group of partners, including leadership.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of experience writing for product, brand and UX across multiple products, teams or surfaces.
  • Experience managing or functionally leading writers.
  • A portfolio that shows ideas expressed clearly across a range of touchpoints.
  • The ability to write clear, succinct and engaging copy while writing for small spaces.
  • The ability to collaborate with multiple partners and adjust copy based on data and input from others.
  • Fluent in branding and UX theory and practice.
  • Proficiency using Figma.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • A love of writing and storytelling, with the ability to apply it to systemic thinking.
  • Curiosity about every piece of the customer journey.
  • A belief in the value of journalism to people and society, and genuine curiosity about our work and company. We hope you enjoy reading, watching and listening to New York Times journalism and products.

job.title: Senior Multimedia Producer/ SVJ, Serial
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Serial Productions, in collaboration with The New York Times Metro desk, is launching a new bi-weekly narrative podcast focused on New York City. The podcast will be accompanied by weekly editorial extensions — primarily social video, but also newsletters and live events — that share the sensibility of the show while standing alone as distinctive creative work.

The Senior Multimedia Producer will lead the conception, production and evolution of these extensions, helping invent a distinctive visual language that translates Serial's narrative, character-driven stories about New Yorkers into social-first video and other formats that feel unmistakably of New York City.

This role is a key member of the Serial editorial team and will work closely with Serial producers and editors, New York Times video, social and marketing teams, and freelance collaborators to create fun, experimental and ambitious content that grows and deepens the audience for the show and for Serial more broadly.

This role is based in New York City. The Senior Multimedia Producer is expected to spend significant time in person with Serial, Metro and partner teams, in accordance with New York Times policies, while also doing field and location work across the city as needed.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the editorial vision and production strategy for all extensions to the podcast, including social video, newsletters and live or virtual events.
  • Develop platform-specific social video concepts (for example, TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts) that translate the show's reporting, characters and ideas into compelling visual storytelling.
  • Oversee end-to-end production of social videos, from pitching and scripting through shooting, editing, sound design, approvals and publishing.
  • Be able to independently shoot and edit straightforward social video pieces when needed, while primarily commissioning work from New York Times video teams and freelance collaborators.
  • Work with the Metro desk, Serial producers and reporters to identify stories, moments and themes that lend themselves to extensions, and to ensure alignment with the core podcast.
  • Hire, manage and direct freelance videographers, editors, designers and other collaborators; over time, this role may supervise staff producers or associates.
  • Work with Serial staff to develop newsletters and other written extensions that bring the project's reporting, voice and perspective to readers in distinctive formats.
  • Partner with events and live journalism teams to design and produce live or virtual experiences that reflect Serial's editorial sensibility and can generate compelling audio and video.
  • Work with the NYT Audience team to define success metrics for extensions, track performance across platforms and incorporate data and audience insights into ongoing strategy.
  • Run experiments in format, tone, length and distribution to learn what resonates with different audiences while maintaining Serial's editorial standards.
  • Ensure all extensions adhere to New York Times and Serial guidelines around fairness, accuracy, ethics and visual and audio standards.
  • Help foster an inclusive, collaborative and creatively adventurous culture on the Serial team and across partner desks.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Executive Editor, Serial Productions.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Experience (typically 4+ years) producing digital video, social content and multimedia storytelling, ideally in a news, documentary or narrative audio environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to conceive, produce and deliver compelling and unique social video series or campaigns that grow and engage audiences across platforms.
  • Strong hands-on production skills, including scripting, directing talent, field production and working with editors on visual and audio cuts, as well as the ability to shoot and edit short-form social video.
  • Experience collaborating with editorial, audience, marketing and visual teams on cross-platform projects.
  • Comfort working with analytics and platform tools (such as TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and internal dashboards) to interpret performance and inform decisions.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Proven experience managing complex projects with multiple stakeholders, deadlines and deliverables.
  • Experience hiring, directing and giving constructive feedback to freelance and, ideally, staff colleagues.
  • Excellent communication, organization and time-management skills.
  • Deep familiarity with, and enthusiasm for, Serial's work and The New York Times's audio journalism.
  • Experience producing content specifically about New York City and its communities, or in another large metropolitan context with similar complexity.
  • Background in podcast or audio production and comfort working alongside audio-first producers and editors.
  • Experience developing live or virtual events tied to audio or video projects.
  • Familiarity with The New York Times newsroom, standards and workflows, or comparable large news organizations.

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.

You have a refined understanding of podcast and video journalistic production (research, prep, scripting, recording, script editing, post-production and publishing).   • Produce full interviews in audio and video from start to finish

You're a strong people manager, thoughtful storyteller and excellent collaborator. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Washington bureau is seeking a temporary senior staff editor to work on editing Washington news, including stories on the White House, Congress, the military, intelligence agencies, the Justice Department, the State Department, the Supreme Court, health care, economics and more.

You will work on a mix of daily and enterprise stories as well as breaking news and live coverage during weekday evenings, picking up from the dayside team and working alongside other editors in the Washington bureau and on the Live team in New York, as needed. You will also monitor news developments, consult with the Washington Night Editor and bureau leadership about priorities, do first and second reads and make judgments on the length, placement and framing of stories and, at times, assign stories to reporters.

You will need to have familiarity with a wide variety of topics, versatility, speed, proven judgment and the ability to collaborate across desks and platforms.

This is a temporary position based in Washington, D.C., with regular presence in the office, 4 days per week. It includes night and weekend work as newsroom needs require.

Responsibilities:

  • You will work with other editors and reporters to ensure stories are cleanly edited.

job.title: Senior Staff Editor, Well
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Times Well desk is seeking a senior staff editor to edit our weekly newsletter and other reporting about health and wellness. This role is a key position on the team, requiring an editor who has experience working with reporters and freelancers and has a proven track record in health coverage.

You will supervise reporters and assign and edit across many story forms, including news, reported features, visual pieces and profiles. Your work will be timely and ambitious. You should be able to connect the dots and spot trends before our competitors do, and shape stories that have perspective and authority. Your assignments should start conversations. You should have tons of ideas and a willingness to experiment.

Your work will support Well's mission to use evidence-based journalism to explore important issues in health and to help people live healthier and more fulfilling lives.

This role requires high productivity, attention to detail, meeting deadlines and the ability to work seamlessly with other editors on the desk. You are joining a successful team that thrives in part because we're highly collaborative and we embrace constant change and opportunity.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • You will conceive, assign and edit articles, serving as a first editor on several stories per week.
  • You will supervise beat reporters and develop a stable of freelance contributors.
  • You will provide sophisticated second edits on stories as needed.
  • You will manage the digital life of stories, including writing engaging headlines, summaries and captions for digital presentation and promotion across platforms.
  • You will collaborate with our art team.
  • You will meet tight deadlines and juggle multiple priorities expertly.
  • You have strong communication and organizational skills.
  • You are collaborative, collegial and flexible.
  • You will abide by The Times's Code of Conduct and exemplify our Values and Behaviors.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Deputy Editor.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 7+ years of experience as a health, science or lifestyle journalist.
  • Significant editing experience, including a deep understanding of digital publishing.
  • Experience supervising beat reporters and freelancers.
  • Science-literate with a proven ability to parse and contextualize scientific research for a general-interest audience.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Passionate about news and service journalism.
  • Willingness to experiment and collaborate on the Well desk and across departments.

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.

The Senior System Analyst is an individual contributor within Enterprise Technology responsible for the configuration, release management, and operational support of Zip, our procurement and intake platform. As a Sr. Systems Analyst - Procurement you will report to the Sr. Manager of HRIS. You will partner with multiple teams, including Sourcing, Accounts Payable, Finance, Legal, and Enterprise Applications. Your partnerships will ensure Zip remains stable, well-governed, and aligned with Workday and other SaaS financial applications.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days/week.

Responsibilities:

  • Manage Zip configuration, including workflows, fields, validations, permissions, and company settings
  • Manage Zip release cycles (monthly and ad hoc), including reviewing release notes, assessing impact, advising business, coordinating testing, and promoting changes from sandbox to production
  • Administer user roles and permissions in Zip to ensure appropriate access, segregation of tasks, and compliance with governance and security standards
  • Partner with Sourcing, Accounts Payable, Finance, and Legal to translate requirements into Zip configuration changes

  • Follow our SDLC and change control procedures to guarantee proper configuration, testing, validation, and deployment

  • Contribute to governance forums and prioritization meetings, helping evaluate and size enhancement requests (S/M/L/XL) for Zip
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience administering or configuring SaaS procurement or finance applications
  • 3+ years in modern integration patterns (APIs, event-driven architectures)
  • Hands-on experience managing configuration in a production SaaS environment, including testing, release management, and change control
  • Familiarity with enterprise ticketing tools (e.g., ServiceNow/Bytes, JIRA) and structured intake and prioritization processes
  • Experience translate requirements into structured configuration changes and document decisions
  • Strong analytical skills, attention to detail and data quality
  • Background in enterprise technology, finance systems, or shared services within a media or similar complex organization
