Why This Role Matters

 

The Washington Post is looking for a Senior Applied Machine Learning Scientist to lead the development of advanced AI/ML systems that power the next generation of journalism. This role will focus on Ask The Post, AI-powered search, retrieval, ranking, content understanding, and generative AI-powered reader experiences.

You will work at the intersection of generative AI, information retrieval, NLP, ranking, recommender systems, and experimentation to build intelligent systems that serve The Post’s journalism, readers, and business goals.

What Motivates You

  • You value world-class journalism and want to build technology that strengthens that mission.

  • You enjoy solving ambiguous, high-impact problems with practical AI/ML solutions.

  • You are excited by advances in generative AI, search, retrieval, ranking, and recommendation.

  • You communicate clearly, collaborate well, and thrive in a feedback-driven environment.

  • You are eager to learn, share, and apply the latest AI/ML techniques.

How You'll Support the Mission

  • Lead applied research and development for AI/ML systems across generative AI, search, retrieval, ranking, content understanding, and recommendation.

  • Formulate ambiguous product and business challenges as scientific problems with clear metrics, experiments, and success criteria.

  • Design, train, evaluate, and deploy advanced AI/ML models, including fine-tuned mid-range LLMs, dense and sparse embedding systems, VLMs, learning-to-rank models, agentic workflows, and efficient model-serving approaches for conversational search systems.

  • Build and improve AI-powered experiences such as Ask The Post, semantic search, content understanding, question answering, ranking, and intelligent discovery.

  • Design rigorous offline and online evaluations, including relevance evaluation, ranking metrics, retrieval quality, A/B testing, and causal analysis.

  • Develop scalable and efficient production ML systems with attention to latency, reliability, cost, monitoring, and maintainability.

  • Analyze large-scale behavioral, content, search, and interaction data to guide model and product improvements.

  • Collaborate with scientists, engineers, data teams, product managers, editors, and other business stakeholders to deliver impactful AI/ML solutions.

  • Provide technical leadership by shaping roadmaps, mentoring junior scientists and engineers, and promoting scientific rigor.

  • Communicate technical approaches, tradeoffs, results, and business impact to technical and non-technical audiences.

The Skills and Experience You Bring

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Machine Learning, or a related technical field.

  • 4+ years of experience in applied machine learning, AI, data science, information retrieval, NLP, recommender systems, or a related field.

  • Strong experience with Python and at least one ML framework such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX.

  • Experience designing, evaluating, and deploying ML models using large-scale datasets.

  • Strong foundation in machine learning, statistical analysis, experimental design, and model evaluation.

  • Experience with search, ranking, retrieval, NLP, GenAI, or recommendation systems.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, Mathematics, Information Retrieval, NLP, or a related field.

  • Deep familiarity with modern ML architectures, including transformer-based models, embedding models, two-tower architectures, LLMs, VLMs, and their applications in large-scale search, retrieval, ranking, and recommender systems.

  • Hands-on experience building production systems for semantic search, retrieval-augmented generation, question answering, ranking, content understanding, recommendation, or GenAI-powered products.

  • Experience with AWS, GCP, Spark, Beam, BigQuery, or similar cloud and big-data technologies.

  • Experience with LLM/VLM evaluation, model calibration, uncertainty estimation, interpretability, responsible AI, or production model optimization.

  • Experience with deep learning, reinforcement learning, multi-armed bandits, causal inference, or learning-to-rank methods.

  • Publications, patents, open-source contributions, or technical talks in AI/ML, NLP, information retrieval, recommender systems, GenAI, or related areas.

job.description:
Application Instructions

Please list all professional experience and explain any gaps in employment history. All of your application materials, which may include PDF files of work samples and/or links to audio, video, photography or graphics, must be uploaded to the field labeled Resume/Cover Letter/Work Samples to be considered for the position.


Join the future of news

We’re on a mission to deliver riveting storytelling for all of America. At The Washington Post, you’ll help reinvent news. Our work is driven by a deep investigative spirit and enhanced by innovation to bring audiences closer to the stories that matter most.


About Our Team


The Washington Post is powered by the passion and talent of our people. It takes all of us to reinvent news. Beyond our award-winning News and Opinions teams, we work across many departments, including Brand & Events, Communications, Customer Care, Engineering & Product, Finance, Human Resources, Legal, Marketing & Advertising, Print Operations, and Sales.


Why This Role Matters

 

The Washington Post is seeking an experienced, imaginative and highly collaborative Senior Photo Assignment Editor to help lead photographic coverage across the newsroom.


We are looking for a visual journalist with exceptional news judgment, sophisticated visual taste and a deep understanding of how photography can distinguish and elevate journalism. This editor will help shape coverage from the earliest stages — identifying stories with strong visual potential, commissioning photographers with distinctive perspectives and ensuring that photography is integral to how our journalism is conceived, reported and presented.


The ideal candidate understands that powerful photography depends not only on what we commission and publish, but also on how audiences experience that work. They will think critically about image selection, sequencing, cropping and presentation and understand how those choices should evolve across mobile and desktop experiences, social platforms, newsletters and other destinations.


This editor should be equally comfortable directing photographic coverage of a major breaking-news event, developing an ambitious visual enterprise project and collaborating across disciplines to determine the strongest form for a story. As a senior member of the Photo department, they will also provide leadership and mentorship to photo editors, helping elevate the ambition, creativity and quality of The Post’s visual journalism.


This position is based in our Washington, D.C., newsroom and will include some evening and weekend shifts to meet deadlines and respond to breaking news.


What Motivates You:

  • You believe photography can reveal dimensions of a story that words alone cannot capture.
  • You have a sophisticated visual sensibility and are constantly looking for original approaches to familiar subjects.
  • You thrive on the urgency of breaking news as well as the opportunity to develop ambitious visual enterprise.
  • You enjoy working closely with photographers and helping them produce distinctive, surprising work.
  • You think deeply about how audiences experience photography across different platforms and formats.
  • You are energized by mentoring visual journalists and helping raise the creative ambition of a team.

How You’ll Support the Mission:

  • Assign, commission and edit photography for breaking news, daily coverage, features, investigations and ambitious visual enterprise.
  • Develop and pitch original photographic story ideas, including journalism conceived from the outset around the strengths of photography.
  • Identify visual opportunities early in the reporting process and work with reporters and editors across the newsroom to develop strong approaches.
  • Direct photographers in the field, providing clear editorial guidance while creating the conditions for distinctive and original work.
  • Apply exceptional visual and news judgment to image selection, sequencing, cropping and presentation.
  • Make thoughtful decisions about how photography should be experienced across mobile, desktop, social platforms, newsletters and other digital destinations.
  • Cultivate a broad and diverse network of freelance photographers and match photographers to assignments based on subject matter, geography, approach and visual sensibility.
  • Research, source and license photography when commissioned work is not appropriate, applying rigorous standards around accuracy, context, copyright, provenance and ethics.
  • Collaborate with News Design, Graphics, Audience, Product and other teams to determine the most effective visual form and presentation for major journalism.
  • Help develop visual approaches to breaking and planned coverage that take advantage of photography alongside video, graphics, text and other forms.
  • Stay current with changes in photography, visual culture, digital publishing, technology and audience behavior and apply that knowledge thoughtfully to coverage.
  • Experiment with new approaches to photographic storytelling and presentation while maintaining rigorous standards for accuracy, ethics and craft.
  • Mentor photo editors and photographers, providing constructive feedback and helping colleagues develop their editorial judgment and visual storytelling skills.
  • Contribute to department-wide coverage planning and help shape The Post’s broader approach to photography and visual journalism.

The Skills and Experiences You Bring:

  • At least seven years of professional journalism experience, including substantial experience assigning and editing photography in a fast-paced newsroom.
  • Exceptional visual and editorial judgment and a demonstrated record of producing distinctive photographic journalism.
  • Deep knowledge of contemporary photography and a broad network of staff and freelance photographers.
  • Experience directing visual coverage of breaking news as well as developing longer-term enterprise and feature photography.
  • Strong understanding of digital storytelling and how photography should be selected, edited and presented for different platforms and audiences.
  • A generous, curious and collaborative editing style, with an openness to experimentation and new approaches.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate across disciplines and to mentor and develop visual journalists.
  • Strong understanding of photographic ethics, sourcing, copyright and image provenance.
  • Ability to make confident decisions under deadline pressure while maintaining rigorous standards for accuracy and visual quality.
  • Fluency with professional photo-editing tools, including Photoshop and Photo Mechanic; familiarity with video and other digital publishing tools is a plus.
  • Flexibility to work some nights and weekends as news demands.

Interested candidates should upload a résumé, cover letter and portfolio or examples of relevant work to our jobs portal. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled, but those received by Oct. 9 will be prioritized. The cover letter should be addressed to Deputy Photo Department Head Olivier Laurent, Photo Department Head Robert Miller and Head of Visuals Soo-Jeong Kang.

job.title: Content Operations Specialist
job.description:
Content Operations Specialist

Overall Responsibilities

The Content Operations Specialist is responsible for managing and ensuring the technical and broadcast quality of all inbound and outbound content feeds, including video and audio signals, for live and recorded programming at Weather Group Television (WGT). This role combines responsibilities from media acquisitions and master control operations and longform content preparation for Entertainment Studios eight digital channels. As this position supports a 24x7 news/weather environment, candidates must have flexibility to work days, nights, overnights, weekends, and holidays as needed and without advance notice.

Specific Responsibilities

ESN - Network Content Operations

  • Review the next day’s list of “barter shows” and editing requirements.

  • Edit barter show segments for two channels, match file titles, segment lengths, and proper transmission standards.  

  • Make necessary adjustments and verify all file segments for final delivery and playback.

  • Review playlists and associated content for missing segments or other incomplete assets

  • Purge older content files, per policy and procedures.

  • Verify all assets for all channels' playlists are correct and ready for playback

  • Verify timing for all playlists for the current day/weekend days.  

  • Communicate playlist or file issues to the appropriate internal or external partner and work toward a solution prior to air time. 

  • Process dub list for promotional/commercial assets

  • Upload/download files to/from the assigned storage repository (local or cloud)

WGT - MEDIA ACQUISITIONS

  • Ensure broadcast quality of all inbound/outbound video and audio feeds using scopes, analyzers, and level monitoring equipment.

  • Monitor multiple networks for high-standard quality control and report technical issues to appropriate departments.

  • Operate video/audio/L-Band routers, route remote feeds, and perform corrective actions to maintain broadcast signal integrity.

  • Manage content acquisition platforms, including LiveU, Dejero, TVU, LTN, and The Switch.

  • Use newsroom content systems to manage recordings and elements for live broadcasts.

  • Coordinate remote resources (IRDs, encoders, and format converters), adjusting levels and troubleshooting in real time.

  • Operate playout automation across networks to edit, load, and update playlists for live programming.

  • Perform daily checks on critical broadcast gear to maintain industry standards and proactively resolve system issues.

  • Utilize technical software tools, including FTP clients, satellite/scheduling software, MAM, MS Office, and Google Workspace.

TWC - MASTER CONTROL OPERATION

  • Responsible for editing, loading, and monitoring The Weather Channel (TWC) playlist using the automation systems.  

  • Work with Editorial and Programming teams to alter the playlist, within approved guidelines to maintain operational “on-air” continuity. 

  • Monitor multiple TWC feeds (uplinks, downlinks, STAR feeds, etc.) and those of other Allen Media & Entertainment Studios networks. 

  •  Provide Tier 1 technical support to internal technical teams by reporting/requesting Engineering  / IT assistance.   

  • Work closely with Engineering on any signal issues, alarms, or technical issues related to monitored network feeds. 

  • Perform operational checks, monitor video/audio quality, and proactively resolve system defects or failures.

  • Maintain shift logs, outage notifications, service request forms, and operational documentation.

  • Communicate status updates and repair workflows with management, engineering teams, and MCR clients.

  • Participate in technical training and adapt to changing operational demands.

Education, Experience, Certification Requirements

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Broadcasting, Communications, a related technical field, or equivalent work experience.

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in news environments, teleport operations, cable, or national broadcast environments.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Ability to communicate professionally with multiple internal technical teams and external vendors. 

  • Strong multitasking and organizational skills, with the ability to manage time effectively and operational resources in a dynamic, 24/7 environment with critical deadlines.

  • Comprehensive knowledge of satellite news gathering (SNG) processes, digital satellite equipment, waveform and vector scopes, and spectrum analyzers.

  • Understanding of broadcast automation systems and how to monitor signal workflow for troubleshooting

  • Experience understanding file formats, including codecs, wrappers, and technical specs

  • Proficiency in HDTV, SDI, ASI, and IP formats, as well as conversion technologies

  • Experience with electronic news/field gathering, teleport, and satellite truck operations, including ingest operations, is desired.

  • Strong troubleshooting skills, with the ability to respond quickly to technical issues and implement solutions under operational constraints.

  • Ability to interact effectively and collaboratively across departments and with management, maintaining professional communication with internal and external stakeholders.

  • Sensitivity to the unique needs and challenges of a 24/7 operation, ensuring operational continuity and quality.

  • Ability to work in a project and live broadcast environment simultaneously

  • Basic understanding of closed captions, including formats and regulations.

Behavior Requirements

  • Unquestionably high ethical standards

  • Customer-focused and team player mentality

  • Flexible and adaptable attitude in an ever-changing environment

  • Ability to get along well with others, willing and able to deal with a diverse cultural & customer base in numerous types of challenging situations

  • Interest in learning as well as teaching and developing skills in others

  • Strong teamwork and problem-solving skills

  • Willingness to work in a team environment or on individual projects on an as-needed basis

  • Ability to interact effectively “horizontally” through Weather Group TV and Allen Media as needed, working closely and collaboratively with multiple departments and management


Physical Requirements

  • Will be required to sit in a chair from 2-5 hours at a time

  • Will be required to view multiple computer documents and video images on multiple screens and/or listen to multiple audio sources simultaneously

  • Must be able to lift and move equipment as required

  • May be required to carry a laptop.


Equal Opportunity

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

job.title: Weather Producer
job.description:
Position Summary

The Weather Producer has editorial and meteorological responsibility and accountability for all weather content included in one of TWCs programs or
dayparts. They will ensure that each show covers relevant weather events through compelling stories and that those stories are told in the proper order
with visual components that are both accurate and meet (or exceed) TWC standards and style. The weather producer will work closely with on-camera
meteorologists to ensure that their weather storytelling is well-organized, well-prepared, and includes language that connects most effectively with our
target television audience(s). The Weather Producer will also be responsible for creating and updating daily weather graphics to support
TWC programming.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Conceive of and create new weather and science-based stories for the assigned program or day part
  • Stay aware of current meteorological pattern and contribute stories to the weather-content editorial process
  • Drive the inclusion and prioritization of weather stories in the assigned program or day part, creates graphics, and /or commissions the creation and/or acquisition of supporting visual content.
  • Mine all available resources, including social media, for possible weather story ideas & content
  • Coordinate with show producers and fellow weather producers to assure continuity in weather storytelling
  • Prepare content using multiple graphic platforms including TruVu Max, Google Earth, Vizrt, and Gibson Ridge
  • Produce weather blocks that are well-organized, well prepared and targets a television audience
  • Maintain proficiency with software changes to TruVu Max and other graphics systems. Ensure that TWC is first-to-air visually and verbally with all breaking weather information
  • Support coverage of significant weather events, including working extra hours and days outside of normally scheduled shifts
  • Create weather graphics that are meteorologically correct and tell an engaging weather story.

Education, Experience, Certification Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in meteorology, atmospheric science, design, or a related field
  • 3 years of meteorological experience to include 3 years of television or graphics building experience
  • 1 year experience using TruVu Max weather systems

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Extensive knowledge and understanding of TruVu Max weather systems
  • Thorough comprehension of numerical models 
  • Strong ability to communicate orally and verbally.  Ability to disseminate complex meteorological information in a useable and understandable manner
  • Possesses exceptional interpersonal and teamwork skills
  • Knowledge of social media and its role in the information and content gathering process
  • Ability to manage multiple projects, involving cross-functional teams, in an efficient manner
  • Exhibits creative problem solving skills and unique resourcefulness in order to complete tasks
  • Quickly learns and applies new technologies
  • Customer focused, innovative, and self-motivated
  • Receives feedback constructively and incorporates that feedback into work products and performance
  • Good multitasking and trouble-shooting skills
  • Displays strong collaborative skills and works effectively through conflict
  • Maintains high standards for product, performance, and ethics
  • Effectively contributes to team goals within a highly interactive, and at times, stressful environment
  • Dependable and flexible in a 24x7 operational environment
  • Experience using augmented reality production pipelines a plus
  • Experience using Photoshop, AfterEffects, and 3D modeling software is a plus

job.description:
Description

  

About Us:

Weigel Broadcasting Co. is a family-owned media company based in Chicago, Illinois. The company owns and operates national television networks, as well as local broadcast stations throughout the country. Weigel is a leader in broadcast television with MeTV, Memorable Entertainment Television, the number one rated classic TV entertainment network, as well as the Catchy Comedy Network, the H&I - Heroes & Icons Network, the Story Television Network and WEST- Western Entertainment Series Television Network, plus the Movies! Network in cooperation with the Fox Television Stations, the Start TV Network and the Dabl Network in association with the CBS Television Stations, and the MeTV Toons Network in collaboration with Warner Bros. Weigel is the creator of the nationally syndicated music format MeTV FM. For more information on Weigel, visit: https://www.weigelbroadcasting.com/.


Brand Director:

Weigel Broadcasting in Chicago, IL is seeking an exceptional leader to drive promotional strategy and creative production across the Weigel networks.


About the Role 

· Collaborate with leadership to align creative strategy with ratings and brand growth objectives

· Maintain and evolve creative standards, workflows, and best practices across the department
 

What You’ll Do 

· Demonstrate detailed knowledge of Weigel network’s brand identities, ensuring consistency across all consumer touchpoints

· Manage all aspects of the Promotions team assignments, deadlines and performance

· Partner cross-functionally to coordinate on log formatting needs and timelines, ensuring consistent consumer awareness and promotion across the networks

· Write, produce, and edit quality creative material for Weigel’s platforms, setting the standard related to the brand presentation of the Weigel networks

· Provide your team with feedback and guidance on all aspects of day-to-day tasks and core job functions

· Align with the VP of Network Marketing on assisting in shaping seasonal, tentpole, franchise, and network-wide promotional initiatives

· Spearhead recruiting, developing, and retaining top creative talent

· Perform additional duties as assigned

· Management experience with an emphasis on top to bottom execution from inception to delivery on all tasks assigned to you and your team

· Strong editorial judgment and attention to brand consistency

· Must have strong leadership skills

About the Team

The Enterprise Subscriptions team at Dow Jones focuses on growing and managing business-to-business (B2B) subscriptions across Dow Jones's premium news brands and products. The team partners with corporations, universities, and other organizations to provide employees, students, and members with access to trusted news, data, and insights from brands such as The Wall Street Journal, Barron's, MarketWatch, and Investor's Business Daily. The organization works closely across sales, marketing, product, customer success, data and insights to drive subscriber growth, engagement, retention, and revenue while identifying new opportunities to expand Dow Jones's enterprise footprint. Enterprise News is a key growth area for Dow Jones, with the broader Enterprise business also including Factiva and Dow Jones Newswires.

About the Role

As the Account Manager, Corporate Subscriptions, you will manage and grow corporate subscription accounts within your assigned territory. You will serve as a strategic partner to clients, ensuring subscription renewals, driving new revenue, and maximizing client value. You will be part of the Sales & Account/Client Management team.


You Will:

  • Act as a trusted advisor, maintain regular communication with customers.
  • Generate and qualify leads through networking, cold-calling, and inbound marketing  efforts

  • Conduct virtual and in-person meetings with clients to establish relationships and drive new opportunities into pipeline
  • Manage pipeline via Salesforce
  • Provide training, resources, and best practices to maximize adoption
  • Address customer concerns and challenges proactively to drive future retention and growth
  • Achieve individual revenue targets

  • Advocate for customers internally by work with product, support and marketing teams
  • Use platforms such as Salesforce and other sales-related resources to track health of sales pipeline
  • Stay up-to-date on Dow Jones suite of enterprise subscription solutions

You Have:

  • Strong ability to build and maintain relationships with clients
  • Experience acting as a trusted advisor to ensure customers maximize the value of the product
  • Ability to stay up-to-date on product offerings (Dow Jones enterprise subscription solutions)

job.title: Administrative Assistant, Opinion
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

The Wall Street Journal is a global news organization that provides leading news, information, commentary and analysis. The Wall Street Journal engages readers across print, digital, mobile, social, podcast and video. Building on its heritage as the preeminent source of global business and financial news, the Journal includes coverage of U.S. & world news, politics, arts, culture, lifestyle, sports, and health. It holds 38 Pulitzer Prizes for outstanding journalism. The Wall Street Journal is published by Dow Jones, a division of News Corp (Nasdaq: NWS, NWSA; ASX: NWS, NWSLV).

 

The WSJ Opinion section has long served as a forum for intelligent, values-driven commentary, dedicated to advocating a consistent philosophy that can be summed up as ‘free markets, free people.’ While we aim to persuade, every word we publish is the product of rigorous reporting, research and debate. WSJ Opinion offers sharp, original analysis and strong points of view on the news of the day. This position will support the daily operation of the opinion section.

 

About the Role:

The Wall Street Journal’s Opinion section is looking for a New York-based administrative assistant to help support our team’s excellent journalism. This person would work closely with other members of the support staff team on multiple daily administrative duties, clerical tasks and ad hoc projects as needed in order to keep the department’s operations running smoothly. This role will also support the Editorial Features editor and the Free Expression editor, along with their respective teams. Responsibilities include handling administrative, clerical and financial tasks, such as processing freelance contributor invoices and managing freelance contracts.

We’re looking for a collaborative team player with a proactive, positive “can do” attitude, a strong work ethic and demonstrated administrative experience. This person should be an effective communicator who is excited about partnering with experienced and dedicated administrative colleagues to maintain a strong level of support for the Opinion section’s daily operations. This position is based in our New York office.

 

You Will:

  • Assist Business Manager with office administration projects and basic support of business operations for Opinion, such as answering department phone calls, document scanning and printing, equipment maintenance, supplies, onboarding and offboarding of employees, coordinating IT requests, etc. 
  • Assist the Editorial Features and Free Expression teams with invoice and contract management, purchase orders, correspondence, calendar management, travel booking, assisting editors with expense report preparation, etc. 
  • Track freelance contributions for monthly and yearly financial reports.
  • Manage the onboarding of new freelance contributors’ payment information and compliance forms. 
  • Process freelance contributor payments and invoices in SAP.
  • Manage freelance contracts by using the Adobe Sign to send, track and retain agreement documents.
  • Assist the administrative team with sorting and delivering mail to the appropriate recipients in the office; open book galleys and review copies for the Books team; ship review copies to contributors.
  • Act as the department liaison with IT to support editors and writers in resolving technology issues.  
  • Communicate and collaborate with team members to ensure seamless maintenance of office operations. This requires backing up team members during scheduled and unscheduled time off and leaves.  

 

You Have:

  • 7+ years of proven administrative experience, including experience managing financial tasks, such as processing invoices, handling purchase orders, and tracking financial reports, and contract management
  • Undergraduate degree and/or equivalent work experience is preferred
  • Familiarity with WSJ Opinion is a plus
  • Knowledge of and interest in current events
  • Strong teamwork and collaboration skills are a must
  • Very detail-oriented with strong organizational skills
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Ability to prioritize jobs, manage time, and work independently 
  • Familiarity with using video conferencing 
  • Ability to communicate effectively and appropriately with a professional demeanor when dealing with VIP guests of the editorial board
  • Proficiency with administrative, financial, and contract management tools, including SAP, Concur, Excel, Adobe Sign, and G-Suite (Gmail, Google Calendar scheduling, Google Drive, Google Docs & Sheets, etc.)

Our Benefits

job.title: Assistant General Counsel - Newsroom
job.description:
Job Description:

About the Team

 

The Legal department has deep expertise across the core practice areas relevant to a global media and information company, including commercial agreements, privacy, intellectual property, employment, litigation, compliance, corporate governance, M&A, and media law. The team partners closely with business leaders across Dow Jones to provide practical, commercially focused advice that supports growth, manages risk, and enables sound decision-making.

 

About the Role

 

Dow Jones is seeking an Assistant General Counsel based in New York City to focus on newsroom counseling and litigation as part of its media law team. 

 

This role will provide timely, practical, and solution-oriented legal advice on defamation, privacy, copyright, court access & freedom of information, and other matters of concern to the journalists across Dow Jones, including The Wall Street Journal, Dow Jones Newswires, Barron’s, MarketWatch, Mansion Global, Financial News, and Investor’s Business Daily.

 

The successful candidate will work with the other members of the media law team as a trusted adviser to reporters and editors, with a shared commitment to publishing impactful journalism while managing legal risks. This is an opportunity for a strategic thinker who thrives in a fast-paced environment and enjoys partnering with clients, while maintaining a superior work ethic, fastidious attention to detail, exceptional organizational skills, and a dedication to ethics and professional responsibility.

 

This role will report to the SVP, Associate General Counsel, who sits in New York City.

 

This is a hybrid role, with three (3) days per week required in our midtown Manhattan headquarters.

 

You Will:

  • Review articles, videos, podcasts and other materials for legal concerns prior to publication
  • Advise reporters and editors on legal issues in the newsgathering process
  • Lead training sessions on media law topics and collaborate with editors on other trainings
  • Investigate pre- and post-publication complaints and provide related advice
  • Respond to threats of litigation 
  • Collaborate on journalist safety issues, including legal advice on risk assessments and helping to address incidents
  • Collaborate closely with internal colleagues and outside counsel (where engaged) on newsroom-related litigation, including reviewing and drafting filings and managing responses to discovery requests, subpoenas, etc.
  • Respond to subpoenas related to newsgathering materials
  • Help negotiate freelance contributor agreements, data use agreements, and other contracts in support of the Dow Jones newsrooms
  • Advise on advertising issues
  • Advise other parts of the business on issues of concern to the newsroom
  • Assist with Dow Jones’s general litigation portfolio, in the U.S. and abroad 

You Have:

  • Juris Doctor (JD) degree from an accredited law school. Currently admitted to the New York bar as an active member in good standing or qualified to register as in-house counsel in accordance with New York rules.
  • At least 8 years of relevant legal experience, with significant in-house experience strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience handling media law matters
  • Strong understanding of libel law, privacy, fair use, access to information and other media law issues 
  • Excellent research and communication skills (written and oral), with strong judgment and attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment and exercise sound judgment in setting priorities.
  • Experience managing matters from investigation or pre-litigation demand through resolution or formal proceedings.
  • A high degree of initiative, accountability, and self-motivation, with the ability to work both independently and collaboratively.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build credibility with stakeholders across functions and levels of seniority.
  • A practical, business-oriented mindset and the confidence to advise senior leaders on complex issues with clarity and discretion.
  • Commitment to ethics, professionalism, and high-quality legal work.

job.title: Chief of Staff to Dow Jones Energy General Manager
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

Dow Jones Energy delivers trusted price transparency, benchmarks, analytics, news, and insights across the global energy, chemicals, metals, and fuel supply value chains. Our offerings support institutional investors, analysts, and traders navigating spot, wholesale, and retail markets, as well as emerging segments tied to the global energy transition.


Through authoritative data, real-time intelligence, and deep market expertise, Dow Jones Energy enables financial professionals to mitigate risk and make high-stakes commercial decisions in volatile, fast-evolving global markets.




About the Role:

As Vice President - Business Strategy for Dow Jones Energy, you will report to the General Manager (GM) of Energy, and manage functions essential to their productivity, as well as the productivity of the broader Dow Jones Energy leadership team. 


You will serve as a versatile right-hand to the GM, be her point person on a day-to-day basis, and foster strong relationships with the leadership team members who report to her - ensuring that growth initiatives are implemented successfully. You will be aware of activity throughout the business, clearly communicate information and actions from the GM, and act as a proxy on her behalf with various stakeholders, including sometimes the Executive Leadership Team members, to maximize performance and output.


You will work in our midtown Manhattan office every weekday.



You Will:
  • Manage key priorities of the GM and Head of Strategy & Business Operations; and serve as the primary point of contact for all executive initiatives
  • Manage the operating rhythm for the business in collaboration with the Energy Leadership Team and finance partners to ensure alignment on strategy and goals
  • Develop client engagement strategy for the GM in alignment with business priorities
  • Provide priority management and oversight for the the GM
  • Attend meetings with GM/Head of S&BO, taking notes, and facilitating takeaways
  • Review, draft, and manage responses to emails, ensuring timely follow-ups and effective communication on behalf of the GM
  • Demonstrate solid understanding of Dow Jones’ core business and strategic plan; regularly promote the GM’s vision to the broader team to ensure alignment and productivity
  • Execute on the vision through tight management of strategic, high-growth projects that are cross-department and cross-brand
  • Manage change management programs in collaboration with the Leadership team
  • Facilitate decision-making with the GM and Energy leadership team; act as confidant and advisor to offer sound perspective and guidance
  • Instill a sense of teamwork and loyalty within the broader team to inspire and motivate others around growth initiatives; act as “eyes and ears” to ensure such initiatives are implemented effectively
  • Travel to meetings with the GM or her representative 
  • Oversee a team of executive assistants and assist them with their career development and work capacity




You Have:
  • Willingness to work on-site in our midtown Manhattan office Monday through Friday
  • Minimum 15 years’ professional experience - including cross-functional leadership roles and/or in operations, strategy or management consulting
  • Experience working closely with executive leaders

job.title: Chief of Staff to the CTO
job.description:
Job Description:



About the Team: 

Our Technology team drives the evolution of our Technology, Engineering, Data, Product and User Experience functions. With a keen focus on delivering cutting-edge solutions, we shape the digital landscape for our customers, readers and users. From revolutionizing visuals to optimizing tools and harnessing the power of data, mobile, video and social platforms, our team is committed to providing a seamless and immersive experience across all touchpoints. Collaborating closely with our newsrooms and strategic partners, we spearhead the development of groundbreaking products and technologies. 


About the Role: 


As the Chief of Staff to the CTO, you will serve as the trusted advisor and strategic proxy to the Chief Technology Officer, shaping the vision, operations, and execution of the Office of the CTO (OCTO). Acting as a strategic owner and key decision maker, you will lead the OCTO team to drive operational excellence across our global Technology organization while contributing to complex strategic initiatives; such as enterprise-wide AI enablement or platform migrations. Reporting directly to the CTO, you will navigate high-level organizational design, negotiate and compromise with internal and external parties to accept new concepts, and drive cross-functional alignment between Technology, Functional, and Business leaders. 


You Will: 

- Drive Strategy & Planning: Partner with the CTO and Tech Leadership to define long-term vision, technology strategy, and OKR frameworks. Act as a strategic owner to lead change management, organizational design, and execution for major strategic initiatives. 


- Act as Strategic Proxy: Serve as the trusted advisor and proxy to the CTO, making critical decisions, providing guidance, and representing the CTO in meetings with cross-functional and C-level stakeholders. 


- Ensure Executive Readiness: Think two steps ahead to anticipate the CTO’s needs, proactively providing strategic advice, briefings, and talking points to ensure they are prepared for all high-profile meetings and events, or issues and critical decisions. 


- Lead Complex Programs: Manage large, complex project initiatives of strategic importance involving large cross-functional teams. Conceptualize and create novel solutions and systems that improve the competitive position of the organization. 


- Run the OCTO Operation: Design, oversee, and continuously automate the operating cadences, executive reporting, and governance models for the Technology organization.

Manage Tech Exec staff meetings, OCEO reporting, communications channels, and optimize workflows to ensure the leadership team functions efficiently at scale.


- Drive Operational Excellence: Implement data-driven performance metrics, streamline internal processes, identify productivity savings across the Technology organization, and oversee technology budget planning processes. 


- Lead Culture & Executive Communications: Communicate with and influence senior executive leadership regarding matters of strategic importance. Direct internal Technology communications (e.g., Tech Pulse blog, Intranet Hub, global Check-Ins) and engagement initiatives. Negotiate and compromise with internal and external parties to accept new approaches. 


- Build and Develop the OCTO Team: Lead, develop, and expand the Office of the CTO team. Provide guidance, coaching, and training to employees across the Company within your area of expertise. 

You Have: 

- Minimum 15+ years of experience in a fast-paced technology, product management, or strategy operations environment. 

- Deep expertise in driving complex, cross-functional initiatives (e.g., enterprise AI integrations, strategic transformations, or organizational change) and translating business goals into actionable technology OKRs. 

- Proven capability to build, manage, and scale high-performing operational teams and establish data-driven operational cadences (e.g., OCEO reporting, automated playbooks, standard operating procedures). 

- Demonstrated experience serving as a key decision maker and proxy to C-suite executives, successfully managing multi-million dollar technology budgets and influencing across complex, matrixed environments. 

- Experience solving extremely difficult problems, utilizing significant conceptualizing and reasoning to improve existing processes or create novel systems that drive competitive advantage. 

- Ability to work in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, balancing multiple priorities at once, while maintaining professionalism and calm. 

- Preferred Product Management, Technology or Consulting background. - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business Administration or equivalent experience.

job.title: Client Engagement Specialist
job.description:
Job Description:

About the Team:

At Dow Jones, we empower global organizations to navigate an increasingly volatile world, where geopolitical shifts, financial crime, regulatory expansion and emerging AI technologies redefine risk every day. Powered by market-leading intelligence capabilities—including Dow Jones Risk & Compliance, Dragonfly, Oxford Analytica, Storyful, Dow Jones Risk Journal, Factiva and Dow Jones Newswires—we deliver the trusted insights our customers need to build resilience, protect their reputations and make mission-critical decisions with confidence.

About the Role:

The Client Engagement Specialist (CES) is responsible for managing all renewal aspects of the relationship with a defined set of customers. The Client Engagement Specialist is responsible for retaining the existing contract revenue within existing buying centers and supporting new sales into these accounts made by the Business Development Managers. 

 

To this end the Client Engagement Specialist will need to liaise with DJ internal teams to ensure the clients business needs are being met consistently to support the renewal. Ultimately the Client Engagement Specialist must develop and drive successful renewals ensuring a strong revenue base for Dow Jones. 

 

Success will be measured based on the retention rates of the Client Engagement Specialists assigned accounts.

You Will

Retention  

  • Responsible for owning the retention strategy for assigned Strategic accounts by building and executing a renewal plan
  • Proactively provide a clear picture to management by highlighting high risk renewal accounts and strategies to mitigate potential losses
  • Responsible for ensuring appropriate levels of customer training and product utilization by working with the Product Training Specialist team and monitoring internal CRM reports
  • Oversee the overall renewal lifecycle; from pricing and contracting alongside the Account Executive, to invoicing and client support, so customer concerns get addressed correctly and efficiently throughout the fiscal year
  • Support new sales into existing accounts to ensure maximum customer ROI with DJ
  • Support clients’s transitions from legacy tools to DJ upgrade platforms

 

Customer Knowledge

  • Know your customer including the development of good account understanding, business groups deriving value from DJ services, understanding the clients’ business/industry, competitor solutions they are using and the client’s current and developing needs
  • Understand how your clients derive value from DJ services/products, know the people involved including decision makers within those groups.
  • Serve as a client conduit internally for feedback and competitive intelligence to DJ Product, Content & Marketing.

Lead Generation

  • Where possible identify opportunities for increased revenue within the set of accounts (up-selling and possibly cross-selling) and work with other members of the sales team to follow through on such opportunities.

The CES must maintain accurate and appropriate client records within the Company’s systems. The CES will communicate with clients mainly via telephone and email.


You Have

job.title: Client Success Manager
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Role:

We are seeking a Client Success Manager to own the post-sale client journey for assigned new business accounts-  from signed deal through launch, activation, early adoption, and handoff into ongoing account management. This role serves as the primary relationship owner and cross-functional coordinator during the early post-sale phase, working closely with Sales, Regional Sales Coordinators, Operations, Adoption, Engagement, Customer Care, and Account Management.

The goal is a seamless transition from signed account to active, engaged client-  reducing friction, accelerating time to value, surfacing risk early, and bringing in the right specialist resources at the right time.

The Client Success Manager is the primary post-sale relationship owner and "quarterback" across the early client lifecycle, accountable for client readiness, launch coordination, onboarding progress, standard-account adoption execution, early engagement, and risk management. The role doesn't personally own every specialist workstream, but ensures each one happens successfully.

This is not a quota-carrying role. Success is measured by how effectively clients launch, activate, adopt key products and workflows, engage early, and transition cleanly into ongoing account management.

You Will:

Own the post-sale relationship and launch orchestration

  • Serve as the primary point of contact from signed deal through onboarding and early adoption.
  • Lead the handoff from Sales, ensuring client goals, use cases, stakeholders, and launch priorities are clearly understood and documented.
  • Build 60–90 day onboarding milestones and success plans so clients know what success looks like and can achieve early wins.
  • Maintain proactive, coordinated communication with clients and internal stakeholders to keep launches on track.

Coordinate account setup with Regional Sales Coordinators and Operations

  • Partner with RSCs on order processing, account setup/changes, billing, CRM updates, and related handoffs.
  • Partner with Operations and Fulfillment on provisioning, entitlements, technical readiness, SLA readiness, and launch execution.
  • Own coordination and follow-through, while RSCs and Operations retain responsibility for their own administrative execution.

Drive onboarding and adoption for standard accounts

  • Execute onboarding using established playbooks, milestones, and training guidance from the Adoption function.
  • Ensure clients understand activation steps and build early usage habits.
  • Loop in the Adoption Specialist for top-tier, high-risk, or complex accounts.

Partner with the Adoption Specialist on strategy and high-touch accounts

  • Work within playbooks and frameworks defined by the Adoption Specialist.
  • Coordinate specialist involvement for strategic accounts, complex launches, low-activation accounts, or accounts needing deeper admin enablement.
  • Apply Adoption function learnings and best practices across the client base.

Partner with Engagement and Lifecycle teams to deepen usage

  • Work with Engagement Strategy & Performance and Customer Lifecycle Marketing to ensure clients get the right communications, campaigns, and enablement programs.
  • Use engagement reporting and health signals to prioritize interventions.
  • Connect clients to the right in-life programs as they move from onboarding into sustained engagement.

Monitor account health and manage risk

  • Track usage, activation milestones, and health signals to catch stalled onboarding, weak adoption, or early churn risk.
  • Escalate early and coordinate support across Adoption, Engagement, Customer Care, Operations, and Account Management.
  • Ensure critical issues stay owned and teams stay aligned on actions and timing.

Act as the voice of the client internally

  • Share feedback, adoption insights, and emerging needs with Product, Marketing, Sales, Customer Care, and Client Success leadership.
  • Partner with the Enterprise Customer Care & Voice of Customer Lead on escalations and service themes.

Support a clean handoff into ongoing account management

  • Ensure a clear transition from early post-sale ownership into the ongoing account management motion once onboarding and early adoption are complete.
  • Share account context, progress, risks, and adoption status with Account Managers so momentum carries through on high-value accounts.

Success Measures

Measured on adoption, engagement, readiness, and handoff outcomes rather than direct revenue. KPIs may include:

  • Account launch readiness and setup completion rate
  • Time to onboarding completion and time to first value
  • Activation and seat activation rate
  • Adoption of priority products, workflows, and features
  • Usage frequency, engagement depth, and health score movement
  • Participation in training, webinars, and lifecycle programs
  • Early identification and escalation of churn risk or stalled onboarding
  • Quality of handoff into ongoing account management

Cross-Functional Partnerships

  • Sales Account Executives — post-sale handoff and continuity from signed deal into launch
  • Regional Sales Coordinators — order processing, account setup/changes, billing coordination
  • Operations and Fulfillment — provisioning, entitlements, technical readiness, launch execution
  • Adoption Specialists — onboarding strategy, playbooks, training, high-touch support
  • Engagement Strategy & Performance / Customer Lifecycle Marketing — health monitoring, engagement plays, in-life programs
  • Enterprise Customer Care & Voice of Customer — escalations, white-glove service, feedback loops
  • Account Managers — transition planning and ongoing relationship continuity

You Have:

  • 5 years of experience in client success, onboarding, implementation, account coordination, or related post-sale roles in B2B, SaaS, media, or subscription environments
  • Strong cross-functional project management skills, able to coordinate multiple stakeholders through launch, onboarding, and adoption milestones
  • Excellent client communication, relationship-building, and stakeholder management skills
  • Comfort using data and health indicators to monitor trends and flag risk early
  • A proactive, organized, solutions-oriented approach to client coordination
  • A client-first mindset focused on driving value through usage, adoption, and engagement — not transactional account support

Our Benefits

  • Robust medical, vision, and dental insurance
  • Generous paid personal time and vacation
  • Savings and retirement planning options
  • Extensive health coverage for individuals and families
  • Tuition assistance and educational development support
  • Paid leave for new parents
  • Resources for family and dependent care
  • Commuting/public transit support
  • Preferred pricing on corporate subscriptions
  • Employee referral incentives

job.title: Compensation Operations Specialist
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

The People team at Dow Jones is dedicated to attracting, developing, and retaining

world-class talent that drives our mission forward. As strategic partners, we provide

comprehensive support across the entire employee lifecycle. Our team includes Talent

Acquisition, Talent Management, People Business Partners, Compensation, HR

Operations, Workplace, and Security—all working together to create an exceptional

employee experience. We champion a culture of inclusion, innovation, and excellence,

ensuring our people have the resources, support, and opportunities they need to thrive

and do their best work.


About the Role:

Dow Jones is hiring a Compensation Operations Specialist to join our People Team in

New York City. Reporting to the Compensation Director, this position combines

compensation analysis with core HR operations oversight. In this role, you will drive the

evolution of the Compensation function by simplifying processes, improving data and

systems, and leveraging automation and technology to make compensation programs

more efficient, scalable, and employee- and business-friendly.


You Will:

● Lead compensation operations and cross-functional processes, ensuring

accurate data, consistent execution, strong controls, and seamless

administration across HR systems.

● Identify opportunities to streamline and automate compensation processes,

evaluating existing workflows to eliminate manual work, reduce process friction,

improve accuracy, and create more scalable solutions.

● Apply creative problem-solving to complex operational challenges, exploring

alternative approaches, challenging existing ways of working, and developing

practical solutions that improve efficiency, accuracy, and scalability.

● Proactively identify opportunities to rethink how compensation processes are

designed and delivered, leveraging technology, cross-functional collaboration,

and innovative approaches to address recurring issues and emerging business

needs.

● Project manage key Compensation initiatives and annual cycles, coordinating

timelines, requirements, stakeholder alignment, testing, communications, and

execution across the People Team.

● Partner closely with HRIS to optimize Workday and other compensation-related

systems, translating business requirements into system enhancements, workflow

improvements, and automation opportunities.

● Develop and maintain compensation processes, documentation, controls, and

operating procedures, ensuring clear ownership and consistent execution across

the organization.

● Build and maintain reporting and tracking that provides visibility into

compensation activity, process performance, workload, data quality, and key

operational metrics.

● Partner with Compensation, HRBPs/PBPs, Payroll, Talent Acquisition, Finance,

and People Operations to resolve operational issues and improve end-to-end

compensation processes.

● Support the administration of compensation programs, including annual salary

planning, incentive programs, promotions, market adjustments, recognition, and

other compensation processes.

● Identify opportunities to leverage AI and emerging technologies to simplify

compensation processes, improve the employee and manager experience, and

enable the Compensation team to operate more efficiently.

● Supervise and mentor one Compensation Coordinator, providing direction on

day-to-day compensation operations, data validation, HRIS maintenance,

reporting, and other operational activities.


You Have:

● 7 to 10 years of prior experience in compensation, HR operations, or a closely

related generalist role within an enterprise environment.

● Proven track record of managing compensation routines, auditing HR data, and

identifying workflow automations.

● Strong project management capabilities with experience leading major HR

programs from planning through execution.

● Direct or indirect leadership experience guiding junior team members or

operational coordinators.

● Advanced proficiency in Excel and HRIS platforms (ideally Workday, or similar

enterprise HR databases).

● An undergraduate degree in Human Resources, Business Administration,

Finance, or a related field of study, or equivalent experience.

job.title: Executive Director - Chemical Markets Price Reporting
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Role:

As Executive Director - Chemical Markets Price Reporting, you will lead Dow Jones Energy's global chemicals price reporting business. You will oversee the editorial teams responsible for the assessment and publication of benchmark prices, assessments and market-moving news across global petrochemical and chemical markets from our PCW brand.

You ensure the integrity, quality, transparency, and market relevance of chemical price assessments while maintaining the highest ethical and methodological standards. You will lead a global team of price reporters and editors responsible for market coverage across key chemical value chains - including aromatics, olefins, plastics, polymers, syngas, methanol, feedstocks, and emerging chemical markets.

You will drive editorial excellence, benchmark innovation, and market engagement, while ensuring compliance with legal requirements and industry standards. You will partner closely with Product, Standards & Compliance, Risk, and other Editorial leaders to ensure Dow Jones Energy's chemicals assessments remain trusted, transparent, and indispensable to global commodity markets.

You will report to the SVP - Markets & Price Reporting.

About the Team:

Dow Jones Energy delivers trusted price transparency, benchmarks, analytics, news, and insights across the global energy, chemicals, metals, and fuel supply value chains. Our offerings support institutional investors, analysts, and traders navigating spot, wholesale, and retail markets, as well as emerging segments tied to the global energy transition.

Through authoritative data, real-time intelligence, and deep market expertise, Dow Jones Energy enables financial professionals to mitigate risk and make high-stakes commercial decisions in volatile, fast-evolving global markets.

You Will:

  • Lead and develop a global team of chemicals price reporters, editors, and market specialists, fostering a culture of editorial excellence, accountability, and collaboration

  • Ensure all chemical market assessments are developed, maintained, and published in accordance with the highest standards of price assessment integrity, market transparency, governance, and ethical conduct consistent with Dow Jones’ and The Wall Street Journal’s values

  • Lead methodology development, periodic methodology reviews, market consultations, and stakeholder engagement processes to ensure pricing methodologies remain robust, representative, and responsive to evolving market dynamics

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with producers, consumers, traders, brokers, exchanges, trade associations, and other market participants to strengthen market engagement, data integrity, and confidence in Dow Jones Energy's petrochemical and chemical markets assessments

  • Partner with Standards & Compliance, Legal, and Risk teams to ensure ongoing compliance with applicable benchmark regulations, internal controls, audit requirements, and governance frameworks

  • Partner with Product to execute the strategic roadmap for global chemicals market coverage, including identifying opportunities for new benchmarks, market expansion, and portfolio optimization

  • Monitor benchmark performance, market adoption, customer feedback, and competitive developments - recommending changes to methodologies, coverage, and editorial priorities as appropriate

  • Recruit, develop, mentor, and retain high-performing editorial talent, ensuring appropriate succession planning, capability development, and organizational resilience across the chemicals price reporting organization

  • Act as a senior spokesperson and subject matter expert for chemicals markets, representing Dow Jones Energy at industry conferences, customer engagements, webinars, and regulatory forums

You Have:

  • 15+ years’ experience in commodity price reporting, market intelligence, or related information services organization

  • Deep knowledge of global chemicals and petrochemical markets, including physical market structures, trading practices, supply chains, and pricing mechanisms

  • Significant leadership experience managing geographically dispersed editorial, price reporting, or market analysis teams

  • Demonstrated experience developing, managing, or launching benchmark price assessments, methodologies, or market intelligence products

  • Strong understanding of IOSCO Principles for Oil Price Reporting Agencies and familiarity with benchmark regulation, governance, assurance, and audit requirements

  • Strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to cultivate relationships with senior leaders and external market participants

  • A university degree -OR- relevant professional experience

Dow Jones Energy delivers trusted price transparency, benchmarks, analytics, news, and insights across the global energy, chemicals, metals, and fuel supply value chains. job.title: Growth Strategy Editor, Free Expression
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

The Wall Street Journal is a global news organization that provides leading news, information, commentary and analysis. The Wall Street Journal engages readers across print, digital, mobile, social, podcast and video. Building on its heritage as the preeminent source of global business and financial news, the Journal includes coverage of U.S. & world news, politics, arts, culture, lifestyle, sports, and health. It holds 38 Pulitzer Prizes for outstanding journalism. The Wall Street Journal is published by Dow Jones, a division of News Corp (Nasdaq: NWS, NWSA; ASX: NWS, NWSLV).


The WSJ Opinion section has long served as a forum for intelligent, values-driven commentary, dedicated to advocating a consistent philosophy that can be summed up as 'free markets, free people.' While we aim to persuade, every word we publish is the product of rigorous reporting, research and debate. WSJ Opinion offers sharp, original analysis and strong points of view on the news of the day.


About the Role:

Free Expression is a daily newsletter on American life, politics, and culture from the Opinion pages of The Wall Street Journal. With over 100K highly engaged readers, we are looking for someone to build a direct audience relationship that starts with free reach and leads to paid value.

 

The Growth Strategy Editor will own the audience-growth strategy for the newsletter, with particular responsibility for turning Substack into a scalable engine for acquisition and engagement. The role sits where editorial, audience, product, marketing, and contributor development meet, and is accountable for reaching, converting, and retaining new audiences well beyond the existing WSJ ecosystem while protecting the editorial distinctiveness and credibility that set Free Expression apart. This role works in our NYC office.


You Will:

  • Own the Free Expression growth strategy — the plan, goals, and operating cadence for acquiring, engaging, converting, and retaining readers — building toward a target of roughly 2,500 net-new Substack readers per week.
  • Make Free Expression native to Substack: own the homepage, Notes, comments, recommendations, cross-promotion, and community, and use recommendation swaps, restacks, cross-posting, and contributor-led promotion to compound reach.
  • Test new distribution channels, partnerships, and audience segments, and turn what works into a repeatable playbook that can inform future Dow Jones newsletter products.
  • Partner with Opinion editors and writers to sharpen the newsletter’s anchor themes and point of view, give each edition a clear reason to run that day, and build recurring franchises and publishing rhythms readers learn to anticipate.
  • Identify high-potential contributors and help turn them into recognizable audience brands, with activation across bylines, promotion, community, audio, video, and live events.
  • Track performance across Substack, the newsletter, the site, and social — list growth, acquisition source, engagement, conversion, and churn — and run experiments that improve content, packaging, cadence, and promotion.
  • Judge growth by quality as well as volume, and work with analytics, product, marketing, and finance to connect audience gains to subscription outcomes, including the decision framework for a future paid model.

 

You Have:

  • Significant experience in audience development, newsletter growth, digital publishing, creator media, platform strategy, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience growing an audience on Substack or a comparable platform, with deep familiarity with its mechanics — recommendations, Notes, restacks, cross-promotion, comments, and community.
  • Strong editorial judgment, including the ability to distinguish content that is merely popular from content that builds a durable reader relationship.
  • Strong analytical skills and comfort working with audience data, dashboards, experimentation, and performance metrics.
  • The ability to work effectively across editorial, product, marketing, analytics, and commercial teams without formal authority.
  • Excellent writing, editing, packaging, and communication skills.
  • Experience developing contributor-, creator-, or talent-led franchises.
  • Experience connecting audience growth to subscription and retention outcomes.
  • A genuine interest in independent voices, ideas, debate, and the role of journalism in a free society.

job.title: Journalist
job.description:
Job Description:


Since 2010, Storyful’s newsroom has been working at the intersection of social media, news and technology to help media partners tell the stories that matter most. As we expand the breadth and depth of our coverage, we are seeking a news journalist to join our editorial team.


The ideal candidate will have an interest in finding compelling stories via social media, and in producing original reporting that uses cutting-edge verification and open-source intelligence techniques. They will be at home in a fast-paced, video-led, breaking news environment, and able to serve a diverse set of media clients. They will want to work as part of a team, helping senior journalists and editors across a range of stories, from conflict zones to weather events and politics. As a journalist, the ideal candidate will be self-motivated and energetic, keen to learn open-source investigative and verification techniques.


Responsibilities will include:

  • Hybrid working
  • Monitoring Storyful’s news feeds for emerging stories and undertaking advanced searches using our proprietary tools to discover original, eyewitness content
  • Verifying images, posts and videos from the social web
  • Writing clean, concise and accurate copy for publication on the Storyful Newswire and social platforms
  • Contacting uploaders and sources involved in stories
  • Working closely with newsroom clients and content creators
  • Working to deadlines and targets
  • Availability to work a flexible schedule in terms of days and hours, including weekends
  • An ability to communicate clearly within the team, and also to clients and media partners
  • Any other duties set out by editorial management team

Experience Required:

  • Proven experience in open-source investigation/social media discovery and verification is an advantage but not essential
  • Either a degree or qualification in journalism/communications, or one year of experience working as a journalist
  • A self-starting journalist who is plugged into current events around the world
  • A fluid, natural communicator who can write clean, simple copy for publication. All finalists will be administered a copy test.
  • Understanding of social media platforms such as Twitter, Facebook, Reddit, 4chan, etc.
  • Excellent computer skills, including basic knowledge of spreadsheets and publishing within content management systems, is an advantage but not essential
  • Foreign language skills are strongly favoured, but not required
  • Video-editing skills are an advantage, but not mandatory

job.title: Mailer
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

The Print Team supports the end-to-end lifecycle of Dow Jones’ print publications—including The Wall Street Journal, Barron’s, Investor’s Business Daily, and the New York Post.


Operating across ad intake, production workflows, plant operations, printing, packaging, single copy and amenity sales, Reprints and Licensing, and distribution; the team collaborates with internal cross-functional partners and external vendors, distributors, and the USPS to ensure quality, content freshness, safety, and cost efficiency from creation to final delivery.

 

About the Role

Perform daily mailroom operations in the manufacturing of Dow Jones' and contract print publications in a cost-effective manner, with the highest quality standards available using existing technology. This includes but is not limited to Preparing, Operating and Maintaining newspaper mailing and bundling equipment and all associated operations. This includes splicing and installing label lists onto labelers, pushing rolls of plastic and paper, sorting tops, setting up and operating controls for stackers, conveyors and other equipment, and general equipment cleaning and maintenance. Customer expectations must be met for reproduction quality, content freshness and productivity, while managing materials consumption cost-effectively. You will be based at the Chicopee, Massachusetts Print Plant reporting to the Operations Manager.

You Will:

  • Prepare the mailroom for the nightly operation of Dow Jones & Co. publications.
  • Discard all printed waste into bailers or compactors.
  • Perform mailroom operations to continuously improve upon the Production Quality Score, which integrates key performance measures such as reproduction quality, content freshness, productivity, and cost-effective materials consumption.
  • Maintain open communication with supervisor and other employees in order to reach the goals and objectives of the department.
  • Assist in the training of new employees.
  • Meet established performance standards, attend recommended training, and complete active assignments.
  • Understand and follow all corporate and plant policies/practices. Keep accurate, useful, and timely operational and maintenance records. Work with the production manager to set equipment maintenance priorities.

You Have:

  • The ability to stand for 7.25 hours, lift 50 lbs., kneel, bend, stoop and reach out and over head, climb stairs and ladders and push rolls of newsprint.

job.title: Manager, Social & Emerging Platforms
job.description:
Job Description:


About The Team:

The Trust is the award-winning creative studio of The Wall Street Journal and Barron's Group, creating premium branded content and storytelling for some of the world's leading brands. We combine the journalistic excellence and authority of our publications with strategic creativity, data-driven insights and innovative content experiences to help clients connect with influential audiences.


About the Role:

The Manager, Social & Emerging Platforms is a strategic and creative thinker tasked with helping to drive the cross-functional vision, growth, and execution of emerging and evolving content formats including social, TV and LLM-optimized formats for Custom Content and Brand Advertising.

Evolving beyond core social channel management and creative vision, this role bridges creative direction, platform strategy, and commercial opportunity. You, with a new social team, will establish centralized ownership over the custom and brand social ecosystem—from pricing and product strategy to paid distribution and end-to-end creative direction. Additionally, this role acts as a primary cross-platform strategist, expanding storytelling initiatives into appropriate TV formats with social extensions as well as actively contributing to traditional video programming, host/talent engagements, and next-generation media consumption platforms.

Positioned with clear cross-departmental visibility, you will re-establish early-stage involvement in pre-sale strategic development, ensuring social and emerging platform strategies are baked into overarching campaign narratives rather than added downstream. You will also oversee dedicated execution resources across paid media and creative strategy, elevating the organization’s overall expertise and driving commercial revenue growth.

This role offers an early progression path toward creative leadership across the broader media organization and visibility with new teams, including TV. 


You Will:

  • Strategic Vision & Commercial Ownership
    • Centralize Social Strategy: Serve as the primary, authoritative voice of social as a cross-MMS function across both Custom Content and Brand Advertising.
    • Product & Pricing Strategy: Partner with Product Strategy to design, price, and package scalable social products, custom content offerings, and paid distribution models that reflect competitive publisher benchmarks.
    • Early-Stage Pre-Sale Ideation: Re-establish early seat-at-the-table involvement in high-value pre-sale pitch workflows, shaping core strategic frameworks and creative directions from inception.
    • Cross-Departmental Enablement: Develop internal education, standards, and training to enable sales, planning, and editorial teams, driving revenue growth and reducing execution friction.
  • Creative Direction & Platform Expansion
    • Omnichannel Creative Direction: Lead high-level creative direction for social-first campaigns while expanding traditional Creative Director duties across broader media formats where new platforms and social and LLM optimization are critical – expected to be a greater number of campaigns. 
    • Emerging Content Platforms: Continuously evaluate and test new platforms, content formats, and media consumption habits to keep the studio at the forefront of digital culture and audience behavior.
    • Paid & Organic Alignment: Oversee paid social strategies and organic content outputs, ensuring campaign creative aligns with platform-native behaviors and delivery algorithms.
  • Team Leadership & Resource Management
    • Team Supervision: Working with your manager, direct and manage dedicated execution resources, including Full-Time Paid Social Strategists and Social Writer, delegating day-to-day tactical output to focus on higher-level strategic expansion.
    • Workflow Optimization: Establish formalized team structures and operational workflows that eliminate organizational ambiguity and streamline production between internal creative, sales, and product teams.

You Have:

  • Experience: 7+ years of progressive experience in digital strategy, social media leadership, or creative strategy within a media publisher, agency, or content studio environment.
  • Strategic & Commercial Acumen: Proven track record of developing market-ready digital/social products, establishing pricing strategy, and shaping pre-sale pitches that win commercial business.
  • Creative Scope: Strong portfolio of creative direction spanning short-form social, native video, platform-first strategy, and cross-platform extensions (e.g., experiential, events, hosting).
  • Team Management: Experience delegating execution to direct reports or specialized strategists (paid and creative) while maintaining quality control and high-level client delivery.
  • Cross-Functional Influence: Ability to navigate complex, matrixed media organizations, build consensus across product/editorial/sales teams, and establish formal operational ownership.
